Present of dilapider: to waste something precious, like money or time.
Vous imperative of poser + les: put them (down).
« D'où » + noun = hence: « d'où le nom du plat » = which is where the name of the dish comes from.
Said of bread that has gone dry and hard.
Italian cured pork belly, used like bacon.
Present of discuter; « discuter de » takes de, hence « dont ».
Present participle of saliver; « attendre en salivant » = to wait with your mouth watering.
Past participle of reculer (to move back); « il a reculé au sixième rang » = he dropped to sixth.
Spoken for winning something hard: « décrocher le titre » = to clinch the title.
Said of heat or skin that is damp: « une chaleur moite ».
« Faire la réputation de » = to be what something is famous for.
Plural of passage; « ses neuf passages » = his nine visits.
Past participle of reléguer; « relégué en fond de grille » = sent to the back of the grid.
Past participle of sacrer; « être sacré » in sport = to be crowned champion.
Past participle of éliminer; « avoir éliminé » is the past infinitive: to have eliminated.
Spoken stress word: « c'était justement l'exploit » = that was exactly the achievement.
« Pas de panique ! » = don't panic, a friendly everyday phrase.
« L'aspect qu'elle doit avoir » = the way it should look.
From étonnant (surprising): « étonnamment peu » = surprisingly little.
Imperative of résister: « résistez à l'envie de… » = resist the urge to…
« Criblée de bulles » = full of holes or dots all over; feminine, agreeing with la pâte.
Feminine plural of espacé, agreeing with « espèces ».
Present of freiner (to brake): « ça les freine » = it slows them down.
« Ranger toute la maison » = to tidy the whole house.
« En général » = usually, as a rule.
Imperative of prendre, nous form: « Prenons une étudiante… » = take a student, for example.
« Faire le ménage » = to do the cleaning.
Découper = to cut into pieces; « découpez » is the vous imperative.
Imperative of attaquer; for a task, « attaquez la première » = get stuck into the first one.
« Au premier abord » = at first sight, at first.
« Arriver à faire quelque chose » = to manage to do it: « d'arriver à s'y mettre » = to manage to get started.
« Se promettre quelque chose » = to promise yourself something.
From faire: what can be done.
Present of écraser: « une montagne qui vous écrase » = a mountain that crushes you.
Je + aime: « j'aime le travail bien fait » = I like work that is done well.
« Les métiers qui vont disparaître » = the jobs that are going to disappear (near future with aller).
Tenir à = to care about, to insist on: « je tiens à ce que le travail soit bien fait » takes the subjunctive.
Past participle of rajouter, the everyday word for adding one more: « en avait rajouté un » = had added one.
« Sans arrêt » = nonstop, all the time.
Present of adorer: stronger than aimer, « il adore le football ».
In everyday talk often shortened to « le foot ».
Past participle of recruter: « Santos l'a recruté » = Santos signed him.
Past participle of sélectionner; for a national team, « sélectionné » = called up.
Past participle of égaler: « personne ne l'a égalé » = nobody has matched it.
Masculine; feminine jolie. Goes before the noun: « un joli jardin ».
Spoken word to sum up: « Bref, meilleures. » = in short, better.
Plural yeux. « Jeter un œil » = to take a quick look.
Imparfait of comparer: a repeated action, « chaque fois qu'elle comparait » = every time she compared.
Imparfait of monter: « les roses montaient plus haut » = the roses grew higher.
Feminine past participle of prendre: « être prise au sérieux » = to be taken seriously (about a woman).
« Prendre au sérieux » = to take seriously.
Present of tuer: « les chasseurs tuent trop de baleines » = hunters kill too many whales.
Present of vouloir, ils/elles form: « quand les gens veulent vraiment » = when people really want to.
Present of chanter, ils/elles form: « les baleines chantent de nouveau ».
« À toute vitesse » = at full speed, very fast.
Subjunctive (and present) of se taire, after « avoir peur que »: « que les mers se taisent ».
« Quelque chose d'énorme »: after « quelque chose », an adjective takes « de » and stays masculine.
An everyday word for something that amazes you: « le résultat est impressionnant ».
« Faire débat » = to be controversial, to divide people.
Past participle of disparaître: « qui avait presque disparu » = which had almost disappeared.
Always plural in this sense: « les pires dégâts » = the worst damage.
Present of remercier: « ton corps te remercie » = your body thanks you.
« Être d'accord » = to agree; on its own, « d'accord ! » = OK!
Spoken for something repeated again and again: « c'était la même rengaine ».
« Se jeter sur » = to throw yourself at, to grab: « se jeter sur le café ».
Conditional of dire: « les médecins vous diraient » = doctors would tell you.
Present of aiguiser, used for a knife or, figuratively, the mind: « aiguise le cerveau ».
Plural of solide: « garde les défenses du corps solides » = keeps the body's defences strong.
« Le plus sage » = the wisest; « sage » also means well-behaved for a child.
« D' » (de) before the town's name: « une maison d'Amherst » = a house in Amherst.
« Chercher à briller » = to try to stand out, to show off.
Spoken for someone, or something, that won't give up: « le plus têtu ».
« -là » after a noun with « ces » points at it, as in speech: « ces choses-là » = those things.
« Généreux en vent et en soleil » = with plenty of wind and sun.
« Ça saute aux yeux » = it's obvious, it jumps out at you.
Question with inversion, normal in a short direct question: « à qui pouvez-vous rendre la journée plus légère ? »
Present of abîmer: « le tartre abîme les gencives » = tartar damages the gums.
Infinitive after « pouvoir »: « on peut brosser autant qu'on veut ».
Present of bouger: « rien ne bouge » = nothing moves.
Spoken present of rater: « ce qu'on rate » = what you miss.
« Un outil en acier » = a steel tool; « en » + material says what it is made of.
Past participle of démarrer: « il a mal démarré » = he got off to a bad start.
Imparfait of pleuvoir, only with « il »: « il pleuvait tellement fort ».
Past participle of repasser, agreeing with « les »: « il les a repassés » = he got back past them.
« Garder son salaire » = to keep being paid.
Imperative of parler with « en » (about it) after a hyphen: « parlez-en à la sage-femme ».
« Le moral en berne » (like a flag at half-mast) = low spirits.
Infinitive after « allait »: « n'allait leur accorder un diplôme qu'en 1948 » = would not grant them a degree until 1948.
Present of accueillir, ils/elles form: « les mains qui accueillent les nouveau-nés » = the hands that receive newborns.
Imparfait of acheter, ils/elles form, for something people did again and again.
Present of améliorer: « elle améliore l'humeur » = it improves your mood.
Imparfait of attendre, ils/elles form: « les canards qui attendaient à la gare ».
« Avoir des doutes » = to have one's doubts, not to be sure.
Past participle of enrichir, feminine plural to agree with « les conférences ».
Same form for masculine and feminine.
« Le patrimoine immatériel » = intangible heritage: know-how, songs and crafts rather than buildings.
L' (it) + present of expliquer, ils/elles form: « les chercheurs l'expliquent » = researchers explain it.
« Un luxe de riches » = a luxury for the rich.
Ne + ose (oser, to dare): « qu'on n'ose pas dire » = that you don't dare say.
Feminine of principal: « l'idée principale » = the main idea.
Infinitive: « un savoir à protéger » = knowledge to protect.
Present of recommencer (re- + commencer): « il recommence » = he does it again.
Imparfait of remettre; « remettre ça » is spoken French for to do it again.
Past participle of replanter (re- + planter): « il a replanté la racine » = he put the root back in the ground.
« Se mettre en retrait » = to step back and stay in the background.
Past participle of retravailler, feminine plural to agree with « les conférences ».
« Se répéter que… » = to keep telling yourself that…
french.translation: to repeat; to keep telling oneself

french.note: Present participle of sortir: « en sortant du travail » = as he left work.
Imparfait of stresser: « le travail le stressait » = work stressed him out.
Past participle of suggérer: « un ami lui a suggéré un truc » = a friend suggested something to him.
Vous form of voler (to steal), here as a command: « ne volez pas » = don't steal. Voler also means to fly.
Imparfait of étudier, ils/elles form, for the background of the past.
Written with a hyphen, said "dizz-weet": « moins dix-huit degrés » = minus eighteen degrees.
« En cas de panne » = if something breaks down; « une panne de courant » is a power cut.
Mostly heard in « prendre le relais » = to take over (from someone or something).
The dim light of a room with the curtains drawn: « dans la pénombre » = in the half-dark.
Said of food that keeps you going: « un petit-déjeuner nourrissant ».
De + y before a vowel: « le droit d'y goûter » = the right to taste it (goûter à quelque chose).
What a people passes on; « le patrimoine vivant » = living heritage, UNESCO's term for traditions.
Past participle of relire (re- + lire): « il a relu le verset » = he read the verse again.
Written with a hyphen; « un demi-million de personnes » takes « de » before the noun, like « un million de ».
Me + avez, the vous form: « vous m'avez rappelé » = you reminded me; a stranger is spoken to with vous.
Adjectives of nationality are lowercase in French and come after the noun: un médecin autrichien.
« À cette heure-là » = at that time (of day); -là points to a moment already mentioned.
« Avec un soin cérémonieux » = with almost ritual care, as if it were a ceremony.
« Ne pas perdre une miette » = not to miss a thing (literally not to lose a crumb).
« Se retrouver » = to gather, to end up together: « le village s'est retrouvé autour de la marmite ».
Present of battre (to beat), used for a heart: « son cœur bat très vite ».
Present plural of trembler: « ses mains tremblent ».
Everyday spoken word for a trick, a tip or any thing: « le truc de son grand-père » = his grandfather's trick.
Present of respirer (to breathe); « respire ! » is also the imperative.
Invariable: « des trucs anti-stress » = things that fight stress.
Spoken French uses « celui-là » for « this one / that one » where writing often has « celui-ci ».
Present of allonger: « quand on allonge l'expiration » = when you make the out-breath longer.
« À l'armée » = in the army, in the military.
Present of publier: « elle publie un roman ».
Present of répéter; the second é becomes è when the ending is silent: je répète, il répète.
Literally « to cash in »; in speech, « encaisser » a disappointment = to take it and carry on.
french.translation: to take (a blow), to cope with

french.note: « Se compliquer » = to get complicated: « quand les choses se compliquent » = when things get hard.
Present of prétendre: to claim, not « to pretend » (« faire semblant »).
« Se corser » = to get tougher: « quand la vie se corse » = when life gets hard (nothing to do with Corsica, la Corse).
Present of rappeler: « elle nous rappelle que… » = it reminds us that…
Present of mixer (to blend with a blender): « il mixe tout »; in a recipe « mixe » is the tu imperative: blend it.
Imparfait of saler (to add salt): « il salait et poivrait à son goût ».
Imparfait of poivrer (to add pepper), the partner of saler.
« Les soirées commençaient à fraîchir » = the evenings were getting cooler.
Imparfait of ressortir: « il ressortait sa recette » = he got his recipe out again (every autumn).
« D'une simplicité désarmante » = so simple it wins you over.
« Au final » is an everyday way to say « in the end, all things considered ».
french.translation: final; « au final » = in the end

french.note: Imparfait of aligner: « un livre qui alignait cinq mille résultats » = a book that listed five thousand results.
Imparfait of étudier with « ne » elided: « il n'étudiait rien d'autre » = he studied nothing else.
« Le ventre vide » = on an empty stomach; « la boule au ventre » = sick with nerves.
« C'était forcément vrai » = it had to be true; a spoken favourite for « necessarily ».
« Continuer sur sa lancée » = to keep going on the same run.
Amy March, the youngest of the four sisters in Little Women.
The year the second part of Little Women came out.
Present of aimer for il/elle/on: « on aime sa phrase » = people love her line.
In everyday French « discuter avec quelqu'un » means to chat with someone, not to argue.
« Ça ne va pas durer » = it isn't going to last; « durer » is used for time, weather, a feeling.
Feminine of gâté: an « enfant gâté(e) » has been given everything they want.
Feminine of marié; « jeune mariée » = newly married (also a bride).
« La météo » is the everyday word for the weather and the forecast.
Literally to ripen, like fruit; said of a person, it means to become wiser and more grown-up.
Feminine of vaniteux: too proud of yourself or your looks.
The year of the anonymous bank advertisement with the oldest known version of the line.
Present of adorer, ils form: stronger than aimer, « les gens adorent l'attribuer à Twain ».
« Attribuer une phrase à quelqu'un » = to say someone wrote or said it.
Spoken French uses « celle-là » where writing often has « celle-ci »: « celle-là ne coûte rien ».
Past participle of fournir: « ils ont fourni l'électricité » = they supplied the electricity.
Everyday word for clever: « ce qui est vraiment malin » = the really clever part.
« Ou, plus probablement » = or, more likely.
« Une publicité pour une banque » = an ad for a bank; in speech often shortened to « une pub ».
« L'électricité supplémentaire » = the extra electricity; same form in masculine and feminine.
Feminine of sérieux: « très sérieuse, elle y a déposé un caillou » = very seriously, she dropped in a stone.
« Le milieu et les pépins » = the core and the pips: what you cut out of an apple before baking it.
Present of repérer: « un rendez-vous repère les problèmes » = a check-up spots problems early.
Spinach is plural in everyday French: « dans les épinards » = in spinach.
« Une drôle d'idée » = a funny idea, a strange idea: drôle de + noun is a very spoken way to say 'odd'.
Negative imperative of attendre: « n'attendez pas « plus tard » » = don't wait for 'later'; ne becomes n' before a vowel.
« Il pique du nez » = he nods off, his head drops with sleep: an everyday idiom for the after-lunch slump.
Lancer une balle = to throw a ball; se lancer = to take the plunge.
french.translation: to throw, to launch; se lancer = to go for it

french.note: French writes decimals with a comma and says it « zéro virgule cent soixante-dix-neuf »; under 2, « seconde » stays singular: « 0,179 seconde ».
Said « cent vingt-trois », with no « et » and no hyphen after « cent »: « 123 points d'avance » = a 123-point lead.
French writes decimals with a comma and says it « treize virgule zéro soixante-dix-huit »: « à 13,078 secondes » = 13.078 seconds behind.
The year said « mille neuf cent cinquante-trois » (or « dix-neuf cent cinquante-trois »): « en 1953 » = in 1953.
Alberto Ascari, the Italian driver who was Formula 1 world champion in 1952 and 1953.
Part of « Circuit of the Americas », the English name of the race track in Austin, Texas, which French keeps as it is.
Alberto Ascari, the last Italian Formula 1 world champion, in 1953.
Present subjunctive of finir, needed after « il fallait que »: « il fallait que Russell finisse neuvième » = Russell needed to finish ninth.
Ordinal number: huit + -ième. « Russell est huitième » = Russell is eighth.
Nationality adjective, written with a small letter: « il est italien »; as a noun it takes a capital: « un Italien ».
F1 slang borrowed from English for the medium tyres: « pneus mediums puis durs » = mediums, then hards.
The French name for Mexico City, the capital of Mexico, where the next race is: « à Mexico » = in Mexico City.
Months take a small letter in French: « le 1er novembre » = on 1 November.
Past participle of plier (to fold), used in speech for something already decided: « la course était quasiment pliée » = the race was pretty much over.
Plural of « le pneu »: « pneus mediums puis durs » = medium, then hard tyres.
Past participle of repasser (re- + passer): in a race, « il l'a repassé » = he overtook him back.
« Sauf un moment » = apart from one moment; unlike « à part », it needs no « de » or « à ».
Borrowed from English: « les arrêts aux stands » = the pit stops.
The US state where Austin is; French says « au Texas » (in Texas), because the name is masculine.
English word kept in dish names: « le chicken tikka masala », « le butter chicken » (masculine); French says « poulet » everywhere else.
Mahal = palace in Urdu and Hindi, as in Taj Mahal; « le Shish Mahal » (Glasgow), « le Moti Mahal » (Delhi): masculine, like « restaurant ».
The everyday word for chicken as meat; « le poulet », and « des hauts de cuisse de poulet » = chicken thighs.
Plural of « une épice »; « des épices » = some spices, with des because you do not count them.
« Du gingembre » = some ginger, with du because you do not count it.
« Un haut de cuisse » = the top of the leg, a chicken thigh; « cuisse » alone is the whole leg.
Plural of « le haut » (the top); in a recipe « des hauts de cuisse » = chicken thighs. As an adjective, haut means high.
Short for « gramme(s) », read aloud: « 600 g » = « six cents grammes ».
Short for « millilitre(s) », read aloud: « 100 ml » = « cent millilitres ».
Read « six cents »: the -s stays because nothing follows the hundreds.
Tu imperative of faire + le: « fais-le dorer » = fry it until golden; the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen.
From paraître (to seem), with the verb before « il » as in a question; slipped into a sentence, it hedges a detail you are not sure of: « et, paraît-il, de la soupe de tomate ».
Tu imperative of griller + les: « grille-les » = grill them, les because « hauts de cuisse » is plural; -er verbs drop the -s in the tu imperative.
Subjunctive of noircir (to blacken, from noir), ils form, after « jusqu'à ce que »: « jusqu'à ce qu'ils noircissent » = until they char.
A year, read « mille neuf cent quarante-sept »; the year India was split at Partition and the two cooks came to Delhi.
A year, read « deux mille vingt-quatre »; « en 2024 » = in 2024, with en and no article.
Read « cinquante »; « 50 g de beurre » = « cinquante grammes de beurre ».
A city in the north-west of the old British India, now in Pakistan; « quitter Peshawar pour Delhi » = to leave Peshawar for Delhi.
The city that holds India's capital, New Delhi; « à Delhi » = in Delhi, with à before a city.
First part of the first name Kundan Lal, which both cooks had: Kundan Lal Gujral and his cousin Kundan Lal Jaggi.
Second part of the first name Kundan Lal, which both cooks had; « Lal » is a common part of names in North India.
Family name of Kundan Lal Gujral, a founder of the Moti Mahal; « les Gujral » = the Gujral family, with no plural -s.
Family name of Kundan Lal Jaggi, Gujral's cousin and partner; « les Jaggi » = the Jaggi family, with no plural -s.
Moti = pearl in Hindi and Urdu; « le Moti Mahal », the « Palais de la Perle », is masculine because « restaurant » is.
English word kept in the dish's name: « le butter chicken » is masculine; in French it is also called « poulet au beurre ».
Never changes its ending: « le poulet tandoori » = chicken marinated in yoghurt and spices and cooked in a tandoor.
A deep clay oven, very hot, used in India and Pakistan; « cuit au tandoor » = cooked in the tandoor, with au.
« Aller au tribunal » = to go to court; the plural is « les tribunaux », -al becoming -aux.
« La Haute Cour de Delhi » = the Delhi High Court; in everyday life « la cour » is also a courtyard or a school playground.
« Son cousin » = his or her (male) cousin; a female cousin is « une cousine ».
« Le même prénom » = the same first name; the family name is « le nom de famille ».
« La partition de l'Inde » is the 1947 split of British India into India and Pakistan, often just « la Partition »; « une partition » is also a music score.
« Le Palais de la Perle » = the Pearl Palace, the meaning of Moti Mahal; palais ends in -s even in the singular.
« Une perle » = a pearl; « le Palais de la Perle » = the Pearl Palace. Said of a person, « une perle » is a gem.
Sécher (to dry), imparfait, ils form: it happened again and again; the adjective is sec, feminine sèche.
Se dessécher (to dry out completely), imparfait, ils form; « se desséchaient » is stronger than « séchaient ».
Past participle of recycler; « on les a recyclés »: it agrees with « les » (the leftovers), placed before avoir. « Recycler les restes » = to turn leftovers into a new dish.
Past participle of repartir (re- + partir), with être: « ils sont repartis de zéro » = they started over from scratch.
Subjunctive of noircir (to blacken, from noir), il form, after « jusqu'à ce que »: « jusqu'à ce qu'il noircisse un peu » = until it's a bit black.
The French name for Beijing, the capital of China, home of Shiqian Ding's team; « à Pékin » = in Beijing.
Un atome, the tiny building block of everything; « le cœur d'un atome » = the heart of an atom.
Le + atome, shortened before the vowel: « le cœur de l'atome » = the heart of the atom.
Un laser, said « la-zèr »; « une lumière laser » = laser light, where laser works like an adjective and never takes an -s.
L' (it) + éclaire, present of éclairer (to light up): the object pronoun comes before the verb, « un laser l'éclaire » = a laser shines on it.
french.translation: lights it up, shines on it

french.note: L' (it) + éclairait, imparfait of éclairer, for the background of the story: « un laser l'éclairait » = a laser was shining on it.
french.translation: lit it up, was shining on it

french.note: From « se tromper » (to be wrong, to make a mistake), reflexive: « le laser se trompe ? » = is the laser wrong?; « se trompait » is the imparfait, for each time it happened.
Read « deux mille trois »: « en 2003 » = in 2003, « depuis 2003 » = since 2003.
Le GPS, said letter by letter « gé-pé-esse »; it means both the satellite system and the box or app in your car or phone.
Read « sept » (the p is silent): « le 7 octobre » = on 7 October, with « le » and no word for « on ».
First name of Thorsten Schumm, the physicist who leads the nuclear clock team at TU Wien, the technical university of Vienna.
Thorsten Schumm, Austrian physicist at TU Wien, whose team ran a nuclear clock on its own in 2026.
First name of Shiqian Ding, the physicist who leads the nuclear clock team at Tsinghua University in Beijing.
Shiqian Ding, Chinese physicist at Tsinghua University in Beijing; in Chinese the family name, Ding, comes first.
From « le noyau » of an atom; « une horloge nucléaire » = a clock that listens to the nucleus, nothing to do with a nuclear power station.
Literally « goes and comes », written with hyphens and never changing in the plural: « le va-et-vient d'un pendule » = the swing of a pendulum.
Le pendule is the swinging weight; careful, « la pendule » (feminine) is a clock on the wall or the mantelpiece.
From « l'atome »; « une horloge atomique » counts the jumps of electrons, the most exact clocks before nuclear ones.
Plural of « le saut » (jump), from sauter; « les sauts des électrons » = the jumps of the electrons.
Plural of « un électron », the tiny particles that move around the nucleus of an atom.
Plural of « le battement », from battre (to beat): the beats of a heart or the ticks of a clock.
A heavy metal; thorium-229 (read « thorium deux cent vingt-neuf ») is the kind whose nucleus can be nudged by a laser, the heart of the new clocks.
Un cristal, plural « des cristaux »: a clear solid whose atoms sit in neat rows, here holding the thorium.
Present of absorber, il/elle form: « le thorium absorbe une lumière laser » = the thorium takes in laser light.
From « se décaler » (to shift a little out of place), reflexive: « si le laser se décale » = if the laser slips.
Present of ramener; the e becomes è when the ending is silent: « l'horloge le ramène » = the clock pulls it back.
De + écart (gap, difference), shortened before the vowel: « une seconde d'écart » = a second off.
Le + écart, shortened before the vowel: how far a measure is from the right value; « l'écart ? » = how far off?
Read « trente »: « 30 millions d'années » = 30 million years, with « de » after millions.
Plural of « un physicien », someone who works in physics (« la physique »); a woman is « une physicienne ».
Read « dix mille »: French groups thousands with a space, not a comma: « 10 000 fois » = 10,000 times.
Le fluorure; « le fluorure de calcium » = calcium fluoride, the clear crystal that holds the thorium.
Le calcium, the same word as in English, said « cal-si-om »; « un cristal de fluorure de calcium » = a calcium fluoride crystal.
First name of Ekkehard Peik, German physicist in Braunschweig, who wrote down the idea of a nuclear clock in 2003.
Ekkehard Peik, German physicist who proposed the thorium nuclear clock with Christian Tamm in 2003.
First name of Christian Tamm, the German physicist who proposed the nuclear clock with Ekkehard Peik in 2003.
Christian Tamm, German physicist, co-author of the 2003 nuclear clock idea with Ekkehard Peik.
« Mettre noir sur blanc » = to put in writing, literally black on white: « ils avaient mis l'idée noir sur blanc » = they had written the idea down.
Une revue is a magazine or a scientific journal: « la revue Nature » = the journal Nature, where scientists publish their work.
A year, read « mille neuf cent soixante-six »: the first issue of the magazine came out in March 1966.
L' + ouest (west), shortened before the vowel; « l'Allemagne de l'Ouest » = West Germany, the country from 1949 to 1990.
German for foundation; French keeps the German name: « la Stiftung Warentest », a foundation in Berlin that tests products.
German Waren (goods) + Test: the second half of the name « Stiftung Warentest », which French does not translate.
Infinitive; « une machine à coudre » = a sewing machine: à + infinitive says what a machine is for.
Plural of « un mixeur », a kitchen machine that mixes or blends food.
Read « cent mille »: French groups thousands with a space, not a comma.

Haften, er/sie/es form: „eine Soße, die haftet“ = a sauce that clings.
The small country in Southeast Asia that eliminated trachoma as a public health problem in 2026; a hyphenated name is one word for the reader.
Das Trachom: an eye infection spread by flies and dirty hands, the world's leading infectious cause of blindness.
Plural of die Fliege; the same word is the verb „fliegen“ (to fly).
Schmutzig (dirty), from der Schmutz: after „so“ it takes no ending („so schmutzig“), before a noun it is declined („schmutzige Hände“).
Die Infektion, plural Infektionen; nouns ending in -ion are always feminine.
Plural of die Wimper: „die Wimpern drehen sich nach innen“ = the lashes turn inward.
Das Auge, plural die Augen: „das Auge kratzen“ = to scratch the eye.
Die Operation: a surgical operation; -ion nouns are feminine.
Three, said „drei“. With a dot it is a day of the month: „am 3. Juli“, „am 3. September“; the dot marks an ordinal (dritten).
Der September; „am 3. September“ = on 3 September.
Augen + Infektion: a compound noun takes the gender of its last part.
Plural of der Wasserhahn (Wasser + Hahn, literally water-cock): a tap.
Vernarben, er/sie/es form, from die Narbe (scar): „Mit jeder Infektion vernarbt das Lid stärker“ = with every infection the eyelid scars more.
Infinitive of blinzeln (to blink) used as a neuter noun: „Jedes Blinzeln tut weh“ = every blink hurts.
Plural of das Antibiotikum, from Greek; almost always used in the plural.
„Sauberes Wasser macht das möglich“ = clean water makes that possible; machen + adjective, undeclined.
Timor-Leste was the 33rd country; the dot after „33.“ makes it an ordinal (dreiunddreißigste).
Die Region: „das letzte seiner Region“ = the last in its region (genitive).
Dative plural of das Tuch (cloth), plural Tücher: „getragen von … geteilten Tüchern“ = carried by shared cloths.
A year, read "zweitausendzwei".
German writes a decimal comma where English writes a point: „1,3 Millionen“ = 1.3 million.
Der Feind, plural Feinde: „ein alter Feind“ = an old enemy.
Das Wunder, plural Wunder: „nicht auf ein Wunder warten“ = not to wait for a miracle.
Der Einwohner, the same form in the plural: „1,3 Millionen Einwohner“ = 1.3 million inhabitants.
Partizip II of beibringen (to teach someone something): „das Gesichtswaschen, jedem Kind beigebracht“ = face washing, taught to every child; the particle bei- stands before ge-.
Der Ratschlag, plural Ratschläge: „nur ein Ratschlag“ = only advice.
Ordinal number used as a noun: „das dritte“ = the third one (tool), „das vierte“ the fourth.
Weiter + tragen, written as one word at the end of a relative clause: „die Fliegen und schmutzige Hände weitertragen“ = that flies and dirty hands spread.
Der Schmerz, plural Schmerzen: „der Schmerz hört auf“ = the pain stops.
Das Lid, short for das Augenlid; plural die Lider.
Lid + Schlag (stroke): der Lidschlag, one blink of the eye; „bei jedem Lidschlag“ = with every blink.
Kratzen with the prefix zer-, which adds damage or destruction: „das Auge zerkratzen“ = to scratch the eye raw; inseparable.
Verdunkeln, from dunkel: „die Welt verdunkelt sich“ = the world grows dark; reflexive, inseparable.
Die Furcht, a more formal word than die Angst; no plural.
Gesicht + -s- + Waschen: the infinitive used as a neuter noun; the linking -s- joins the two parts.
The first name of the mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan (1887–1920).
Srinivasa Ramanujan (1887–1920), the self-taught Indian mathematician whose notebooks are still read today.
Fünf + zehn = 15; „ist fünfzehn“ = is fifteen (years old).
Mathe (short for Mathematik) + Buch: das Mathebuch.
Fünf + tausend, written as one word: 5,000.
The city in southern India now called Chennai, where Ramanujan worked as a clerk from 1912.
The year Ramanujan wrote to Hardy: 16 January 1913.
Der Professor, plural Professoren: „Ein Professor liest den Brief“; before a name no article: „Professor Hardy“.
The English university town where Hardy taught and Ramanujan spent five years.
Süd (south) + Indien, written as one word: „in Südindien“.
Partizip II of beschließen: „hat beschlossen, … zu finden“ = decided to find; inseparable.
The year Ramanujan became a clerk in Madras.
Tag + -s + über: „tagsüber Rechnungen, nachts Mathematik“ = sums by day, mathematics by night.
The day in „am 16. Januar 1913“; the dot makes it an ordinal (sechzehnten).
Der Januar; „am 16. Januar“ = on 16 January.
Schüchtern (shy) has no ending after sein or as an add-on („schüchtern und allein“), and is declined before a noun: „der schüchterne Mann“, „ein schüchterner Mann“.
G. H. Hardy, the Cambridge mathematician who read Ramanujan's letter and answered: come.
A hyphenated compound with a place name, one word for the reader: „dem Cambridge-Professor Hardy“ (dative).
„Sie müssten wahr sein“ = they must be true; the noun is die Wahrheit.
Inseparable: „Niemand konnte sie erfinden“ = nobody could invent them; „hat man im Ausland erfunden“, „wurde im Ausland erfunden“ = was invented abroad (Partizip II).
The year Ramanujan died, aged thirty-two.
Hyphenated compound; der Mathematiker is the person, die Mathematik the subject.
Präteritum plural of enthalten (to contain): „am Ende enthielten die Notizbücher Mathematik“; inseparable.
„Die nirgends im Buch stand“ = that was nowhere in the book.
Studieren, er/sie/es form: „Brian May studiert Physik“; a field of study takes no article.
First word of the name „Royal Society“, kept in English.
Die Royal Society, London's academy of sciences, founded in 1660.
Die Mathematik; stressed on the last syllable.
The year Ramanujan, aged fifteen, borrowed the maths book.
Fünfzehn + Jahr + -ig, used as a noun that declines like an adjective: „ein Fünfzehnjähriger“ = a fifteen-year-old (boy).
Das Büro, plural Büros, from French: „in einem Büro in Madras“.
Büro + Angestellter: an adjective used as a noun, so the ending changes: „ein Büroangestellter“, „der Büroangestellte“; after „wurde“ no article.
Plural of die Rechnung (from rechnen, to calculate): „tagsüber Rechnungen“ = sums by day.
Declined form of einsam (lonely, solitary): „einsame Jahre“ = lonely years.
Partizip I of frieren (to be cold): „voller Heimweh und frierend“ = homesick and cold.
Heim (home) + Weh (pain): das Heimweh; „voller Heimweh“ = full of homesickness.
Beweisen (to prove), the verb of der Beweis: „jedes davon selbst zu beweisen“ = to prove every one himself; inseparable.
Das Stipendium, plural Stipendien: money that lets a student study.
Das Mitglied, plural Mitglieder: „Mitglied der Royal Society“ = Fellow of the Royal Society.
Die Periode, also called die Regel or die Menstruation: the days when the lining of the womb leaves the body with some blood.
Schleim (mucus) + Haut (skin): here the lining of the womb, which grows every month and leaves the body as the period.
Gebär- (from gebären, to give birth) + Mutter: the organ where a baby grows; the everyday word, not a euphemism.
Der Zyklus, plural Zyklen: the menstrual cycle, „Ein Zyklus hat 28 Tage“.
Partizip II of abstoßen: „wird abgestoßen“ = is shed.
„Um Tag 14“ = around day 14, the middle of a 28-day cycle, when the egg is released.
Die Eizelle: Ei (egg) + Zelle (cell), the woman's egg; a compound takes the gender of its last part.
A year, read „neunzehnhundertachtundneunzig“.
A year, read "zweitausendsechzehn".
The first name of Arunachalam Muruganantham, the inventor of a low-cost pad machine, born in 1962 in Tamil Nadu.
Arunachalam Muruganantham, the Indian inventor who tested his own pads; „Murugananthams Frau“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
Der Lappen, the same form in the plural: an old piece of cloth; „einen Lappen verstecken“ = to hide a rag.
Die Binde, plural Binden: short for Damenbinde, a sanitary pad; the same word also means a bandage.
Plural of die Rupie, the Indian currency: „für wenige Rupien“ = for a few rupees.
Ehren (to honour): „ehrt“ present, „ehrte“ Präteritum, „geehrt“ Partizip II: „2016 hat Indien ihn geehrt“.
„Binden waren zu teuer“ = pads were too expensive; after sein the adjective takes no ending.
Tier + Blut: „gefüllt mit Tierblut“ = filled with animal blood; a compound takes the gender of its last part (das Blut).
Frauen + Gruppen, plural of die Frauengruppe: „Er hat sie Frauengruppen gegeben“ = he gave it to women's groups (dative plural).
Plural of die Firma: „Er gab sie Frauengruppen, nicht Firmen“ = to women's groups, not companies.
Präteritum of verleihen (to award, to confer): „2016 verlieh ihm Indien eine hohe Auszeichnung“; inseparable.
Partizip II of zurückkommen: „war zurückgekommen“ = had come back; the particle zurück- stands before ge-.
Motor + Roller: der Motorroller, a motor scooter; the same form in the plural.
Partizip II of freisetzen: „wird eine Eizelle freigesetzt“ = an egg is released; the particle frei- stands before ge-.
„Ein Zyklus hat 28 Tage“ = a cycle is 28 days (achtundzwanzig).
Plural of der Krampf, with umlaut: „Krämpfe“, dative „mit Krämpfen“.
Plural of das Hormon: „In der letzten Woche sinken die Hormone“ = in the last week the hormones fall.
Die Müdigkeit, from müde (tired); -keit nouns are feminine.
Die Laune: „schlechte Laune“ = a bad mood, a short temper.
Plural of die Träne: „Tränen ohne Grund“ = tears for no reason, tears from nowhere.
Der Wunsch, plural Wünsche: „der Wunsch nach Ruhe“ = the wish to rest.
Die Gereiztheit, from gereizt (irritated); -heit nouns are feminine.
Partizip II of demütigen (to humiliate), used here to open the sentence: „Gedemütigt verließ ihn seine Frau“.
Präteritum of sich weigern (to refuse), always reflexive and followed by zu + infinitive: „Er weigerte sich, sie zu verkaufen“.
Die Auszeichnung, from auszeichnen (to honour, to distinguish); -ung nouns are feminine.
A regular verb: spielt (present), spielte (Präteritum), gespielt (Partizip II). Capitalised, Spiel is the noun: "im neunten Spiel" = in the ninth game; "in sieben Spielen" = in seven games.
german.translation: to play; (das Spiel, die Spiele) game, match

german.note: Die Musik; no plural.
The German name of Plato, the Greek philosopher (c. 428–348 BC) who wrote The Republic.
Der Akkord: several notes played together.
Der Bruch: a fraction in maths; also a break.
Der Staat: the state, and the German title of Plato's Republic, „Der Staat (Politeia)“.
Around 375 BC, when The Republic was written.
„Vor Christus“ (v. Chr.) = BC, before Christ.
Die Harmonie: notes that sound well together.
Klatschen, er/sie/es form: „ein Kind, das im Takt klatscht“ = a child who claps in time.
Die Erziehung, from erziehen; -ung nouns are feminine.
The capital of England, where Brian May studied physics at Imperial College.
Die Band, an English loanword pronounced the English way: „Die Band heißt Queen“; plural die Bands.
A year, read "neunzehnhundertsiebzig".
The year Brian May finished his doctorate, thirty-seven years after starting it.
The first name of Brian May, guitarist of Queen and astrophysicist, born in London in 1947.
Die Physik: „studiert Physik“ = studies physics; no article, no plural.
Doktor + Arbeit: die Doktorarbeit, the thesis written for a doctorate.
Der Staub: „Staub im All“ = dust in space, „der Staub zwischen den Planeten“; no plural.
Die Gitarre, plural Gitarren: „spielt Gitarre“ = plays guitar, with no article.
The British rock band formed in London in 1970; its guitarist Brian May finished a doctorate in astrophysics in 2007.
Gewinnen: „Die Musik gewinnt“ = the music wins; „er hat gewonnen“ = he won (Perfekt).
Sieben + und + dreißig = 37, one word; the units come before the tens.
Physik + Student; after „war“ a role takes no article: „war Physikstudent“ = was a physics student.
Das Konzert, plural Konzerte: „ihr erstes Konzert gegeben“ = gave its first concert.
Das Verhältnis: a ratio in maths; also a relationship.
First word of the name „Imperial College“, kept in English.
Das College, kept in English: Imperial College London, the university where Brian May studied physics.
Declined form of musikalisch: „die musikalische Erziehung“ = musical training.
Präteritum of kehren (to sweep, to turn). Separable: … zurück = zurückkehren, to return; „2007 kehrte Brian May zurück“ = in 2007 Brian May returned.
„37 Jahre zu spät“ = thirty-seven years late (siebenunddreißig).
Partizip II of anfangen (to begin), with ge- between the particle and the stem: an-ge-fangen.
Die Bühne: „auf der Bühne“ = on stage.
From innen (inside): „innerlich ein wenig unfertig“ = a little unfinished inside.
Unfertig (unfinished) used as a noun after „etwas“, with a capital letter and the ending -es: „etwas Unfertiges“.
Unerledigt (not dealt with) used as a noun: „ein kleines Unerledigtes“ = a small unfinished thing; it declines like an adjective.
Der Zusammenhang, plural Zusammenhänge: „den Zusammenhang sehen“ = to see the link.
Superlative of mächtig (powerful), from die Macht: „die mächtigste Lehrerin“ = the most powerful teacher.
Das Innerste, the superlative of inner used as a noun: „in das Innerste der Seele“ = into the inward places of the soul.
Takt (time, bar) + Schlag (stroke): der Taktschlag, one beat of the music.
Das Holz, plural Hölzer: „aus dem Holz eines alten Kamins“ = from the wood of an old fireplace.
Genitive of der Kamin (fireplace): „eines alten Kamins“ = of an old fireplace.
The Italian city whose sauce Artusi wrote down: „die Soße aus Bologna“.
Der Sellerie: here the stalks, not the root.
Der Wein: „etwas Wein“ = a little wine.
Italian ribbon pasta, plural in Italian and in German: „die Tagliatelle“.
Second word of „Spaghetti bolognese“, the dish as it is known outside Italy; an Italian adjective (from Bologna), written in lower case.
Hacken (to chop) + Fleisch: minced meat.
Der Deckel: „Legen Sie den Deckel auf“ = put the lid on.
Vorbeikommen, joined at the end of its relative clause: „von jedem, der vorbeikommt“ = from whoever passes.
Plural of der Koch, with umlaut.
Das Ausland: „im Ausland“ = abroad (literally in the out-land).
Die Geduld; the adjective is geduldig.
Erlauben, er/sie/es form: „wie die Geduld es erlaubt“ = as patience allows.
Der Schuss: literally a shot; in the kitchen „ein Schuss Wein“ = a splash of wine.
Partizip I of zischen used as an adverb: „zischend verdampfen“ = to hiss away.
„Lassen Sie ihn zischend verdampfen“ = let it hiss away; from der Dampf (steam).
A year: achtzehnhunderteinundneunzig.
The first name of Pellegrino Artusi (1820–1911), the retired merchant whose cookbook holds the first written recipe for the sauce of Bologna.
Pellegrino Artusi, author of the cookbook of 1891; „Artusis Buch“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
Koch + Buch: das Kochbuch, plural Kochbücher.
Ein + und + siebzig = 71; „mit einundsiebzig“ = at seventy-one.
Der Verlag, plural Verlage: a publishing house; „Jeder Verlag sagte Nein“ = every publisher said no.
Drucken (to print): „druckt“ present, „druckte“ Präteritum, „gedruckt“ Partizip II: „Er druckt es selbst“, „hat er es selbst gedruckt“.
Partizip II of drucken used as an adjective: „das erste gedruckte Rezept“ = the first printed recipe.
„Servieren Sie die Soße mit Tagliatelle“ = serve the sauce with tagliatelle; the Sie-imperative looks like the infinitive.
Der Kaufmann, plural Kaufleute: a merchant or businessman.
Only used in the plural: „zu seinen Lebzeiten“ = in his lifetime.
Vier + zehn = 14; „vierzehn Auflagen“ = fourteen editions.
Plural of die Auflage: „vierzehn Auflagen“ = fourteen editions (print runs).
„Über das Köche bis heute streiten“, „seither streiten die Köche darüber“ = cooks have argued about it ever since; streiten über + accusative.
Ruhe (rest) + Stand (state): „ein Kaufmann im Ruhestand“ = a retired merchant.
Pellegrino Artusi's age in 1891: „Pellegrino Artusi, 71“, „Er war 71“ = he was seventy-one (einundsiebzig).
Declined form of schriftlich (in writing), from schreiben: „das erste schriftliche Rezept“ = the first written recipe.
Genitive of Italien with -s: „jeder Verlag Italiens“ = every publisher in Italy.
Schmerzen (to hurt), er/sie/es form: „was mit einundsiebzig schmerzt“ = which stings at seventy-one.
Zusammen + fallen, one word after „lassen“: „in sich zusammenfallen“ = to collapse, to sink down soft.
The verb umrühren (to stir) used as a noun: „ein Umrühren“ = a stir.
Declined form of hungrig: „die lange, hungrige Geduld“ = the long, hungry patience.
A year: German says it as „neunzehnhundertzweiundsiebzig“, and a bare year can start a sentence: „1972 stirbt …“.
Separable verb: in a subordinate clause it stays whole („sobald Symptome auftreten“), in a main clause it splits („Symptome treten auf“). Separable: … auf = auftreten, to occur.
Behandeln (to treat): „behandelt“ is the Partizip II („hat behandelt“) and „behandelten“ the Präteritum plural („die jeden Biss behandelten“).
Präteritum of bescheinigen (to certify); the formal word for a written confirmation, from Bescheinigung = certificate.
Der Biss (bite); plural Bisse, genitive Bisses. Do not confuse it with „biss“ as a verb form (he bit).
The country in South America; German country names usually take no article.
Partizip II of eliminieren (to eliminate); verbs in -ieren form the participle without ge-: „hat eliminiert“.
Die Eliminierung, from eliminieren; nouns in -ung are feminine.
Fordern, er/sie/es form. „Es fordert Opfer“ = it claims victims (lives).
Impfen (to vaccinate): „impft“ is the present (Chile impft seine Hunde), „geimpft“ the Partizip II (hat geimpft).
The Swiss city where the World Health Organization has its seat; German name of Geneva.
Das Glück: „auf Glück warten“ = to wait for luck; an abstract noun used without an article.
Der Helfer; the plural has the same form, so only the article or the verb shows it: „Helfer gehen“.
Impfen (to vaccinate) + Team; the plural of das Impfteam.
Die Impfung; nouns in -ung are feminine, plural Impfungen.
Die Katze; plural Katzen: „Hunde und Katzen“ = dogs and cats.
Die Lepra, the old disease also called Hansen's disease; no plural.
From Mensch (person); „menschlich“ takes endings: „der menschliche Fall“, „Chiles letzter menschlicher Fall“ = Chile's last human case.
Das Merkwürdige is an adjective used as a noun, written with a capital: the strange thing.
Das Opfer; plural has the same form: „zehntausende Opfer“.
Die Routine: ordinary repeated work.
The capital of Chile.
From sofort (immediately); „die sofortige Behandlung“ = the immediate treatment.
Das Symptom; plural Symptome: „sobald Symptome auftreten“ = as soon as symptoms appear.
Die Tollwut, the disease passed on by a bite; no plural.
From der Tod (death): „tödlich enden“ = to end fatally.
The prefix un- turns sichtbar (visible) into its opposite.
Inseparable verb; for time it takes sein: „Fünfzig Jahre vergehen“ = fifty years go by.
The US capital, where the WHO has a regional office (the Pan American Health Organization).
Welt (world) + weit: across the whole world.
Zehn + tausend as a plural noun: „zehntausende Menschen“.
Das Zertifikat; the official paper from the WHO.
Present participle of ziehen used before a noun: „von Tür zu Tür ziehende Impfteams“ = teams going door to door.
Die Überwachung, from überwachen; nouns in -ung are feminine.
In „Formel 1“ the numeral is said „eins“: „Formel eins“.
German writes a decimal comma where English writes a point: „2,3 Sekunden“ (zwei Komma drei) = 2.3 seconds.
The year of the last Formula 1 race at Sepang before 2026 (zweitausendsiebzehn); German uses the bare year, without „in“: „Er gewinnt hier auch 2017.“
The day in „der 4. Oktober“; the dot after the numeral makes it an ordinal (der vierte, am vierten).
„84 Punkte“ = eighty-four points; German says the units before the tens: vierundachtzig.
90; the tens end in -zig (neun + zig): „neunzig Minuten“ = ninety minutes, an hour and a half.
Max Verstappen, a Dutch Formula 1 driver for the Red Bull team.
The first name of Kimi Antonelli, who drives for Mercedes in Formula 1.
Kimi Antonelli, an Italian Formula 1 driver for the Mercedes team; „Antonellis Vorsprung“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
George Russell, a British Formula 1 driver for the Mercedes team.
The first name of Lewis Hamilton, who drives for Ferrari in Formula 1.
Lewis Hamilton, a British Formula 1 driver for the Ferrari team.
First word of „Red Bull“, the name of Max Verstappen's Formula 1 team, kept in English.
Second word of „Red Bull“, Max Verstappen's Formula 1 team; „Red Bulls ersten Sieg“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
The Formula 1 team of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell; one car is „der Mercedes“, and the plural has the same form: „zwei Mercedes“.
The Formula 1 team Lewis Hamilton drives for; a team name takes no article: „für Ferrari“.
The place in Malaysia with the racing track where Formula 1 raced on 4 October 2026; place names take no article: „in Sepang“.
The country where Sepang lies; most country names are neuter and take no article: „in Malaysia“, „nach Malaysia“.
The German spelling of Singapore, a city and country in South-East Asia with a Formula 1 race on its streets.
The country that gives the race its name: the Grand Prix von Bahrain was moved to Malaysia in 2026.
Die Formel; „die Formel 1“ (said „Formel eins“) is the car-racing series, always with the feminine article.
First word of „der Grand Prix“, French for „Großer Preis“: the name of a Formula 1 race, as in „der Grand Prix von Bahrain“.
Second word of „der Grand Prix“ (a Formula 1 race); the x is silent, as in French, and the plural has the same form.
Der Oktober; months are masculine: „am 4. Oktober“ = on 4 October.
Das Feld: in a race, all the cars together; a safety car brings the field close together again.
Formel 1 + Rennen, joined by hyphens into one neuter noun: „das Formel-1-Rennen“.
Die Meisterschaft: the contest over the whole season, decided on points; nouns in -schaft are feminine.
Der Fahrer (driver) has the same form in the plural, so „die Mercedes-Fahrer“ = the Mercedes drivers; the hyphen joins the team name to the noun.
Plural of die Position: a driver's place in the race; „viele Positionen verlieren“ = to lose many places.
Der Rang: the place in a race or a table; „auf Rang drei“ = in third place, with a plain number and no article.
Das Rennen, from the verb rennen (to run, to race); the plural has the same form: „sieben Rennen“ = seven races.
Plural of die Runde, one lap of the track: „wenige Runden vor Schluss“ = a few laps from the end.
Das Safety-Car, an English loan written with a hyphen: the car that drives ahead of the racing cars and slows the race down for a while.
Der Sieg, from siegen (to win): „sein erster Sieg“ = his first win.
Stark (strong) + Regen (rain): the compound for very heavy rain, used here without an article.
Der Start: the beginning of a race; „beim Start“ = at the start.
Start + Platz: the place a car starts from; „auf Startplatz eins“ = first on the grid.
Die Strecke: here the racing track; „auf nasser Strecke“ = on a wet track.
Der Vorsprung: how far ahead someone is; „mit 2,3 Sekunden Vorsprung“ = 2.3 seconds ahead.
Partizip II of sich verspäten, used like an adverb: „begann neunzig Minuten verspätet“ = began ninety minutes late.
Wohin names a direction (where to), wo a place (where): „Sepang, wohin der Grand Prix verlegt worden war“.
Regnen (to rain) always has the subject „es“: „es regnet“ (present), „es regnete“ (Präteritum), „es hat geregnet“ (Perfekt).
Starten (to start): „startet“ is the present, „startete“ the Präteritum, „ist gestartet“ the Perfekt, with sein because it is a movement.
Überholen is not separable, so its Partizip II has no ge-: „hat überholt“; „überholte“ and „überholten“ are the Präteritum.
Partizip II of verlegen (to move something to another place or date): „nach Malaysia verlegt“ = moved to Malaysia.
Partizip II of zusammenführen; the ge- goes between the particle and the verb. Separable: … zusammen = zusammenführen, to bring together.
Präteritum of vorfahren, written as one word at the end of a subordinate clause: „während er auf Rang drei vorfuhr“. Separable: … vor = vorfahren, to move up.
The year Ole began to make wooden toys (neunzehnhundertzweiunddreißig); German uses the bare year, without „in“: „1932 war Ole …“.
The year Ole's workshop burned down for the first time (neunzehnhundertvierundzwanzig).
The year Ole's workshop burned down for the second time (neunzehnhundertzweiundvierzig).
The year of the wooden duck: „ab 1935“ = from 1935 on.
The year Ole named his company LEGO (neunzehnhundertvierunddreißig).
A year, read "neunzehnhundertachtundfünfzig".
Elf; with a full stop it is an ordinal in a date: „am 11. März“ is read „am elften März“ = on 11 March.
Ole Kirk Christiansen, the Danish carpenter of this story; „Oles Werkstatt“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
The middle name of Ole Kirk Christiansen.
The family name of Ole Kirk Christiansen, the carpenter who began to make wooden toys in 1932.
Ole's son, who sent off the ducks with two coats of varnish instead of three.
The village in Denmark where Ole Kirk Christiansen had his workshop; place names take no article: „in Billund“.
The country; most country names are neuter and take no article: „in Dänemark“.
The name Ole gave his company in 1934, from the Danish for „spiel gut“ (play well); it is written in capitals and takes no article.
Der Zimmermann builds the wooden parts of houses; the plural is Zimmerleute. After sein a profession takes no article: „Ole ist Zimmermann“.
Das Spielzeug: one toy or toys in general, usually without a plural: „Spielzeug aus Holz“ = toys made of wood.
Holz (wood) + Spielzeug (toys); the last part gives the gender: das Holzspielzeug.
Das Jo-Jo, plural Jo-Jos: the toy that runs up and down a string; German writes it with J and a hyphen.
Die Ente, plural Enten: „jede Ente“ = every duck.
Die Firma, plural Firmen: „seine Firma“ = his company.
Plural noun with no singular in everyday use: „arme Eltern“ = poor parents.
Der Bahnhof, plural Bahnhöfe: „zum Bahnhof“ = to the station, „am Bahnhof“ = at the station, „vom Bahnhof“ = from the station.
Der Lack (varnish) + die Schicht (layer): die Lackschicht, plural Lackschichten; „zwei Lackschichten“ = two coats of varnish.
Die Kiste, plural Kisten: a sturdy box for packing goods.
Der Ausdruck, plural Ausdrücke: „der dänische Ausdruck für …“ = the Danish expression for …
Die Lieferung, from liefern (to deliver): „eine Lieferung Enten“ = a shipment of ducks, with no „von“.
Das Motto, plural Mottos: „wurde zum Motto“ = became the motto.
Bauen (to build) + Stein (stone): der Baustein, the small brick a child builds with.
Der Kunststoff, the usual German word for plastic: „aus Kunststoff“ = made of plastic.
Der März; months are masculine: „am 11. März“ = on 11 March.
Die Kleinigkeit, from klein (small); nouns in -keit are feminine: „keine Kleinigkeit“ = no small thing.
From Dänemark; dänisch takes the ending -en after im, dem or einem: „im dänischen Dorf“ = in the Danish village.
Partizip II of ziehen (to pull) used before a noun with an adjective ending: „eine an einer Schnur gezogene Ente“ = a duck pulled on a string.
Bestellen (to order): „bestellt“ is the present (niemand bestellt) and also the Partizip II (hat bestellt), without ge- because of the prefix be-; „bestellte“ is the Präteritum.
Lackieren, from der Lack (varnish): „lackiert“ is the present and also the Partizip II (verbs in -ieren take no ge-), „lackierte“ the Präteritum.
Brennen (to burn): „brennt“ is the present, „brannte“ the Präteritum. Separable: … ab = abbrennen, to burn down; „Die Werkstatt brennt ab“ = the workshop burns down.
Partizip II of abbrennen (to burn down); it takes sein: „ist abgebrannt“ = has burned down, „war abgebrannt“ = had burned down.
Partizip II of aufbauen (to build up); with wieder it means to rebuild: „hat sie wieder aufgebaut“ = rebuilt it.
Partizip II of abschicken (to send off); ge- stands between the particle and the stem: ab-ge-schickt.
Partizip II of zurückschicken (to send back): „hat ihn zurückgeschickt“ = sent him back.
Partizip II of nennen (to name, call); the vowel changes e → a: „hat seine Firma LEGO genannt“ = named his company LEGO.
Sparen: „Geld sparen“ = to save money; „gespart“ is the Partizip II: „hatte Geld gespart“ = had saved money.
Präteritum of sich verlegen auf + accusative, to turn to a new activity: „er verlegte sich auf Holzspielzeug“ = he turned to wooden toys.
Partizip II of patentieren; verbs in -ieren form it without ge-: „wurde patentiert“ = was patented.
The year Lucy Wills came to Bombay (neunzehnhundertachtundzwanzig); A1 tells the story in the present: „Es ist 1928“.
The city in India where the story takes place, under the name it had in 1928; city names take no article: „in Bombay“.
The first name of Lucy Wills, the doctor from England in this story.
The family name of Lucy Wills; B1 and B2 call her by it alone.
Schwanger sein = to be pregnant; „schwangere Frauen“ = pregnant women. With a capital letter it is a noun: „bei Schwangeren“ = in pregnant women.
With little colour in the face: „blass und sehr müde“ = pale and very tired.
Plural of die Fabrik (factory): „in Fabriken arbeiten“ = to work in factories.
Die Hefe (yeast) + der Aufstrich (something you spread on bread): der Hefeaufstrich.
Das Vitamin, plural die Vitamine; the stress is on the last syllable.
Die Folsäure: the vitamin of this story; die Säure = acid. It takes no article after „nehmen“: „Nehmen Sie Folsäure“.
Textil- + die Fabriken: factories where cloth is made; singular die Textilfabrik.
Plural of die Ratte (rat).
Forms of billig (cheap): „aus einem billigen Glas“; „billiger“ is also the comparative: cheaper.
The year Lucy Wills wrote about what she had found (neunzehnhunderteinunddreißig); a bare year can open the sentence: „1931 hat sie …“.
Vierhundert: „400 Mikrogramm“ is read „vierhundert Mikrogramm“.
Das Mikrogramm, one millionth of a gram; after a number the unit stays in the singular: „400 Mikrogramm“.
Schwanger (pregnant) + -schaft: die Schwangerschaft; „vor der Schwangerschaft“ = before pregnancy.
Das Risiko, plural die Risiken; „das Risiko für …“ = the risk of …, „das Risiko senken“ = to lower the risk.
Der Wirbel (vertebra) + die Säule (column): die Wirbelsäule, the backbone.
Die Anämie: the medical word; everyday German also says „Blutarmut“.
Plural of die Textilarbeiterin: Textil- + Arbeiterin; the ending -innen marks women.
Der Verdacht; „etwas im Verdacht haben“ = to suspect something: „Wills hatte das Essen im Verdacht“.
Präteritum of füttern (to feed an animal); „mit … füttern“ = to feed on …
Adjective of Anämie: „wurden anämisch“ = became anaemic.
Krank (ill) + die Station: the part of a hospital where patients stay; „auf ihrer Krankenstation“ = on her ward.
Der Stoff: a substance or material („der unbekannte Stoff“); the same word also means cloth.
Der Wills-Faktor: the name of the unknown substance until 1941; a personal name and a noun are joined with a hyphen.
The year the substance was found in spinach and named folic acid (neunzehnhunderteinundvierzig).
Der Spinat + die Blätter (leaves); the dative plural adds -n: „in Spinatblättern“.
Ordinal of zwölf: „bis zur zwölften Woche“ = until the twelfth week.
Plural of die Fehlbildung: fehl- (wrong) + Bildung (formation), a part of the body that has not formed as it should.
Form of schwer (heavy): „die schweren Möbel“ = the heavy furniture; with an illness it means severe: „eine schwere Anämie“.
Nachgehen + dative (to look into something); in the infinitive with zu, the zu stands between particle and stem: nach-zu-gehen.
Die Ernährung, from sich ernähren (to feed oneself): everything a person eats.
Präteritum of feststellen (to find, to establish); in a subordinate clause the verb stays in one piece: „wie sie feststellte“ = as she found.
From der Mangel (lack): „mangelhaft“ means that something needed is missing.
Die Kost: what a person or an animal is given to eat; more formal than Essen.
Der Spinat, a green leaf vegetable; „aus Spinat“ = from spinach.
Partizip II of isolieren; verbs in -ieren form it without ge-: „wurde isoliert“ = was isolated.
Form of lateinisch, the adjective of Latein: „nach dem lateinischen Wort für Blatt“ = after the Latin word for leaf.
From entdecken (to discover) + -ung: die Entdeckung.
Form of gängig: what is commonly said or done; „ein gängiger Rat“ = a routine piece of advice.
Die Empfängnis: the moment a pregnancy begins; „vor der Empfängnis“ = before conception.
Plural of der Neuralrohrdefekt: das Neuralrohr (neural tube) + der Defekt (defect).
First word of the Latin medical name „Spina bifida“, a neural tube defect; German uses the Latin name unchanged: die Spina bifida.
Second word of the Latin medical name „Spina bifida“; it is written with a small letter and never stands alone.
Neural- + das Rohr (tube): das Neuralrohr; „schließt sich“ = closes.
Die Dosis, plural die Dosen: the amount of a medicine or vitamin taken at one time; „eine höhere Dosis“ = a higher dose.
The year of Ashoka's war: „etwa 261 vor Christus“ = in about 261 BC (zweihunderteinundsechzig).
The king in India (B2: emperor) of this story, about 261 BC; a person's name takes no article.
Der König, plural die Könige; „Ashoka ist ein König“ = Ashoka is a king.
Der Brunnen: a hole dug in the ground for water, or a fountain in a square; the plural has the same form, die Brunnen.
Die Medizin: what helps sick people and animals; here without an article: „Es gibt Medizin“ = there is medicine.
Der Hass, the opposite of die Liebe; it has no plural and often stands without an article: „Hass endet durch Liebe“.
Die Liebe, from lieben (to love): „durch Liebe“ = by love, through love.
Ost- (east) + die Küste (coast): „an der Ostküste“ = on the east coast.
100 000, written as one word and without „ein“: „hunderttausend Menschen“ = a hundred thousand people.
Der Sieger, from siegen (to win): „wie ein Sieger“ = like a winner.
Partizip II of sich fühlen (to feel): „Er hat sich nicht wie ein Sieger gefühlt“ = he did not feel like a winner.
Leidtun is separable: at the end of a dass-clause it is one word, „dass es ihm leidtut“ = that he is sorry; in a main clause it splits: „Es tut ihm leid“.
Das Volk: all the people of a land or of a king; „für sein Volk“ = for his people.
Partizip II of graben (to dig): „hat Brunnen gegraben“ = dug wells. Before a noun it takes an adjective ending: „von gegrabenen Brunnen“ = of wells that were dug.
Meißeln: to cut into stone with a chisel (der Meißel). „Gemeißelt“ is the Partizip II; before a noun it takes an ending: „in Stein gemeißelten Bericht“ = account carved in stone.
german.translation: to carve (in stone), to chisel; carved

german.note: Dürfen (modal verb), ich/er/sie/es form: „dass man nie wütend sein darf“ = that one may never be angry.
Präteritum of erobern (to conquer, to take a land by war): „Ashoka eroberte Kalinga“.
The place on the east coast that Ashoka conquered in about 261 BC; such names mostly take no article.
Die Inschrift: words cut into stone; in- + die Schrift (writing).
Partizip II of wegbringen (weg = away + bringen); the verb is separable, so -ge- stands in the middle: „wurden weggebracht“ = were taken away.
Berichten, er/sie/es form: „Dieselbe Inschrift berichtet, dass …“ = the same inscription reports that …
Die Reue: the feeling of being deeply sorry for what one has done; „Reue empfinden“ = to feel remorse.
Die Lehre, from lehren (to teach): what a teacher teaches; „die Lehre des Buddha“ = the Buddha's teaching.
The teacher whose teaching Ashoka turned to; German says „der Buddha“, and the genitive here has no ending: „die Lehre des Buddha“.
Das Imperium: a very large land under one ruler; „überall in seinem Imperium“ = across his empire.
Plural of die Säule: a tall, round post of stone; „in Felsen und Säulen“ = into rocks and pillars.
Der Schatten (shade) + die Bäume (trees): trees planted to give shade; -n is the dative plural after „von“.
Plural of die Religion: „Frieden zwischen den Religionen“ = peace between religions.
Die Zeile: one line of a text or a poem; „eine Zeile, die zu ihm passt“ = a line that fits him.
Fünf: „Vers 5“ is read „Vers fünf“, the fifth verse of the Dhammapada.
Verbieten (to forbid), er/sie/es form; ver- is not separable: „Der Vers verbietet die Wut nicht“ = the verse does not forbid anger.
Die Wut: what a person feels who is wütend (angry); it has no plural.
Der Kaiser: a ruler above kings; „der indische Kaiser Ashoka“ = the Indian emperor Ashoka.
Stands after its noun and takes the dative: „seinem eigenen Bericht zufolge“ = according to his own account.
150 000: hundert + fünfzig + tausend, written as one word.
Partizip II of deportieren (to take people away from their land by force); verbs in -ieren form it without ge-: „wurden deportiert“ = were deported.
Überliefern, er/sie/es form: to pass something on to later times; über- is not separable here: „Die Inschrift überliefert seine Reue“.
Partizip II of siegen (to win, to be the victor): „Nachdem er gesiegt hatte“ = after he had won.
Präteritum of entsagen (to renounce, to give up for good); it takes the dative: „entsagte der Eroberung“ = renounced conquest.
Die Eroberung, from erobern (to conquer) + -ung: taking a land by war.
Das Gebot, plural die Gebote: a rule of a religion; „deren erstes Gebot“ = whose first precept.
Infinitive; with „zu“ it names the content of the precept: „nicht zu töten“ = not to kill.
Plural of das Edikt: an order that a ruler makes public; „seine Edikte“ = his edicts.
Form of medizinisch, the adjective of die Medizin: „von medizinischer Versorgung“ = of medical care (dative feminine ending -er).
Die Versorgung, from versorgen (to provide for, to care for) + -ung: „medizinische Versorgung“ = medical care.
Die Eintracht: when people or groups live together in agreement, without quarrel.
Plural of die Glaubensrichtung: der Glaube (faith) + -s- + die Richtung (direction): a religion or a branch of one.
Der Zorn: strong anger, a more literary word than die Wut; „verbietet keinen Zorn“ = forbids no anger.
Nähren: to give food to; „sich von etwas nähren“ = to feed on something. „Genährter“ is the Partizip II before a noun: „mit Hass genährter Hass“ = hatred fed with hatred.
The year the sisters' story begins, said „achtzehnhundertvierundneunzig“: „ab 1894“ = from 1894 on.
A year, said „neunzehnhundertsechs“: „von 1894 bis 1906“ = from 1894 to 1906.
Said „hundert“ or „einhundert“: „100 Gramm Butter“ = 100 grams of butter.
Stéphanie Tatin, the sister who cooked in the hotel; a first name takes no article.
Caroline Tatin, Stéphanie's sister; the two ran the hotel together.
The family name of the sisters Stéphanie and Caroline; today the tart carries it.
The town in France where the sisters had their hotel; town names take no article: „in Lamotte-Beuvron“.
A region of France; in German it keeps its article: „in der Sologne“.
Das Hotel, plural Hotels: „ein kleines Hotel“ = a small hotel.
Die Tarte, a word taken from French; the plural is Tartes: „solche Tartes“ = such tarts.
Apfel + Tarte; the last word gives the gender: die Apfeltarte.
Die Vorsicht (caution); alone it is a warning: „Vorsicht, heiß!“ = careful, hot!
Die Legende: a story people tell without proof. „Der Legende nach“ = according to legend; in this phrase „nach“ follows its noun.
Das Gramm stays singular after a number and needs no „of“: „100 Gramm Butter“ = 100 grams of butter.
Das Kilo, short for Kilogramm; it stays singular after a number and needs no „of“: „ein Kilo Äpfel“ = a kilo of apples.
Teig + Platte: dough rolled out flat; „eine runde Teigplatte“ = a round of pastry.
Takes the dative: „gegenüber dem Bahnhof“; in speech often „gegenüber vom Bahnhof“ = opposite the station.
The opposite of unten: „oben der Teig“ = the pastry on top.
Ofen + fest: it can go into the oven; -en is the dative ending after „in einer“: „in einer ofenfesten Pfanne“.
Partizip II of halbieren (to halve) used like an adjective: „halbierte Äpfel“ = halved apples; after the noun it takes no ending.
Partizip II of backen (to bake): „hat … gebacken“ = baked, „wurde … gebacken“ = was baked.
„Bei“ + dative says with whom: „bei Jägern beliebt“ = popular with hunters.
Kopf + über: with the top at the bottom; „kopfüber gebacken“ = baked upside down.
Präteritum of führen (to lead): with a hotel or a shop it means to run it; „führten ein Hotel“ = ran a hotel.
Partizip II of schälen (to peel); after the noun and between commas it takes no ending: „Äpfel, geschält und halbiert“.
Rund (round) with the ending -e after „eine“ + feminine noun: „eine runde Teigplatte“ = a round sheet of pastry.
Bedecken + accusative, with „mit“ for the cover: „die Pfanne mit einem Teller bedecken“ = to cover the pan with a plate. The prefix be- never separates.
Oben + auf in one word: on top of the rest; „Sie legte ihn obenauf“ = she laid it on top.
Partizip II of umdrehen (to turn over) used as an adjective: „umgedrehte Tartes“ = upside-down tarts.
Breiten + über: to lay something flat over something else; „eine Teigplatte über die Früchte breiten“.
With „zu“ + infinitive: „Sie scheinen es nie aufgeschrieben zu haben“ = they seem never to have written it down. Scheinen can also mean to shine.
A year (zweitausendzehn); German says „im Jahr 2010“ or just „2010“, never „in 2010“.
Dreitausendzweihundert; German writes no comma in a number: a four-digit number stands without a mark, longer ones take a point or a space (10.000).
Fünftausendsiebenhundert; German writes no comma in a number: a four-digit number stands without a mark, longer ones take a point or a space (10.000).
Dreiundsiebzig: German says the units before the tens, „three-and-seventy“; „73 Prozent“ = 73 per cent.
Eight, said „acht“: „8 km“ = eight kilometres. With a dot it is an ordinal, a day of the month: „am 8. Oktober“, read „am achten Oktober“.
Acht + -zig: „in rund achtzig Ländern“ = in some eighty countries.
The nature organisation that published the report; the abbreviation is said letter by letter and is masculine: der WWF.
The English article, here in the report's English title „The Science of Hope“; German would say der, die or das.
English word in the title „The Science of Hope“; German uses the genitive instead: „die Wissenschaft der Hoffnung“.
English word in the report's title „The Science of Hope“, kept in English; the German word is die Wissenschaft.
English word in the report's title „The Science of Hope“, kept in English; the German word is die Hoffnung.
First word of the English name „Living Planet Report“, the WWF's report on the world's wild animals; the name is kept in English.
Der Planet; here part of the English name „Living Planet Report“, which German keeps as it is.
Der Report; here part of the English name „Living Planet Report“. The everyday German word is der Bericht.
The English name of a category on the international list of animals in danger, kept in English; its German name is „stark gefährdet“.
The English category name + die Liste, joined with a hyphen: the list of species classed as Endangered (German: stark gefährdet).
The English name of the category for species that are not in danger, kept in English; its German name is „nicht gefährdet“.
Der Tiger; the plural has the same form: die Tiger.
Meer (sea) + Schildkröte (turtle), joined with -es-. „Die Grüne Meeresschildkröte“ is the name of one kind of turtle, so Grüne takes a capital.
Plural of der Strand (beach); the a becomes ä.
Der Durchschnitt; „im Durchschnitt“ = on average.
Tier + Population: all the animals of one kind that live in one area.
Wild (wild animals) + Hüter (keeper): a person whose job is to guard wild animals; the plural has the same form.
Partizip II of bezahlen (to pay); verbs with be- take no ge-: „haben … bezahlt“ = have paid.
Partizip II of stoppen (to stop someone or something): „haben … gestoppt“ = have stopped.
Die Lektion: what one learns from an experience; also a unit in a course book.
Die Schlagzeile: Schlag (blow) + Zeile (line), the big line at the top of a piece of news.
Der Bestand, plural Bestände: how many animals of one kind there are; „der Bestand wilder Tiger“ = the wild tiger population. Not to be confused with „bestand“, the Präteritum of bestehen.
Partizip II of steigen (to rise), with sein: „ist von … auf … gestiegen“ = has risen from … to …
Präteritum of schulen (to train, to teach the skills for a job), from die Schule.
Präteritum of bekämpfen (to fight something); it takes a direct object, where kämpfen needs „gegen“: „bekämpften den illegalen Handel“.
Illegal with the accusative masculine ending -en: „den illegalen Handel“ = the illegal trade.
Der Handel (no plural): buying and selling; the verb is handeln.
The adjective from der Atlantik; it takes a capital here because it belongs to the name of the fish: der Atlantische Blauflossenthunfisch.
Blau + Flossen + Thunfisch (blue + fins + tuna), built exactly like the English name: der Atlantische Blauflossenthunfisch = the Atlantic bluefin tuna.
Plural of die Fangquote: Fang (catch) + Quote (quota), the amount of fish that may be caught.
Partizip II of senken (to lower something); do not confuse it with sinken (to sink, to go down by itself).
Staying about the same; the stress is on the second syllable.
Dark, also of news or a mood: „eine düstere Schlagzeile“ = a grim headline.
Here in the fixed phrase „wie eh und je“ = as ever, as always; on its own, colloquial „eh“ means „anyway“.
Partizip II of erfassen (to record, to register) used as an adjective with the ending -en: „die von ihm erfassten Bestände“ = the populations it tracks.
Plural of der Wildtierbestand: Wildtier (wild animal) + Bestand (population, stock).
From der Durchschnitt (average) + -lich: „um durchschnittlich 73 Prozent“ = by an average of 73 per cent.
Partizip II of schrumpfen (to shrink), with sein: „sind … geschrumpft“ = have shrunk.
Unter + Titel: „trägt den Untertitel“ = bears the subtitle, is subtitled.
Präteritum of betragen (to amount to), used with figures: „betrug 2025 etwa 5700“ = stood at about 5,700 in 2025.
Präteritum of vergrößern (to make bigger), built on größer, the comparative of groß.
Plural of das Schutzgebiet: Schutz (protection) + Gebiet (area), land where nature is protected.
Präteritum of verfolgen (to pursue, to go after someone): „verfolgten Schmuggler“ = pursued traffickers.
Der Schmuggler, same form in the plural: someone who takes goods across a border against the law.
Plural of die Grenze (border); „über Grenzen hinweg“ = across borders.
Plural of der Niststrand: nisten (to nest) + Strand (beach), a beach where turtles lay their eggs.
Partizip II of bewachen (to guard); verbs with be- take no ge-: „bewacht wurden“ = were guarded.
Präteritum of wechseln (to change, to switch): „wechselte von … zu …“ = moved from … to …
Partizip II of gefährden (to put in danger), from die Gefahr. On the list of animals in danger, „stark gefährdet“ is the German name of Endangered and „nicht gefährdet“ of Least Concern.
Partizip II of einstufen (to put in a category), from die Stufe (step, level); ge- stands after the particle ein-: „als Endangered eingestuft“ = listed as Endangered.
Partizip II of kürzen (to shorten, to cut), from kurz: „die Fangquoten wurden gekürzt“ = the catch limits were cut.
Present tense of warnen (to warn): „Der Bericht warnt, dass …“ = the report warns that …
Plural of der Zuwachs (increase), from wachsen (to grow): what has been added.
A formal word for „if“ that sends the verb to the end; „sofern … nicht“ = unless.
Plural of die Ursache: the reason why something happens.
Plural of der Verlust (loss), from verlieren (to lose): here the wild animals that have been lost.
Partizip II of angehen (to tackle a problem); ge- stands after the particle an-: „angegangen werden“ = to be addressed.
„24 Sekunden“ = twenty-four seconds; German says the units before the tens: vierundzwanzig.
The day in „am 25. Oktober“; the dot after the numeral makes it an ordinal, read „am fünfundzwanzigsten Oktober“.
„In jeder einzelnen der 62 Runden“ = in every single one of the 62 laps; read zweiundsechzig, the units before the tens.
„102 Punkte“ = a hundred and two points; read (ein)hundertzwei.
With a dot it is an ordinal: „sein 250. Grand Prix“ is read „sein zweihundertfünfzigster Grand Prix“ = his 250th Grand Prix.
Charles Leclerc, the Ferrari driver who finished second in Singapore on 11 October 2026.
The first name of Lando Norris, who drives for McLaren in Formula 1.
Lando Norris, the McLaren driver who finished fourth in Singapore on 11 October 2026.
The first name of Oscar Piastri, who drives for McLaren in Formula 1.
Oscar Piastri, the McLaren driver who finished fifth in Singapore on 11 October 2026.
The Formula 1 team of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri; one car is „der McLaren“, and the plural has the same form: „die beiden McLaren“ = the two McLarens.
The city in the United States where Formula 1 races on 25 October 2026; city names take no article: „in Austin“.
Die USA is a plural name, so it keeps its article: „in den USA“ = in the United States (dative plural).
Ordinal of fünf used as a noun for a place in a race, with a capital letter and no article: „wurden Vierter und Fünfter“ = came fourth and fifth.
Ordinal of neun used as a noun for a place in a race, with a capital letter and no article: „wird Neunter“ = comes ninth.
Leuchten (to shine, to give light): „Die Lichter leuchten“ = the lights are on; the Perfekt is „haben geleuchtet“.
german.translation: to shine, to be lit; shone

german.note: Motoren (engines) + Strafe (penalty): a penalty for the car's engine; here it sends a driver to the back at the start.
Hinter + einander: „zweimal hintereinander“ = twice in a row.
german.translation: in a row, one after another

german.note: Infinitive of gewinnen; after a modal verb it stands at the end of the clause: „kann den Titel gewinnen“ = can win the title.
Das Flutlicht: the strong lamps that light a stadium or a track at night; „unter Flutlicht“ = under floodlights, with no article.
Schwül: hot and damp at the same time; here with the dative ending -en: „in einer heißen, schwülen Nacht“ = on a hot and humid night.
Präteritum of verlieren (to lose): „verlor Positionen“ = lost places.
Die Schwüle: damp, heavy heat; the noun of the adjective schwül (humid, muggy).
Nacht + Rennen: a race held after dark; the last noun of a compound gives the gender (das Rennen).
Früher (earlier) as an adjective, with the dative plural ending -en: „bei neun früheren Besuchen“ = on nine earlier visits.
Der Rückstand: how far behind someone is, the opposite of Vorsprung; „mit 24 Sekunden Rückstand“ = 24 seconds behind.
Start + Aufstellung (line-up): the order in which the cars stand at the start of a race; „ans Ende der Startaufstellung“ = to the back of the grid.
Partizip II of versetzen (to move to another place); ver- is not separable, so there is no ge-: „ans Ende versetzt“ = sent to the back.
Vorn (also vorne) is the opposite of hinten; „nach vorn“ = to the front, forward: „fuhr auf Rang neun nach vorn“ = moved up to ninth place.
Schluss (end) + Phase: the last part of a race or a game; „in der Schlussphase“ = in the closing stages.

Präteritum of zurückfallen (to fall back). The verb is separable, but at the end of a subordinate clause it is written as one word: „bevor er auf Rang sechs zurückfiel“ = before he dropped back to sixth place.
Die Folge: one thing after another; „in Folge“ = in a row: „zwei Rennen in Folge“ = two races in a row.
A formal word for obwohl; it sends the verb to the end of its clause.
Außer takes the dative: „außer Reichweite“ = out of reach, „außer ihm“ = except for him.
Die Reichweite: how far one can reach; „außer Reichweite“ = out of reach, with no article.
Der Champion, an English loan: the winner of a championship; after sein it takes no article: „könnte Champion sein“ = could be champion.
A numeral + -er makes a decade: „die 1940er Jahre“ = the 1940s (read: neunzehnhundertvierziger); the form never changes, so the dative is „in den 1940er Jahren“.
The first name of Edson Arantes do Nascimento, the Brazilian boy of this story, whom the world later called Pelé.
The place in Brazil where Edson grew up; place names take no article: „in Bauru“.
Der Ball, plural die Bälle; as the object of „hat“ it stands in the accusative: „keinen Ball“, „einen Ball“.
Die Socke, plural die Socken: „eine Socke mit Papier füllen“ = to fill a sock with paper.
Plural of die Teestube: Tee + Stube (a small room), a simple place where tea is served; „in Teestuben arbeiten“ = to work in tea shops.
Der Verein: a sports club, here a football club; „in einem großen Verein“ = in a big club.
Sechs + zehn = 16, but the s of sechs drops out: sechzehn; „mit sechzehn“ = at sixteen.
Genitive of Brasilien with -s and no apostrophe: „Brasiliens Mannschaft“ = Brazil's team.
Die Mannschaft: the team in a sport; nouns in -schaft are always feminine.
Das Finale: the last game of a tournament, the one that decides the winner; „im Finale“ = in the final.
Short for die Weltmeisterschaft and said as two letters (We-Em): „im Finale der WM“ = in the World Cup final.
Schießen (to shoot): er schießt, schoss, hat geschossen; German „shoots“ a goal: „zwei Tore schießen“ = to score two goals.
Das Tor, plural die Tore: the goal in football (the word also means a gate); „ein Tor schießen“ = to score a goal.
The name by which the world knows Edson Arantes do Nascimento, the Brazilian footballer of this story.
The second part of the full name Edson Arantes do Nascimento, the boy later called Pelé.
Not a German word: a Portuguese „of the“ inside the family name „do Nascimento“.
The last part of the full name Edson Arantes do Nascimento, the boy later called Pelé.
