Voltaire (1694–1778), the French writer of Candide, who lived at Ferney from 1759.
Voltaire's short novel of 1759 and its hero; the title stays in French in every language.
The village right by Geneva where Voltaire lived from 1759; today it is called Ferney-Voltaire.
The name Ferney took after Voltaire; it became official in 1878, a hundred years after his death.
Der Februar: the months are all masculine, and „in“ + month becomes „im“: „im Februar“.
Der Bauernhof = Bauer (farmer) + Hof (yard): „auf einem Bauernhof leben“ = to live on a farm.
„Der letzte Satz ist berühmt“ = the last line is famous; after „sein“ the adjective takes no ending.
Das Pech = bad luck: „nach viel Pech“ = after a lot of bad luck; „Pech gehabt!“ = tough luck!
The old word for working the land: „den Garten bestellen“ = to cultivate the garden; in a shop or café bestellen means to order.
german.translation: to cultivate, till (a garden or field)

german.note: Sumpfig (swampy, from der Sumpf); -em is the dative neuter ending with no article: „auf sumpfigem Land“.
Plural of die Katastrophe; „ein Leben voller Katastrophen“ = a lifetime of disasters, „voller“ meaning full of.
Die Langeweile = lange (long) + Weile (a while): time that feels too long.
Das Laster = a vice, a bad habit; careful, der Laster (masculine) is a lorry.
Die Not = real need or hardship, not the English „not“: „in Not sein“ = to be in need.
Fernhalten (to keep away), er/sie/es form, written as one word at the end of a „dass“ clause; in a main clause it splits: „hält … fern“.
Partizip II of vormachen, with ge- between particle and stem: „er hat es vorgemacht“ = he showed how by doing it himself.
Pflastern (to pave) used as an adjective: „gepflasterte Straßen“ = paved streets, -e for a plural with no article.
Die Nichte = niece, a sister's or brother's daughter; the nephew is der Neffe.
French for Mrs, kept before a French name: Madame Denis, Voltaire's niece.
Madame Denis, Voltaire's niece, in whose name Ferney was bought in 1759.
Der Held, the hero of a story; a weak noun: „den Helden“. A heroine is die Heldin.
Der Hof: a farmyard, and so a small farm; short here for Bauernhof.
Das Übel = an evil, something harmful; the plural looks the same: „drei große Übel“.
„Sich von der Welt abschotten“ = to shut yourself off from the world; ab + schotten (from das Schott, a ship's bulkhead), here whole after „sollte“.
Plural of der Sumpf, with an umlaut: der Sumpf → die Sümpfe.
Partizip II of trockenlegen (to drain land): trocken (dry) + legen (lay), with ge- in the middle: trocken-ge-legt.
„Viermal so viele“ = four times as many; -mal makes a number into how many times: einmal, zweimal, viermal.
Read siebzehnhundertachtzig; a year on its own needs no „im“: „1780 hatte es …“.
Read achtzehnhundertachtundsiebzig: the year the name Ferney-Voltaire became official.
Das Sumpfland = der Sumpf (swamp) + das Land; the gender comes from the last part: „das Sumpfland gesünder machen“ = to make the swampy land healthier.

italian.note: Centocinquanta, written as one word: 150 g = centocinquanta grammi.
The year Little Women was first published.
Surname of Louisa May Alcott, the author of Little Women.
The main character of this story.
Emily Dickinson, the poet in this story.
Emily Dickinson, the poet in this story.
Jo March, a character in Little Women.
The main character of the four-count-breath story.
Part of the author's full name, Louisa May Alcott.
The US state where Amherst is.
The American writer often credited with this quote.
The main character of the morning-light story.
Basic preposition of place or direction; "ad" is used before a vowel.
Used both for sufficiency and as an intensifier.
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
Infinitive; also used for "to accommodate" customers.
Feminine past participle of accorgersi, "to realize."
Basic word for water; the contractions mean "of/on/in the water."
As in military or professional training.
A person assigned to a task.
Describes something you can count on.
From affrontare, used for facing a difficulty.
From aggiungere, to add; aggiunto = added ("ha aggiunto" = added, has added); aggiungi is the tu imperative of recipes: aggiungi panna e pollo = add cream and chicken.
As in "a proprio agio," at ease.
Contraction of a + il; in dish names it tells what it's made with: pollo al burro = butter chicken.
italian.translation: to the / at the; (in dishes) with

italian.note: Indefinite adjective/pronoun agreeing in gender and number.
Feminine plural past participle of alimentare.
Fixed phrase for being in the open air.
Describes a worrying rate or trend.
A common connector word; opening a sentence it is the spoken so, well: allora, siamo nel 1947 = so, it's 1947.
italian.translation: then / in that case; so, well

italian.note: Altro/a/i/e agree in gender and number; altrove means "elsewhere."
Agrees in gender with the noun it describes.
One of the most common Italian adverbs.
Used here figuratively, to anchor a rhythm.
From andare, a key irregular verb.
Anno/anni; the contractions mean "of the year" and "this year."
Corrects or strengthens the previous statement.
Past participle of aprire, used as an adjective (open) and after avere: hanno aperto = they opened.
Color adjective, invariable form used here for plural.
The material of the water carrier's pots.
Here, the main point of an idea.
As in "time and attention." Un' = una before a vowel (un'attenzione).
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
Tools or gear needed for a task.
As in an increase in customers.
Used here for native tree species.
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
"Aver" is the truncated form used before a consonant.
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
Guides plastic into the collection basket.
Forms of battere, to beat: a heart that beats ("il cuore batteva"), or a team that beats another ("ha battuto il Leipzig").
Forms of bello before different nouns.
"Ben" is a shortened form used before adjectives.
A general word for a drink.
Bianco (masculine), bianca (feminine): white; "vestiti di bianco" = dressed in white, "nero su bianco" = in black and white, in writing.
As in "avere bisogno di," to need.
Bollire (verb) and bollore (noun, the boiling point).
As in a purse or handbag.
The hollow pressed into the rice.
Buio/buia, also buio as a noun for darkness.
Forms of buono agreeing with the noun.
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
Caldo/calda; caldissimo = very hot (-issimo means very).
Calmo/calma, also calma as a noun for calmness.
The noun form, a walk taken.
From cantare; canto can also mean "song" as a noun.
As in opening the wallet with caution.
A more literary synonym of famoso.
Cento = 100; the compounds mean "fifty years" and "a hundred fifty years."
As in the center of the rice ball.
As in sleep helping the brain.
From cessare, to cease: cessa is the present (it ceases), cesseranno the future (they will cease).
One of the most common Italian words, linking clauses.
From chiamare; chiamarsi = to be named: si chiamano Kundan Lal = they're called Kundan Lal.
italian.translation: to call; si chiama(no) = is/are called

italian.note: Short for chilogrammo: un chilo, due chili.
A very flexible little word, also used in c'è.
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
The first meal of the day.
As in "sentirsi in colpa," to feel guilty.
From cominciare, a synonym of iniziare.
Completo/a, completamente as adverb, completare as verb.
Past participle of complicare used as adjective.
From concepire, as Dickinson conceives of hope.
As in the texture of a mixture.
As in "al contrario," on the contrary.
From intuitivo, "intuitive," with the counter- prefix.
As in finding the courage to begin.
As in "nel corso di," in the course of.
From costare: costa = it costs, costano = they cost.
A very common connector and intensifier.
The flaw in the cracked pot.
A relative pronoun used after a preposition.
Cuocere = to cook, in a pan or in the oven; cuoceva (he/she) and cuocevano (they) are the imperfect: cooked, used to cook.
italian.translation: to cook; was cooking, used to cook

italian.note: Both the organ and the emotional sense.
Cura as noun "care"; curava, imperfect of curare, "to tend to."
The spice that turns milk golden.
Contraction di + affari, as in "uomo d'affari."
Contraction di + avena, as in oat milk.
Past participle of dare, also "a given fact."
As in "davanti a," in front of.
Contractions of di + il/i/lo/la/le, forms of the partitive.
A more formal synonym of soldi.
One of the most common Italian prepositions.
From dire, an irregular verb: dice = says, dicono = they say (dicono che = people say that), diceva = said, used to say.
Plural of difesa, as in the body's defenses.
The pot's crack, seen as a flaw.
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
As in "preso dimora," taken up residence.
"Dir" is the truncated form of dire before a consonant.
Feminine of discreto, here "a fair amount."
Feminine plural past participle of disperdere.
From diventare, a very common verb.
First person of dare. In the Portuguese name "Arantes do Nascimento", "do" is Portuguese for "of the".
As in preparing lunch for tomorrow.
Plural of donna; title "Piccole donne," Little Women.
As in "il doppio," twice as much.
Duro/dura as adjective, duramente as adverb; dura is also the present of durare: "dura tre ore" = it lasts three hours.
Describes the body processing food well.
As in either end of the pole.
From fare; also used for "ago," as in "cinquant'anni fa."
As in "nel pieno delle proprie facoltà," in one's right mind.
Second person of fare, also its tu imperative; fai + infinitive = make something happen: fai sciogliere il burro = melt the butter.
italian.translation: you do / make; do, make (tu imperative)

italian.note: From fare, one of the most common irregular verbs.
Past participle of fare; "fatto" can also mean "fact."
As in a slice of bread.
As in growing confidence from practice.
"Fin" is short for fino; finché means "until", and the non that often follows adds no negation: finché non diventa nero = until it goes black.
As in the end of the week.
From finire; finire in + place = to end up in: sono finite in tribunale = they ended up in court.
italian.translation: to finish; to end up (finire in)

italian.note: A sheet of paper, or of something thin: "un foglio di alga" = a sheet of seaweed.
As in the back of the fridge.
As in giving something a shape.
Foto is invariable; fotografia is the fuller word.
As in the body's brake pedal.
From frullare (to blend): frulla = blends, or blend! as a tu imperative; frullala = blend it; frullava = blended, used to blend (imperfect).
As in "a fuoco lento," on low heat.
Giornata refers to the day as an experience.
As in "nel giro di," within (a period of time).
Masculine plural article, or indirect object pronoun "to him."
"Gran" is a shortened form before certain nouns.
As in a letter of gratitude.
As in "il corpo ti sarà grato," the body will be grateful.
The standard word for thanks; grazie a / grazie ai = thanks to ("grazie ai gol di Díaz").
As in a tangle of saplings.
From impostare, as in setting a timer.
Describes being tied to a desk.
The dent pressed into the rice.
As in drivers reacting with indignation.
Marks the last step in a sequence.
As in "ha deciso di provarlo," determined to try.
Interno/interna, also "interno" as a noun for "inside."
L' + altro. "Tra l'altro" = by the way, among other things.
L' + asprezza, of the tomato's tartness.

italian.translation: had it / has it / they have it

italian.note: Feminine singular article, or object pronoun "her/it."
As in each side of the path.
As in a can of tomatoes.
The main ingredient of golden milk.
Feminine plural article, or object pronoun "them" (feminine). Also the pronoun "to her", and with Lei "to you": "Le serve" = you need, "le dà" = gives you.
italian.translation: the / them; to her, to you (formal Lei)

italian.note: As in a letter received in the mail.
Letto as noun "bed," or past participle of leggere.
Masculine plural direct object pronoun (li vedo = I see them); also li, the old Chinese measure of distance, about half a kilometre (mille li).
italian.translation: them; (a Chinese li) about half a kilometre

italian.note: As in the book Little Women.
Imperfect of liquidare, here "to dismiss (an idea)."
Feminine of liscio, as in a smooth soup.
As in a long to-do list.
Masculine singular article (before s+consonant/z), or object pronoun "it/him."
As in the song traveling far.
A general word for a place.
One of the most common contrastive conjunctions.
As in fare male (to hurt); niente male = not bad at all, said with pleasant surprise; meno male = thank goodness.

italian.note: As in a ship captain's rough weather.
As in a handful of ingredients.
As in material for a journal entry.
The opposite of "più." "Meno male!" = thank goodness!; "fare a meno di" = to do without.
As in a busy mind at night.
From mescolare; mescola is also the tu imperative of recipes: mescola il pollo con yogurt = mix the chicken with yoghurt.
As in trying something for a month.
From migliorare; migliore/migliori = better, with the article the best.
From misurare, "to measure"; in sport, vincere di misura = to win narrowly, by one goal.
As in "in modo che," so that.
Molto agrees in gender and number, or is used as an adverb.
Used figuratively for a huge task.
As in the walls of a house.
As in the space needed to recover.
Nessuno agrees in gender before a noun.
Niente, a common negative pronoun; niente male = not bad (at all).
The basic disjunctive conjunction. Anche la lettera del gruppo sanguigno O.
As in one more obligation on a list.
Ogni is invariable; ognuna is feminine "each one."
As in "oltre mille anni," over a thousand years.
Japanese rice balls; the title of this story.
As in "un paio d'ore," a couple of hours.
Palmo, plural palmi, of the hand.
The wooden pole across the shoulders.
The baked good sold at the bakery.
La panna: cream, often stirred into soups and sauces at the end; panna montata = whipped cream.
As in the parasympathetic nervous system.
The noun parte/parti; also the verb partire: «parte primo» = he starts first.
As in one small step at a time.
As in "non ho paura," I'm not afraid.
As in the body's brake pedal.
As in "vale la pena," it's worth it.
One of the most common Italian prepositions.
Describes the pocket forest's quiet argument.
As in "mettere piede," to set foot.
As in cycling in the rain.
Plural of piuma, from the Dickinson poem.
As in a pinch of salt.
One of the most common Italian words.
Short for "poco," as in "un po' di."
Porta as noun "door," or verb form of portare.
The wallet found on the train.
From posarsi, as in the bird perching.
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
As in a letter arriving by mail.
Pratica (noun), pratico (adjective); "in pratica" = in practice. In an office, la pratica = the paperwork, the application.
As in "prestare attenzione," to pay attention.
As in going to bed early.
As in "dal principio," from the start.
A masculine noun despite the -a ending.
Proprio agrees in gender and number (la propria casa); as a talk word it means really, just (è proprio così).
italian.translation: own / one's own; (in speech) really, just

italian.note: Provare (verb: to try, to test); la prova (noun: proof, test).
italian.translation: to try, to test / proof, test

italian.note: As in a pickled plum filling.
A point of an argument, or points in a ranking: «123 punti di vantaggio».
As in "per pura curiosità," out of pure curiosity.
The green notebook in this story.
Quale, plural quali: quale dei due? = which of the two?
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
Invariable noun ending in an accented vowel.
A comparison/quantity word; a quanto pare / a quanto si racconta = apparently, from what people say.
italian.translation: how much / as much as; a quanto = from what

italian.note: The ordinal (il quarto giro, the fourth round); un quarto = a quarter (di circa un quarto = by about a quarter).
Quello agrees in gender and number.
Questo agrees in gender and number.
As in "le quinte dei concerti," concert wings.
Reale, plural reali; realmente as adverb.
Regione is singular, regioni the plural; feminine: la regione.
As in Dickinson's rendering of hope.
Riconoscendo is the gerund (recognizing); riconosciuto the past participle (recognized); "riconosciuta" is its feminine.

English word, in the report's English title The Science of Hope; in Italian: la speranza.
Against the law, the opposite of legale; the plural is illegali.
Present of intitolarsi (lui/lei), from il titolo, the title: il rapporto si intitola… = the report is called…
L'otto: dates take the article, and before otto it is l': l'8 ottobre = (on) 8 October.
What you learn from a class or from an experience: la sua lezione è semplice = its lesson is simple; the plural is lezioni.
Plural of il limite, the point you may not go past: i limiti di pesca = fishing limits.
English word, in the name Living Planet Report, which Italian keeps in English.
From la magia, magic: niente di magico = nothing magical (after niente the adjective takes di).
Feminine of marino, of the sea (il mare): una tartaruga marina = a sea turtle.
Short form of minore, smaller or less; «Minor Preoccupazione» is the Italian name of the Red List category Least Concern.
From il nido, the nest: le spiagge di nidificazione are the beaches where the turtles lay their eggs.
English word, in the report's English title The Science of Hope; in Italian: di.
80; the tens end in -anta from quaranta on: quaranta, cinquanta, sessanta, settanta, ottanta, novanta.
Past participle of pagare, to pay: hanno pagato più ranger = they paid more rangers.
Past participle of perseguire, to go after someone so that the law can stop them: hanno perseguito i trafficanti = they pursued the traffickers.
From pescare, to fish: i limiti di pesca = fishing limits; una pesca is also a peach.
English word, in the name Living Planet Report; in Italian: il pianeta.
All the animals (or people) of one kind that live in a place; the plural is popolazioni.
The most important one: il dato principale = the main figure; the plural is principali.
Plural of il progresso, a step forward; Italian often uses the plural: fare progressi = to make progress.
Present of proteggere (loro), to keep safe: le persone proteggono le foreste = people protect the forests.
An English word used in Italian for a person who guards a forest or a park; it never changes: il ranger, i ranger.
English word, in the name Living Planet Report, which Italian keeps in English; in Italian: il rapporto.
Past participle of riprendersi, to get well or strong again; it takes essere: il tonno si è ripreso = the tuna recovered.
Past participle of scendere (irregular: sceso), to go down; feminine plural to agree with le tigri: scese a 3.200 = down to 3,200.
English word, in the report's English title The Science of Hope; in Italian: la scienza.
The careful study of the world, the work of scientists (gli scienziati): la scienza della speranza = the science of hope.
Past participle of servire, which also means to be needed: sono serviti quindici anni = it took fifteen years (fifteen years were needed).
Past participle of sorvegliare, to keep watch over something; feminine plural to agree with le spiagge.
A second title under the main one (sotto = under): ha per sottotitolo… = it has as its subtitle…
Plural of la spiaggia; nouns in -ggia drop the i in the plural: spiaggia, spiagge.
One word for the animal on land and in the sea: una tartaruga marina = a sea turtle; the plural is tartarughe.
Present of tentare (lui/lei): dove lo si tenta = where it is attempted (where one tries it).
English word, in the report's English title The Science of Hope; il tè, the drink, is a different word.
Plural of la tigre; the noun is feminine for every tiger, male or female: le tigri selvatiche.
A large sea fish; il tonno rosso (red tuna) is the Italian name of the bluefin tuna.
Plural of il trafficante, a person who buys and sells illegal goods (from il traffico).
Past participle of trattarsi di, to be a matter of: non si è trattato di un miracolo = it was not a miracle.
italian.translation: been a matter of (si è trattato di)

italian.note: The organisation that published the report on 8 October 2026; Italian keeps the letters and says il WWF.
Read "undici"; dates use the plain number, without "of": domenica 11 ottobre = Sunday, 11 October.
Read "ventiquattro": a 24 secondi dal vincitore = 24 seconds behind the winner.
Read "venticinque"; a date takes the article il: il 25 ottobre = on 25 October.
Read "sessantadue": tutti i 62 giri = all 62 laps of the race.
Read "centodue": 102 punti di vantaggio = 102 points ahead, Antonelli's lead in the championship.
Read "duecentocinquantesimo"; the small º turns a number into a masculine ordinal: il suo 250º Gran Premio = his 250th Grand Prix.
A city in Texas, in the United States, with a Formula 1 track; ad Austin = in Austin, with ad before the vowel.
Charles Leclerc, the Ferrari driver who finished second in Singapore.
First name of the McLaren driver Lando Norris.
Lando Norris, the McLaren driver who finished fourth in Singapore.
First name of the McLaren driver Oscar Piastri.
Oscar Piastri, the McLaren driver who finished fifth in Singapore.
The Formula 1 team of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri; team names take the feminine article: la McLaren, and le McLaren = the McLaren cars.
The ordinal of nove: arriva nono = he finishes ninth; al nono posto = in ninth place.
Before a length of time fra looks ahead from now: fra due settimane = in two weeks; fra and tra mean the same.
Gli Stati Uniti = the United States: stati is here the plural of lo stato (state), and uniti agrees with it; negli Stati Uniti = in the United States.
Past participle of gareggiare, to take part in a race (una gara): ha gareggiato di notte = it raced at night.
A punishment under the rules of a sport; nouns ending in an accented -à do not change in the plural: le penalità.
The machine that makes a car move; una penalità per il motore = an engine penalty.
The ordinal of sei: è arrivato sesto = he finished sixth; al sesto posto = in sixth place.
Di fila = in a row, one after the other: due gare di fila = two races in a row.
Here the championship title: vincere il titolo = to become champion; il titolo is also the name of a book or a film.
Plural of il riflettore, a strong lamp that lights a stage or a stadium; sotto i riflettori = under the floodlights.
The ordinal of cinque: quarto e quinto = fourth and fifth.
Irregular past participle of scendere (to go down), with essere: è sceso al sesto posto = he dropped to sixth place.
Essere al comando = to be in the lead: è al comando del campionato = he leads the championship.
Contraction in + l'umidità (nell' before a vowel); l'umidità, feminine, is the noun of umido (humid).
Feminine of notturno, the adjective of la notte: la gara notturna = the night race.
Plural of la presenza; in sport una presenza is one time that someone takes part: nove presenze = nine appearances.
Past participle of staccare (to detach), used as an adjective in sport: staccato di 24 secondi = 24 seconds behind.
Past participle of relegare, to send to a lower or worse place: relegato in fondo alla griglia = sent to the back of the grid.
La griglia is a grill (alla griglia = on the grill, grilled) and, in racing, the starting grid: in fondo alla griglia = at the back of the grid.
Plural of the adjective finale, the same for masculine and feminine: le fasi finali = the closing stages.
From raggiungere (to reach) with the negative prefix ir- (in- before r) and -ibile (-able): something that cannot be reached.
The winner of a championship (il campionato); the feminine is la campionessa.
Millenovecentosessantadue, the year of Pelé's second World Cup; a year takes the article: nel 1962 = in 1962.
Ventitré; a date takes il and the plain number, without "of": il 23 ottobre 1940 = 23 October 1940, the day Pelé was born.
Ventinove; a date takes il and the plain number: il 29 giugno 1958 = 29 June 1958, il 29 dicembre 2022 = 29 December 2022.
A football score, said cinque a due: il Brasile ha vinto 5–2 = Brazil won by five goals to two.
Imperfect of allenarsi (lui/lei), a reflexive verb, to train: si allenava con un calzino = he practised with a sock.
Part of the full name of Pelé: Edson Arantes do Nascimento.
The town in Brazil where Edson grows up; a city takes a or di without an article: a Bauru = in Bauru, di Bauru = from Bauru.
A person who plays football (il calcio); the plural is calciatori. After essere the article can be left out: era calciatore.
A short sock; the plural is calzini. Un calzino pieno di carta is the boy's ball in this story.
An English word that Italian uses for a football club; it never changes: il club, i club.
Passato remoto of convocare (lui/lei); in sport it means to call a player into the national team: il Brasile lo convocò.
A cup, also the prize of a competition: la Coppa del Mondo = the World Cup, the football tournament that Italians also call i Mondiali.
The material of shoes, bags and old footballs: un pallone di cuoio = a leather ball.
The name by which the father of Pelé, a footballer, is known.
The first name of Edson Arantes do Nascimento, the boy whom the world later knows as Pelé.
Past participle of firmare, to sign your name: ha firmato per il Santos = he signed (a contract) for Santos.
Formare (to form, to shape) with the pronoun lo (him) joined to the infinitive: a formarlo non fu il pallone = what made him was not the ball.
italian.translation: to shape him, to make him

italian.note: A person who plays (giocare) a game or a sport; the plural is giocatori: nessun altro giocatore = no other player.
From giocare, to play: il gioco here is football; the plural is giochi.
The sixth month; months are masculine and written in lower case: il 29 giugno 1958.
From the English goal; it never changes: un gol, due gol. Fare gol or fare un gol = to score.
To get money for your work: lavorava per guadagnare soldi = he worked to earn money; a regular -are verb.
Imperfect of imbottire (lui/lei), to fill something tight with soft material: lo imbottiva di giornali = he stuffed it with newspaper.
In- (not) + eguagliato, equalled: un titolo che resta ineguagliato = a title that nobody else has reached.
Passato remoto of ingaggiare (lui/lei), said of a club that takes on a player: il Santos lo ingaggiò = Santos signed him.
I Mondiali, always plural and with a capital letter, is the everyday name of the football World Cup (la Coppa del Mondo): ai Mondiali = to the World Cup.
The last part of the full name of Pelé: Edson Arantes do Nascimento.
Ottanta + due, written as one word: a ottantadue anni = at the age of eighty-two.
The large ball of football and other sports (una palla is any ball); the plural is palloni.
One game of football or another sport: l'ultima partita dei Mondiali = the last match of the World Cup, the one that decides it; the plural is partite.
The name by which the world knows the Brazilian footballer Edson Arantes do Nascimento.
Gerund of potere; with non it gives a reason: non potendo la famiglia permettersene uno = as the family could not afford one.
The net, and in football the goal that ends in it: andare in rete = to score; the plural is reti.
The Brazilian football club that Pelé joins at fifteen; clubs take the article: il Santos.
The number 16; an age takes a: a sedici anni = at sixteen, or just a sedici when anni has already been said.
Countries take the article (la Svezia), but not after in: in Svezia = in Sweden; contro la Svezia = against Sweden, the national team.
A competition of many matches with one winner at the end; here the World Cup: vincere il torneo = to win the tournament.
Passato remoto of vincere (lui/lei), the past tense of written stories: il Brasile la vinse 5–2 = Brazil won it 5–2; in speech: ha vinto.
The year Sweden's parental leave began; said millenovecentosettantaquattro, and a year takes the article: il 1974, nel 1974 = in 1974.
A rule that a state makes for everyone, here a law: una nuova norma = a new law; di norma means as a rule, usually.
The year Sweden reserved one month for each parent; said millenovecentonovantacinque: nel 1995 = in 1995.
The family word for padre; the accent is on the last a and the plural does not change: il mese del papà = the father's month, literally the dad's month.
The man a person is married to (the wife is la moglie): un marito o partner = a husband or partner.
Fumare is a regular -are verb: non fuma = he does not smoke; smettere di fumare = to stop smoking, with di before the infinitive.
Present of the reflexive alzarsi (lui/lei), to get up: di notte si alza = he gets up at night; without si, alzare means to raise. Of the wind, "si alza il vento" = the wind picks up.
italian.translation: gets up (si alza); (of the wind) picks up

italian.note: All' = a + l' before a vowel; chiedere takes a before the person you ask: chiedono all'ostetrica = they ask the midwife.
Past participle of introdurre (irregular, like ridurre → ridotto): la Svezia ha introdotto una nuova norma = Sweden brought in a new law.
Italian writes decimals with a comma where English uses a point: 0,5 = zero virgola cinque; lo 0,5 per cento = 0.5 per cent.
Dividere is to split something between people (dividere le notti = to share the nights; dividersi = to share out between them) or to divide a country: l'India è stata divisa = India was divided.
italian.translation: to share, to split, to divide; divided

italian.note: Time away from work that the law allows: il congedo parentale = parental leave; il congedo di maternità = maternity leave.
Of the parents (i genitori); careful, i parenti are relatives, not parents: il congedo parentale = parental leave.
The number of paid days the parents could share; said centottanta.
Italian writes decimals with a comma: 99,5 = novantanove virgola cinque; il 99,5 per cento = 99.5 per cent.
What comes from a cigarette, and also the habit of smoking; il fumo passivo is the smoke other people breathe in (fumo is also "I smoke", from fumare).
From il danno, damage; it takes per: può essere dannoso per il bambino = it can be harmful for the baby.
Reflexive, and followed by di: occuparsi di alcune poppate = to see to some of the feeds.
italian.translation: to take care of, to see to

italian.note: Plural of la poppata, one meal of milk for a baby, at the breast or from a bottle.
The noun of triste, sad; the ending -ezza makes a noun from an adjective, as in bello → bellezza.
The new thing comes after con: sostituire il congedo di maternità con il congedo parentale = to replace maternity leave with parental leave.
Nouns in -tà are feminine and do not change in the plural; il congedo di maternità = maternity leave, the leave for the mother.
L' + uno, used in a pair with l'altro: l'uno o l'altro genitore = one parent or the other, either parent.
A change to a law or a system; here the change of 1995: prima della riforma = before the reform.
Il fumo passivo is the smoke of someone else's cigarette that the people nearby breathe in: second-hand smoke.
The given name of Virginia Woolf (1882–1941), the English writer who gave two talks in Cambridge in October 1928.
Virginia Woolf, English novelist and essayist, author of A Room of One's Own (1929); Italian keeps the surname unchanged.
Newnham College, founded in 1871, one of the two colleges for women in Cambridge in 1928; il college is masculine in Italian.
Girton College, founded in 1869, the other college for women in Cambridge where Woolf spoke in 1928.
The year A Room of One's Own came out; said millenovecentoventinove, and with the article: nel 1929 = in 1929.
The year Cambridge first gave women full degrees; prima del 1948 = before 1948, with di + il = del.
Cinque + cento written as one word, like all Italian numbers: cinquecento sterline = five hundred pounds.
The degree you get at the end of university; prendere la laurea = to get one's degree.
Plural of discorso, a talk given to an audience; tenere un discorso = to give a talk.
Plural of conferenza, a talk given to an audience, not a meeting: tenere una conferenza = to give a talk.
The lock built into a door; you close it with a key: chiudere a chiave = to lock.
Plural of sterlina, the British pound; the currency is feminine in Italian: cinquecento sterline.
Università is feminine and ends in a stressed -à, so it takes l' before the vowel and never changes in the plural; dell' = di + l'.
Adjectives in -e have one form for masculine and feminine: l'idea centrale, il punto centrale.
Novels and stories as a kind of writing, as opposed to essays or poetry: scrivere narrativa = to write fiction.
Feminine, with a stressed -à that never changes in the plural: la libertà di pensare = the freedom to think.
Plural of romanziere, a person who writes romanzi (novels); -iere becomes -ieri.
Careful thinking about something; un lavoro che richiede riflessione = work that needs thought.
Plural of ascoltatrice, the feminine of ascoltatore (from ascoltare, to listen); -trice becomes -trici.
Plural of femminile, one form for both genders: i college femminili = the women's colleges.
Past participle of rivedere (to revise), feminine plural to agree with le conferenze; as a noun, riviste also means magazines.
Past participle of racchiudere (to enclose), feminine to agree with la tesi: è racchiusa = is contained, a passive.
The infinitive after per for a purpose: il tempo per riflettere = the time to reflect.
An advantage only some people have; masculine, plural privilegi.
The year Bircher-Benner opens his sanatorium; said millenovecentoquattro, and with the article: nel 1904 = in 1904.
First name of Maximilian Bircher-Benner (1867–1939), the Swiss doctor who created the dish now called muesli.
Surname of Maximilian Bircher-Benner, a doctor in Zurich; the double name is one hyphenated word.
The Italian name of the Swiss city of Zürich; city names are feminine, but Zurigo is used without an article: a Zurigo = in Zurich.
The adjective for Zurigo, one form for both genders: un medico zurighese = a Zurich doctor.
Svizzero tedesco is the German spoken in Switzerland; like other language names it is masculine: in svizzero tedesco = in Swiss German.
Swiss German for "the dish", Bircher-Benner's own name for his apple meal; it is kept as it is in every language.
German word in the name of the sanatorium, Lebendige Kraft; it is left in German and glossed as forza viva.
German noun in the name Lebendige Kraft (living strength); German capitalises all nouns.
Feminine of vivo, agreeing with forza: forza viva = living strength.
A clinic where patients stay for a long rest and a special diet, often in the mountains or above a town.
Italian uses the singular for the grain: un cucchiaio di avena = a spoon of oats.
Used in the phrase in ammollo: lascia in ammollo = leave to soak (in water, so it softens).
Past participle of ammollare (to soak), feminine to agree with avena: avena ammollata = soaked oats.
Not cooked; it agrees with its noun: mela cruda (feminine), cibo crudo (masculine).
From grattugiare: grattugia is the tu imperative of a recipe, grattugiata the participle that agrees with mela; as a noun, la grattugia is the grater.
Past participle of tritare (to chop finely), feminine plural to agree with noci: noci tritate = chopped nuts.
As much as a spoon holds; the suffix -ata turns an object into its contents, like boccata (mouthful).
Tu imperative of incorporare, to work an ingredient into a mixture until it disappears into it.
Tu imperative of cospargere; the thing scattered follows di: cospargi la superficie di noci = scatter nuts over the top.
A loanword that does not change in the plural.
Made thicker by removing water: latte condensato = condensed milk.
From zucchero (sugar), masculine to agree with latte: latte condensato zuccherato = sweetened condensed milk.
A lung disease; in the past it could be passed on through fresh milk. Feminine, unchanged in the plural.
Past participle of servire (to serve food); with essere it forms the passive and agrees with the subject: era servita (mela), era servito (ciò).
Gives the purpose of an action and is always followed by the subjunctive: affinché resti bianca = so that it stays white.
The mountain range across Switzerland, Italy, France and Austria; always plural: le Alpi, sulle Alpi = in the Alps.
Feminine; it usually takes the article (l'Europa) but drops it after in: in tutta Europa = all over Europe.
A loanword from Swiss German for a dish of oats, fruit and nuts; masculine and unchanged in the plural.
Any of the day's meals (colazione, pranzo, cena); plural pasti.
From sera, one form for both genders: un pasto serale = an evening meal.
Written as one word or as per lo più; it means for the most part.
L' + originale: as a noun it means the first version from which later ones came.
The year Haiti became independent; said milleottocentoquattro, and a date takes il: il primo gennaio 1804 = 1 January 1804.
The Caribbean country that became independent from France in 1804; it is used without an article and treated as feminine: Haiti è libera.
Plural forms of haitiano, from Haiti; with the article it works as a noun: gli haitiani = Haitian people, le famiglie haitiane = Haitian families.
Soup joumou is the Haitian Creole name of the pumpkin soup eaten every 1 January; Italian keeps the name unchanged and makes it feminine, like zuppa: la soup joumou.
La zucca is pumpkin or squash; una zuppa di zucca = a pumpkin soup (di + the ingredient).
The green citrus fruit; the word is borrowed and does not change in the plural: succo di lime = lime juice.
Plural of la patata: feminine nouns in -a take -e in the plural.
Ridotto in schiavitù (reduced to slavery) is the respectful way to say enslaved: it names what was done to people, not who they were; the final accented ù never changes.
Past participle of schiavizzare used as an adjective: i cuochi schiavizzati = the enslaved cooks, the form used instead of a bare schiavi for people.
Plural of il padrone, the person who owns land, a house or, in the history of slavery, other people.
La cultura: the customs, food and arts of a people; la cultura viva = living culture.
Jean-Jacques Dessalines (1758–1806), the leader who declared Haiti's independence at Gonaïves on 1 January 1804; the hyphenated first name is one word.
A town on Haiti's west coast where independence was declared in 1804; the dots on the ï show that a and i are said separately.
Nouns in -zione are feminine: la rivoluzione, plural le rivoluzioni.
Un litro e mezzo = one and a half litres; e mezzo comes after the noun.
Il manzo is the animal and its meat: carne di manzo = beef.
One's own country; in patria e all'estero = at home and abroad.
What a people inherits and keeps alive; il patrimonio vivente = living heritage, UNESCO's term for traditions still practised.
Gerund of porre (irregular, to put); porre fine a = to put an end to: ponendo fine a una rivoluzione = ending a revolution.
From terra (land); it is almost always used in proprietari terrieri = landowners.
Assaggiare (to taste, to try a little) + la (it), joined to the infinitive: permesso assaggiarla = allowed to taste it.
Quindici; dates use the plain number, not an ordinal, except for the first of the month: il 15 giugno = 15 June.
Diciotto; dal 13 al 18 ottobre = from 13 to 18 October, with dal and al (da/a + il) before the days.
The year of the first Paris show, said milleottocentonovantotto; with the article: nel 1898 = in 1898.
Novantunesima: the raised ª marks a feminine ordinal agreeing with volta, so per la 91ª volta = for the 91st time (masculine: 91º).
Centoquarantamila; Italian marks the thousands with a point where English uses a comma.
Cinquecentomila; Italian marks the thousands with a point where English uses a comma: più di 500.000 = more than 500,000.
Cinquecentodiciottomilatrecentosettantadue; the point separates the thousands, where English writes a comma.
Like all tens, sessanta does not change: più di sessanta produttori = more than sixty makers.
The capital of France; Italian has its own form of the name, and cities are feminine: Parigi è grande.
A town just west of Paris, famous for its palace; the name keeps its French spelling and the final s is silent.
A garden in the centre of Paris, next to the Louvre; Italian keeps the French name, plural and feminine: il giardino delle Tuileries.
The French word for di, kept here in a French place name: Porte de Versailles, an exhibition area in the south of Paris.
Il salone dell'auto is a motor show; salone is also a large hall or a living room (from sala, room, + -one, big).
Plural of il produttore, from produrre (to produce): produttori di auto = car makers.
Plural of il costruttore, from costruire; in news about cars it is the usual word for a car maker.
Plural of l'organizzatore, from organizzare; nouns in -tore name the person who does the action.
Plural of il visitatore, the person who visits (visitare); a woman is una visitatrice.
A foreign word, so it does not change in the plural: un taxi, due taxi.
A singular noun for many people; attirare la folla = to draw the crowd.
Plural of il contadino, someone who works the land in the countryside (il contado).
A flat open area raised above the ground; sulla terrazza = on the terrace (su + la).
Plural of il modello; for cars it means one type of car made by a maker.
Plural of il veicolo, a formal word for anything that carries people or goods.
The way from one place to another and the trip along it: il tragitto fino a Versailles = the run to Versailles.
Plural of il mezzo in the sense of 'means'; con i propri mezzi = under its own power, without help.
Quello shortens to quell' before a vowel: quell'estate = that summer (l'estate is feminine, but the form is the same).
Elettrico changes -co to -ci in the masculine plural but keeps the hard sound in the feminine plural -che: taxi elettrici, auto elettriche.
Piccola + -issima, the absolute superlative: -issimo/-issima means 'very' and agrees like any adjective.
Plural of accessibile; for prices and products it means within reach, affordable: più accessibili = more affordable.
Feminine plural of affollato, from folla (crowd); before the noun it sounds literary: le affollate strade.
Plural of automobilistico, the adjective of automobile: costruttori automobilistici = car manufacturers.
Past participle of arare (to plough) used as an adjective: un campo arato = a ploughed field.
Past participle of visitare; after the object pronoun lo it stays masculine: lo hanno visitato = they visited it.
Past participle of partecipare (to take part), with avere: hanno partecipato = they took part.
Past participle of progettare, feminine to agree with l'auto: era stata progettata = it had been designed.
Feminine past participle of esporre, to put on show; it agrees with un'auto in the passive essere esposta.
Past participle of rilanciare (ri- again + lanciare, to launch): bring a name back onto the market.
Imperfect of figurare (loro): to be present in a list or a group; fra le macchine figuravano… = among the machines were…
Passato remoto of accorrere (loro), irregular: to hurry to a place in large numbers.
Read "diciassette"; dates use the plain number: sabato 17 ottobre = Saturday, 17 October.
A football score, read "sei a uno"; the home team's goals come first when the score is given as a result.
Read "tre a zero": all'intervallo era già 3–0 = it was already 3–0 at half-time.
Read "tre a uno": ha vinto 3–1 = won three goals to one.
Read "tre a due": a win by one goal, in Italian press a vittoria di misura.
Read "uno a zero": una vittoria per 1–0 = a 1–0 win; era sotto 1–0 = was 1–0 down.
Read "settantasettesimo"; the small º makes a masculine ordinal: al 77º minuto = in the 77th minute.
Feminine of settimo, agreeing with vittoria: la settima vittoria = the seventh win.
First name of Luis Díaz, the Bayern Munich forward who scored three goals against RB Leipzig.
Luis Díaz, the Bayern Munich player who scored three goals in the 6–1 against RB Leipzig on 17 October 2026.
First name of Aleksandar Pavlović, a Bayern Munich player.
Aleksandar Pavlović, the Bayern Munich player who scored one of the other goals against RB Leipzig.
First name of Michael Olise, a Bayern Munich player.
Michael Olise, the Bayern Munich player who scored one of the other goals against RB Leipzig.
First name of Harry Kane, a Bayern Munich player.
Harry Kane, the Bayern Munich player who scored one of the other goals against RB Leipzig.
FC Bayern Munich, the football club; Italian uses the masculine article and a singular verb: il Bayern vince.
Monaco (di Baviera) is the Italian name of Munich, so the club is il Bayern Monaco; on its own Monaco can also mean the principality of Monaco or a monk.
L' + RB, the start of the club name RB Leipzig: l'RB Leipzig, with l' because the letters are read "erre bi".
RB Leipzig, the football club from the German city of Leipzig (Lipsia in Italian), beaten 6–1 by Bayern.
Borussia Dortmund, the German football club, often just il Dortmund.
Borussia Dortmund, the German football club level with Bayern on 14 points; il Dortmund, masculine like all clubs.
The top German football league; Italian uses it unchanged and feminine: la Bundesliga, in Bundesliga.
Manchester City, the English football club; il Manchester City, often just il City.
Short for Manchester City, the English club with seven wins in seven games; il City.
L' + Ipswich: Ipswich Town, the English club beaten 3–2 by Manchester City; l' before the vowel.
Part of the club name Ipswich Town, from the English town of Ipswich.
L' + Arsenal, the London football club, second in the Premier League; l' before the vowel, masculine like all clubs.
The English city of Nottingham, home of Nottingham Forest; a Nottingham = in Nottingham.
Part of the club name Nottingham Forest, the English club beaten 1–0 by Arsenal.
FC Barcelona, the Spanish football club with nine wins in nine games; il Barcelona (Italian papers also write il Barcellona).
Part of the club name Real Betis; real is Spanish for royal.
Real Betis, the Spanish football club beaten 5–2 at home by Barcelona.
L' + Inter, the Italian football club; Inter is feminine (l'Inter ha vinto, finita in svantaggio), because the full name is l'Internazionale.
Paris Saint-Germain, the French football club, il Paris Saint-Germain; the city itself is Parigi in Italian.
Part of the club name Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), which came back from 1–0 down to win 3–1 in Strasbourg.
The Italian name of Strasbourg, the city in eastern France; a Strasburgo = in Strasbourg.
A + l' + Allianz: all'Allianz Arena = at the Allianz Arena, Bayern Munich's stadium.
Part of the stadium name Allianz Arena, Bayern Munich's home ground; in Italian arena also means sand or arena.
The country; in Germania = in Germany, with no article after in.
The country; in Spagna = in Spain, with no article after in.
The country; in Italia = in Italy, with no article after in.
Feminine plural of altrettanto, agreeing with partite: nove vittorie in altrettante partite = nine wins in as many games.
Pari does not change its ending; alla pari con il Dortmund = level with Dortmund.
A + l' + intervallo: in football the intervallo is the break between the two halves.
In sport, in svantaggio = behind, trailing; the opposite of in vantaggio.
Vincere in rimonta = to win after being behind, to come from behind.
Past participle of rimontare, to come back from behind: ha rimontato e ha vinto = came back and won.
Ribaltare la partita = to turn the match around, from losing to winning.
Three goals by one player in one match; Italian papers say firmare una tripletta, to sign a hat-trick.
Past participle of travolgere, to sweep away: ha travolto l'RB Leipzig 6–1 = swept RB Leipzig aside 6–1.
Past participle of arrotondare, to round off: arrotondare il punteggio = to add more goals to a win already made.
The score of a match; a punteggio pieno = with full points, having won every game.
The top of a mountain; in vetta alla classifica = top of the table.
Gerund of centrare, to hit the target: centrando la settima vittoria = achieving the seventh win.
Vittorioso per 1–0 = the 1–0 winner; it agrees with its noun: l'Arsenal, vittorioso.
Plural of lunghezza, length; in sports papers a tre lunghezze = three points behind.
In sport, a team's run of results: la marcia impeccabile = the flawless run.
Past participle of espugnare, to storm a fortress; in sport, to win on the opponent's ground: ha espugnato il campo del Real Betis.
Sei; dates use the plain number before the month: il 6 gennaio = 6 January.
The year Maria Montessori qualified in medicine, said milleottocentonovantasei; nel 1896 = in 1896.
The year the first Casa dei Bambini opened, said millenovecentosette; il 6 gennaio 1907 = 6 January 1907.
The year Maria Montessori died, said millenovecentocinquantadue; nel 1952 = in 1952.
First name of Maria Montessori; the A1, A2 and B1 texts call her simply Maria, B2 says la Montessori.
Maria Montessori (1870–1952), the Italian doctor whose way of teaching small children is known worldwide; Italians traditionally say la Montessori.
San is the short form of santo before a masculine name that starts with a consonant: San Lorenzo, San Marco.
San Lorenzo is a working-class district of Rome, east of Termini station, where the first Casa dei Bambini opened.
The ending -ina turns a round number into an approximate quantity: una cinquantina di bambini = about fifty children (also una decina, una ventina).
A jug for pouring water or milk; plural le brocche, with an h to keep the hard c sound.
The broom for sweeping the floor; spazzare is the verb that goes with it.
The floor you walk on inside a room; a floor of a building (first floor, second floor) is il piano.
I mobili is plural in Italian where English furniture is uncountable; one piece of furniture is un mobile.
In Italian a palazzo is any large building, usually with flats, not only a palace.
La medicina is the science and the degree subject (laurearsi in medicina); a medicine you take is also una medicina, plural le medicine.
Laurearsi is reflexive and takes essere in compound tenses: si è laureata, si era laureata = she graduated, she had graduated.
From diffondersi, reflexive: il suo metodo si è diffuso = her method spread, the passato prossimo people say; si diffuse is the written passato remoto.
Spazzare (il pavimento) = to sweep (the floor), a regular -are verb: spazzano (present), hanno spazzato (passato prossimo), spazzavano (imperfect).
A very common spoken word: costruito apposta per = built specially for; fare apposta = to do something on purpose.
Un colpo is a blow or a knock; di colpo is the spoken way to say suddenly, like all'improvviso; un colpo di scena = a twist, a surprise.
italian.translation: blow, knock (di colpo = suddenly; colpo di scena = twist)

italian.note: La zecca is the mint where coins are made, so nuovo di zecca, like a fresh coin, means brand-new.
Plural of popolare; le case popolari are flats built by the state or the city for families with little money.
The year the people of North Karelia asked the government for help; years are said as one number: millenovecentosettantuno.
Said duemilaquattordici; fino al 2014 = up to 2014, by 2014.
L' + 80: percentages take the article in Italian, l'80 per cento = 80 percent.
Di + l' + 84: calare dell'84 per cento = to fall by 84 percent; the article goes before a percentage.
A region in eastern Finland (and Russia); la Carelia del Nord = North Karelia, the Finnish region of this story.
The country in northern Europe; in Finlandia = in Finland.
First name of Pekka Puska, the young Finnish doctor who led the North Karelia Project from 1972.
Surname of Pekka Puska, the Finnish doctor who led the North Karelia Project.
Chiedere aiuto = to ask for help; the verb is aiutare.
I frutti di bosco (literally fruits of the wood) are berries: blueberries, raspberries, lingonberries.
Plural of il frutto, one single fruit; la frutta is fruit as food in general. Frutti di bosco = berries.
Imperfect of c'entrare, a spoken idiom: non c'entra niente = it has nothing to do with it.
Il caseificio, plural i caseifici: the dairy plant, not the shop.
italian.translation: dairy (where milk is made into butter and cheese)

italian.note: Past participle of copiare, to copy; aveva copiato l'idea = had copied the idea.
Plural of il grasso, fat in food: il sale e i grassi = salt and fat.
Latte magro is low-fat milk; said of a person, magro means thin.
A spread for bread made from vegetable oils; margarina vegetale = plant-based spread.
Feminine of mezzo; la mezza età = middle age, roughly from 40 to 65.
A letter many people sign to ask for something: firmare una petizione = to sign a petition.
Plural of locale; i rappresentanti locali = the local leaders.
Plural of il rappresentante, someone who speaks and acts for a place or a group.
Borrowed from English and invariable: un record, due record; un triste record = a sad record.
Latte scremato = skimmed milk, with the cream taken off.
Imperfect of spalmare, to spread butter or jam on bread; the imperfect tells a habit.
Feminine plural of spaventato, agreeing with le famiglie; in speech you also say avere paura.
Same form for masculine and feminine; plural terribili.
Plural of il politico (politician); i politici locali = the local politicians, the everyday word for the people who run a place.
Said millenovecentonovantatré; years take the article: nel 1993, nell'ottobre del 1993.
Trecento; intorno al 300 a.C. = around 300 BC.
The country; countries take the article except after in: in Cina, nella Cina centrale.
A city in Hubei, central China; the Guodian tomb was found near it.
An old Chinese book, named after the sage said to have written it; also called the Daodejing.
The other name of the Laozi, "the book of the way and its power".
Stressed on the last syllable, so it never changes in the plural.
Plural of ladro; un ladro = a thief.
Plural of archeologo, with -gi; people who dig up the past.
L' = il before a vowel; autore is who wrote a book, scrittore a writer by trade.
Capitolo, plural capitoli; il capitolo 64 = chapter 64.
Mezzo chilometro = half a kilometre; mezzo before a noun does not take un.
The first green tip a plant puts out; plural germogli.
No accent: la meta = the goal; metà with an accent means half.
In speech grosso often means big in size: un albero grosso = a big, thick tree.
Abbracciarlo = abbracciare + lo (it): the pronoun is joined to the infinitive.
italian.translation: to hug, to put your arms around

italian.note: Short for bicicletta, and what everyone says; it never changes in the plural: le bici.
A passo d'uomo = at walking pace; said of traffic that crawls.
italian.translation: of a man (in: a passo d'uomo)

italian.note: Imbottigliato (literally 'bottled up') = stuck in a traffic jam; masculine plural here.
Past participle of voltare, to turn; voltare pagina = to turn the page, to make a fresh start.
Masculine assurdo; in speech it often just means 'crazy, unthinkable'.
Come + era: com'era prevedibile = as you'd expect.
Superlative of male: malissimo = really badly.
From peggiorare, to get worse; the opposite is migliorare.
Imperfetto of ripetere: ripetevano = they kept repeating.
Reflexive muoversi: muoversi in bici = to get around by bike.
Parecchi clienti = quite a few customers; feminine parecchie.
Contro ogni previsione = against all expectations.
Ri- + dare: ridare spazio = to give space back.
Imperative of scusare (tu form): scusa = sorry; scusami = forgive me, said to someone close.
Da + l'altra: dall'altra parte = on the other side; often the noun is dropped.
From innaffiare, to water: tu li innaffi = you water them; li hai innaffiati = you watered them (agrees with li).
A long stick carried on the shoulders, with a pot at each end.
Tenere in equilibrio = to keep balanced.
Imperfect subjunctive of fare: per quanto facesse attenzione = however careful she was.
Un'esplosione di fiori = a burst of flowers; esplosione is feminine.
Past participle of seminare, to sow seeds (semi).
Accorgersi + ne: senza accorgertene = without noticing it. Te and ne are joined to the infinitive.
Past participle of colorare, to colour: hanno colorato il villaggio = they brought colour to the village.
Imperfetto of ostinarsi: ti ostinavi a chiamare = you kept on calling.
In- + aspettato: una cosa inaspettata = something unexpected.
Superlative of sano with -issimo: sanissimi = very healthy.
Contro ogni aspettativa = against all expectations; plural aspettative.
Lo/la + aspettava: non se l'aspettava = he did not expect it (aspettarsi, to expect).
Mettersi d'impegno = to put your mind to it, to really try.
Uno spicchio di cielo = a patch of sky; also a clove of garlic or a wedge of orange.
Di passaggio = passing by, just passing through.
A dispetto di = in spite of, despite.
Imperative of infilare, to slip something into: infila la teglia nel forno.
A essere sinceri = to be honest.
Imperative of sistemare + le: sistemale sulla teglia = arrange them on the tray.
In abbondanza = generously, plenty of it.
Rovinare = to ruin; può rovinarti il sonno = it can ruin your sleep (ti joined to the infinitive).
In speech attaccare means to start a shift: attacca alle quattro = he starts at four.
Non chiudere occhio = not to sleep a wink.
Imperfetto of buttarsi: si buttava sul caffè = he turned to coffee.
Imperfetto of dare, loro form: lo davano = they were giving it.
Non parla di teoria = he is not talking about theory.
Un accordo è una proporzione = a chord is a ratio (between notes).
The year Atlantic bluefin tuna was listed Endangered; said duemilaundici.
Past participle of allargare, to make larger (largo).
From deporre: depone le uova = it lays its eggs.
Copiare + li: the pronoun joins the end of the infinitive, so copiarli = to copy them.
Magari is the everyday spoken word for maybe; on its own it can also mean 'if only!'.
From scaricare, to unload or dump: i fiumi la scaricano nell'oceano = the rivers dump it into the ocean.
Giocare d'anticipo = to act before a problem arrives, literally to play ahead of time.
Dare fastidio a = to bother, to disturb: senza dare fastidio ai pesci = without bothering the fish.
Destinati a + infinitive = bound to: rifiuti destinati a finire in mare = rubbish that would end up in the sea.
Ri- + pulire: ripulire is to clean something up completely, to clear it.
From puntare: puntare su qualcosa = to bet on, to focus on something. Also the noun la punta = the tip, the point: "a punta" = pointed.
italian.translation: bets, aims (punta su); (la punta) tip, point; a punta = pointed

italian.note: A disposizione di tutti = available to everyone; mettere a disposizione = to make available.
Apertura alle sette = opening at seven; from aprire, to open.
Ingrandire (to enlarge, grow) + lo: ingrandirlo = to make it bigger. It comes from grande.
italian.translation: to make it bigger, to expand it

italian.note: Non avere più una briciola = to have not a crumb left.
Con le migliori intenzioni = with the best of intentions; singular intenzione.
Abbondare = to be plentiful, to overdo it: senza mai abbondare = without ever overdoing it.
Senza pietà = without mercy; nouns ending in -tà never change in the plural.
Fare compagnia a qualcuno = to keep someone company.
Parecchie conversazioni = quite a few conversations; parecchio agrees with its noun when it is an adjective.
Staccare gli occhi da = to take your eyes off: senza staccare gli occhi dallo schermo.
Una ventina di = about twenty; -ina after a number makes it approximate (una decina = about ten).
Soddisfatto di = pleased with: soddisfatto della sua metafora.
Il guaio è che… = the trouble is that…; plural guai.
Non avere la minima idea = not to have the faintest idea.
La minima idea = the slightest idea; masculine minimo.
Insomma sums up what came before: insomma, se mangi in fretta… = so basically, if you eat fast…
L'esatto contrario = the exact opposite; esatto drops the article's vowel: lo esatto becomes l'esatto.
Gerund of gustarsi, to enjoy something for yourself: gustandosi quello che aveva davanti.
Buco (hole) + -etto, which makes things small: un buchetto, dei buchetti.
Servirsi = to help yourself to food: perché tutti possano servirsi.
Com'è is come + è: così com'è = just as it is, and ecco com'è nato = that's how it was born (è + participle is the past).
Fare la scarpetta = to mop up the sauce with a piece of bread.
From sognare; nessuno si sogna di… = nobody would dream of…
Questa ora becomes quest'ora before a vowel.
Un invito a + infinitive = an invitation to do something.
Sbrigarsi is the everyday reflexive verb for hurrying up: sbrigati! = hurry up!
Rimandare (to postpone) + la: invece di rimandarla = instead of putting it off.
Una telefonata = a phone call; fare una telefonata = to make a call.
Mettere / lasciare a bagno = to leave to soak.
Litigare (to argue) + ci: litigarci sopra = to argue about it.
A spese sue = at his own expense; singular spesa.
Un tentativo, dei tentativi = attempts, tries; from tentare.
English word used in Italian, masculine: il weekend, nel weekend.
Il vitello is both the calf and its meat, veal.
La pancetta is cured pork belly, used in small cubes in sauces.
Uno addosso all'altro = one right up against the other, packed tight.
The everyday word for repairing a broken thing.
Essere all'altezza = to measure up, to be good enough (literally at the height).
A + l'altro; uno addosso all'altro = one against the other.
Anche + io, shortened before the vowel; anch'io voglio = I want it too.
Dopo anni di assenza = after years away.
Diminutive plural of bolla (bubble): the -ina ending makes it small.
Brutto + -ino: a bit ugly, said kindly or with a smile.
La cosa buffa è che… = the funny thing is that…
Il calcio is the game, and a kick is un calcio; in chemistry il calcio = calcium (fluoruro di calcio).
Past participle of capitare, with essere: le è capitato di guardare = she happened to look.
Imperfetto of confrontare, for something she did again and again.
Contendersi qualcosa = to fight over it, each trying to get it: contendersi la luce.
Plural of controllo; controlli costanti = constant checks.
Convincere + ti: convincerti a cominciare = getting yourself to start.
italian.translation: to get yourself to, to convince yourself

italian.note: Past participle of convocare; in sport, called up to the national team.
Diciamo (che)… brings in an example or softens a statement; diciamolo = let's be honest.
Past participle of eguagliare: un record che nessuno ha eguagliato = a record nobody has matched.
From fare: something you can actually do.
Lavori senza futuro = jobs with no future.
O giù di lì = or so, more or less (literally or down around there).
Glielo + ha: gliel'ha dato = gave it to them; gli and lo join into glielo.
Said of something big and threatening that hangs over you.
Lo + inizio, shortened before the vowel; the opposite is la fine.
Plural of lontano used as an adjective: erano stati lontani = they had stayed away.
The raised path for walking beside a street.
Meritare + te + lo: per meritartelo = to have earned it yourself; ti becomes te before lo.
Mettiamo (literally let's put) brings in an example, like English say.
Rimettere in ordine = to tidy up, to sort out.
The comparative of male (badly); crescere peggio = to grow worse.
Pezzo + -etto: a little piece, said warmly.
Preoccuparsi with ti: non preoccuparti = don't worry (negative tu imperative = non + infinitive).
A written report for work or school; it also means relationship.
Tu imperative of resistere: resisti alla tentazione = resist the temptation.
From richiamare: to call back, to draw in.
From ricrescere: ri- + crescere, to grow again.
Ri- + mettere; rimettere in ordine la casa = to tidy up the house.
Tu imperative of ripensare: ripensa a… = think back to…
Non è una sciocchezza = it's no small thing, it's not silly.
Uscirne sconfitto = to come out of it beaten, to lose.
To break into pieces: spezzare un compito = to break a task down.
Masculine despite the -a: il tema. At school, un tema is a written essay.
Present of tenere, io form; tenerci a qualcosa = to care about it: ci tengo al lavoro fatto bene.
italian.translation: I hold; ci tengo = I care

italian.note: Past participle of sognare: ho sempre sognato dei lamponi = I've always dreamed of raspberries.
Resistere alla tentazione = to resist the temptation.
Da + l'Olanda; dall'Olanda all'India = from the Netherlands to India.
What Italians usually say for the Netherlands (officially i Paesi Bassi).
Gli anni Settanta = the seventies; decades are written with a capital letter.
Muto is for a person or thing that makes no sound at all: un mare muto = a silent sea.
Imperfetto of mancare: mancava da un secolo = it had been missing for a century.
Certe (feminine plural of certo) before a noun means 'some, certain': in certe popolazioni = in some populations.
Words ending in stressed -tà are feminine and never change in the plural: la velocità, le velocità.
Feminine of straordinario; a dir poco straordinaria = extraordinary, to say the least.
Concentrata (feminine) = focused, concentrating: era molto più concentrata.
D'altri tempi = from another age, old-fashioned; d' is di before a vowel.
D'istinto = instinctively, without thinking it through; d' is di before a vowel.
Una fissazione is an idea someone can't let go of; used lightly in speech, like 'a thing of hers'.
Sommersa dagli impegni = swamped with commitments; literally 'submerged'.
Imperfetto of spaventare: la spaventava = it scared her.
Compagni (di scuola, di corso) = classmates; the singular is compagno.
Essere d'accordo con = to agree with; on its own, d'accordo = fine, granted.
Nell'Ottocento = in the 1800s; Italian names centuries after their hundreds, with a capital letter.
Present of viaggiare, lei form: viaggia pochissimo = she hardly travels.
Sottovoce (literally 'under the voice') = in a low voice.
Fare chiasso = to make a racket; a lively, everyday word for noise.
Participle of posarsi used as an adjective: posata = perched (said of the bird, la speranza).
Si è sistemato = it has settled in, made itself at home.
-issima means 'very': una vela altissima = a very tall sail.
Past participle of calcolare: l'ha calcolato Ember = Ember worked it out.
Di + l' before a vowel: dell'aprile 2025 = than April 2025, of April 2025.
Ragazza covers a girl and a young woman; the masculine is ragazzo.
Smuovere + lo: to budge it, move something stuck.
Farsi + li (them): farseli raschiare = to have them scraped.
-issimo means 'very': ha piovuto tantissimo = it rained a lot.
Feminine participle of vincere, agreeing with la (the race): l'ha vinta Verstappen.
Comandare il campionato = to lead the championship.
Participle of costringere: ha costretto la Formula 1 ad aspettare = forced Formula 1 to wait.
Fare a turno = to take turns.
Antico + the suffix -issimo = very old; the c becomes ch to keep the hard sound.
Dire + le (them, feminine plural): the pronoun attaches to the end of the infinitive.
Custodire is to guard something precious with care: un sapere da custodire.
italian.translation: to look after, to keep safe

italian.note: Tenere d'occhio = to keep an eye on; d' is di before a vowel.
Sport has the same form in the plural; fare sport = to exercise.
Reflexive ripetersi = to say again and again to yourself; ripetendosi is its gerund.
Imperfetto of stressare: il lavoro non lo stressava più = work no longer stressed him out.
Literally 'nailed': inchiodato alla scrivania = stuck at the desk all day.
Past participle of suggerire: gli ha suggerito = suggested to him.
Smaltire is to get rid of something bit by bit: smaltire lo zucchero di un pasto = to process the sugar from a meal.
All'istante = right away, this very moment; more spoken than immediatamente.
Adverb from onesto with -mente: più onestamente vera = more honestly true.
Nessuna before a feminine noun starting with a vowel becomes nessun': nessun'altra foresta.
Present of ospitare: ospita animali e piante = it is home to animals and plants.
Tu imperative of friggere, the same as the present: friggi l'aglio = fry the garlic.
Non rubare = don't steal: non + infinitive is the negative imperative for tu.
Passato prossimo of rimandare (ri- = back, again): l'ha rimandato = he sent him back.
Past participle of spedire: ha spedito = he sent off (by post, train or truck).
Imperfetto of sperare: che sperava di risparmiare = who was hoping to save.
Il discorso is a talk, but also the whole line of an argument: tutto il discorso si riduce a = it all comes down to.
Un lusso = a luxury; di lusso = luxurious.
Appunto stresses that this is exactly the point: appunto perché = precisely because.
18; meno diciotto gradi = minus eighteen degrees.
Plural of il grado: a meno diciotto gradi = at minus eighteen degrees.
Gli si è accesa la lampadina = the light bulb came on for him: it finally dawned on him.
Imperfect subjunctive of mancare after se: se mancasse la corrente = if the power went off.
Feminine of sostanzioso: a meal that keeps you full.
Nouns ending in stressed -tà are feminine and never change in the plural: la felicità, le città.
Prendere una brutta piega = to take a turn for the worse, said of a day, a situation or a conversation.
Capo (head) + treno: the person in charge on a train; the plural is i capotreno.
Months are lowercase in Italian: nel novembre 2022 = in November 2022.
From accendere, to light: accende un fuoco = she lights a fire; the past participle is acceso.
Perdersi d'animo = to lose heart; non si è persa d'animo = she did not lose heart.
The ending -issimo makes a superlative: gentile = kind, gentilissimo = very kind.
Un'aria sospettosa = a wary look; masculine sospettoso.
Con una certa solennità = with a certain ceremony; nouns in -tà never change in the plural.
Di corsa = in a rush, at a run: è tornata di corsa = she hurried back.
Conditional of venire; of a dish, verrebbe meglio = it would turn out better.
From mancare: mancano dieci minuti all'esame = there are ten minutes to go before the exam.
From respirare: respira is both the tu imperative (breathe!) and he/she breathes.
From agitato, agitated: le mani agitate = restless, shaking hands.
Con + il: col mare grosso = in rough seas; spoken Italian uses col more than con il.
From espirare, to breathe out: l'espirazione lunga = the long out-breath.
From aggrapparsi a, to cling to: le cose a cui ci aggrappiamo = the things we cling to.
Essere in ansia = to be anxious, worried.
Spoken synonym of ovunque: lo trovi dappertutto = you find it everywhere.
Fixed phrase: il cuore batteva all'impazzata = her heart was pounding like mad.
In modo misurabile = measurably, in a way you can measure.
Spoken emphasis after a statement: Jo la paura ce l'ha eccome = Jo is afraid all right.
Fare finta che / di = to pretend: non fa finta che = she does not pretend that.
In + l' + assenza: non nell'assenza di paura = not in the absence of fear.
L' + acidità; nouns in -tà keep the same form in the plural.
Imperfetto of aggiustare; aggiustare di sale e pepe = to season with salt and pepper; l'aggiustava = he seasoned it.
In cooking, far appassire la cipolla = to cook the onion gently until soft.
Short for pomodori pelati, the tinned peeled tomatoes of every Italian kitchen.
Ci teneva a precisare = he made a point of saying it.
Liscia come la seta = smooth as silk.
Le stesse identiche parole = the very same words; identico, identica.
Man mano che = as, little by little: man mano che le sere si facevano più fredde.
Fare l'impiegato = to work as a clerk (Italian uses fare + article for a job).
Neanche una dimostrazione = not even one proof; a spoken synonym of nemmeno.
A spoken connector that adds a reason everyone can see: d'altronde era felice solo tra i numeri.
Col cuore in gola = with his heart in his mouth, very anxious.
From sbagliare; non sbaglia un colpo = it does not miss a beat.
Chiudere il conto = to put the game beyond doubt; il conto also means the bill.
A pari merito = level, tied on points.
Spuntarla = to win narrowly in the end; the la stays: l'ha spuntata = he pulled it off.
Su + l' + Ipswich: 3–2 sull'Ipswich Town = 3–2 against Ipswich Town.
Spoken link to another thread of the story: il Barcelona, intanto, = meanwhile Barcelona.
Amy March, the youngest of the four sisters in Little Women.
The year the second part of Little Women came out.
Present of amare for lui/lei: la gente ama le sue parole = people love her words.
Present of ammettere; ammette di non sapere = she admits she doesn't know.
Present of chiacchierare: to chat, to talk in a relaxed, friendly way.
Future of durare: non durerà = it won't last; quanto durerà = how long it will last.
Present of maturare; said of a person it means to grow up: poi matura molto.
Il meteo is the everyday word for the weather and the forecast; it does not change in the plural.
Feminine of sposato; sposata da poco = newly married.
Feminine of vanitoso: too proud of yourself or your looks.
Feminine of viziato: a child who has been given everything she wants.
Infinitive of digerire, an -ire verb with -isc- in the present: digerisco, digerisce.
La pubblicità is both one ad and advertising in general; the accent never changes in the plural: le pubblicità.
The year of the oldest known version of the line: an unsigned bank advertisement.
Read "zero virgola centosettantanove"; Italian writes a comma where English has a decimal point: con 0,179 secondi su Verstappen = 0.179 seconds faster than Verstappen.
Read "tredici virgola zero settantotto"; Italian writes a comma where English has a decimal point: a 13,078 secondi da Antonelli = 13.078 seconds behind Antonelli.
Read "centoventitré": 123 punti di vantaggio = 123 points ahead, Antonelli's lead in the championship.
Read "millenovecentocinquantatré"; a year after nel: nel 1953 = in 1953, the year of Alberto Ascari's second title.
First name of Alberto Ascari, the Italian driver who was Formula 1 world champion in 1952 and 1953.
Alberto Ascari, Formula 1 world champion in 1952 and 1953; dai tempi di Ascari = since Ascari's day, the last Italian champion.
English name kept in Italian: il Circuit of the Americas is the race track in Austin, Texas.
Part of the English name of the track in Austin, Texas: il Circuit of the Americas.
italian.translation: the Americas (in: Circuit of the Americas)

italian.note: The US state where Austin is; in Texas = in Texas, with no article after in.
Il Messico is the country; Città del Messico = Mexico City, where the next race is: a Città del Messico = in Mexico City.
Italiano/italiana/italiani/italiane, with a small i: è italiano = he is Italian; il primo italiano = the first Italian (champion).
The ordinal of otto: arriva ottavo = he finishes eighth; ottavo e quarto = eighth and fourth.
English term kept in Italian: il pit stop, plural i pit stop (no -s), is the stop in the pits to change tyres.
English term kept in Italian: un solo pit stop = just one pit stop; the plural stays i pit stop.
The Italian word for a pit stop: una sola sosta = just one stop; plural soste.
La gomma, plural le gomme: the tyres of a car; dalle gomme medie alle dure = from medium to hard tyres.
Feminine plural of medio, agreeing with gomme: le gomme medie = the medium tyres, the middle of the three dry compounds.
Feminine plural of duro, agreeing with gomme: le dure = the hard tyres, the ones that last longest.
A very short time, the everyday word for it: un attimo = a moment; aspetta un attimo = wait a moment.
Tranne un attimo = apart from a moment; it leaves something out of what the rest of the sentence says.
One stop on a journey or one race of a season: prossima tappa = next stop, said of the next race.
Imperfect of bastare: non bastava vincere = winning was not enough.
Conditional of bastare: gli basterebbe il nono posto = ninth place would be enough for him.
Past participle of approfittare; ne ha approfittato = he took advantage of it (ne = of it).
Passare + lo (him) joined at the end of the infinitive: per passarlo = to get past him, to overtake him.
Past participle of ripassare, to pass again (ri- = again): l'ha ripassato = he got past him again.
Imperfect subjunctive of arrivare, needed after a past "serviva che": gli serviva che Russell arrivasse nono = he needed Russell to finish ninth.
Millenovecentoquarantasette, the year of the Partition of India; years take the article: nel 1947 = in 1947.
Duemilaventiquattro; nel 2024 = in 2024, and with a month nel gennaio 2024 = in January 2024.
Cinquanta; 50 g di burro = cinquanta grammi di burro, with di between the amount and the food.
Seicento, written as one word; 600 g = seicento grammi.
The first name the two cooks of this story shared: Kundan Lal Gujral and his cousin Kundan Lal Jaggi, who left Peshawar for Delhi in 1947.
Kundan Lal Gujral, one of the founders of Moti Mahal; family names do not change in the plural: i Gujral = the Gujral family.
Kundan Lal Jaggi, cousin of Kundan Lal Gujral and co-founder of Moti Mahal; like every family name it stays the same in the plural: i Jaggi.
Moti is Hindi and Urdu for pearl: il Moti Mahal, the Pearl Palace, the restaurant the two Kundan Lals opened in Old Delhi; it is masculine, like ristorante.
Mahal = palace in Urdu and Hindi: lo Shish Mahal (Glasgow), il Moti Mahal (Delhi).
A city in the north-west of today's Pakistan; until 1947 it was part of British India.
The capital region of India, where the two cooks started over in 1947; its High Court is l'Alta Corte di Delhi.
La Partizione is the division of British India into India and Pakistan in 1947, when millions of people had to leave their homes.
Il pollo, the bird and the meat; cosce di pollo = chicken thighs.
Plural of coscia (thigh): cosce di pollo = chicken thighs; -cia loses its i in the plural.
La salsa: any sauce; a thick tomato sauce is also la salsa di pomodoro.
Plural of spezia (spice), almost always used in the plural.
Lo zenzero: lo because the word starts with z.
Abbreviation of millilitri: 100 ml di panna = 100 millilitres of cream.
English word kept in dish names: chicken tikka masala, butter chicken; in Italian the dish is masculine (il chicken tikka masala, il butter chicken).
Tu imperative of unire (unisco, unisci…): in recipes it means to add one thing to another.
Present of bruciacchiarsi, from bruciare + -acchiare (a little, here and there): si bruciacchiano ai bordi = they char at the edges.
English word kept in the dish's name: il butter chicken, which Italians also call pollo al burro (il burro = butter).
Said of food cooked in a tandoor, the clay oven of North India and Pakistan; it never changes: il pollo tandoori.
A tall clay oven heated with charcoal or wood, used in North India and Pakistan; Italian keeps the word: il tandoor.
Literally cooked earth (terra cotta): un forno di terracotta = a clay oven; argilla is the raw clay.
A very hot oven for bricks, glass or metal; caldo come una fornace = as hot as a furnace, also said of a hot room in summer.
Gli avanzi, from avanzare (to be left over): the food left after a meal; niente male, per degli avanzi = not bad for leftovers.
Il cugino, la cugina; with a possessive and no other word it takes no article: suo cugino = his cousin.
Andare in tribunale = to go to court; finire in tribunale = to end up in court, the everyday words for a legal fight.
La corte is a court in official names: l'Alta Corte di Delhi = the Delhi High Court; in everyday talk a court is il tribunale.
Masculine plural of nero, agreeing with i bordi: finché i bordi non diventano neri = until the edges go black.
In- (not) + venduto (sold), masculine plural: i pezzi invenduti = the pieces nobody bought.
Imperfect of seccarsi (loro), for what kept happening: si seccavano = they dried out, got dry.
