Past participle of ricominciare (ri- again + cominciare); ricominciare da zero = to start over from nothing.
A spoken word for surprise or emphasis: i Gujral addirittura già a Peshawar = the Gujrals even say it was back in Peshawar.
La perla, plural le perle: il Palazzo della Perla = the Pearl Palace, which is what Moti Mahal means.
Nero agrees with what it describes, here il pollo (masculine singular): finché non diventa un po' nero = until it goes a bit black; plural neri, feminine nera.
The Italian name for Beijing, the capital of China, home of Shiqian Ding's team; «a Pechino» = in Beijing (a before a city).
L'atomo, the tiny building block of everything; «il cuore di un atomo» = the heart of an atom.
Di + l'atomo, joined with an apostrophe before the vowel: «il cuore dell'atomo» = the heart of the atom.
Il laser, the same in the plural; «la luce laser» = laser light, where laser does not change like an adjective.
Illuminare (to light up): illumina is the present, illuminava the imperfect for the background: «un laser lo illuminava» = a laser was shining on it.
Correggere (to correct): corregge is the present, correggeva the imperfect, for each time it happened: «lo correggeva da solo» = it fixed it by itself.
Read «duemilatré»; a year takes the article: «del 2003» = from 2003, «nel 2003» = in 2003.
Il GPS, said letter by letter «gi-pi-esse»: the satellite system that tells your phone or car where it is.
Read «sette»; dates use the plain number with il: «il 7 ottobre» = on 7 October (but «il primo» for the 1st).
First name of Thorsten Schumm, the physicist who leads the nuclear clock team at TU Wien, the technical university of Vienna.
Thorsten Schumm, Austrian physicist at TU Wien, whose team ran a nuclear clock on its own in 2026.
First name of Shiqian Ding, the physicist who leads the nuclear clock team at Tsinghua University in Beijing.
Shiqian Ding, Chinese physicist at Tsinghua University in Beijing; in Chinese the family name, Ding, comes first.
From il nucleo of an atom; «un orologio nucleare» = a clock that listens to the nucleus, nothing to do with nuclear power.
Il dondolio, from dondolare (to swing, to rock): «il dondolio di un pendolo» = the swing of a pendulum.
Il pendolo, the weight that swings to and fro in an old clock.
From l'atomo; «un orologio atomico» counts the jumps of electrons, the most exact clocks before nuclear ones.
Plural of il salto, from saltare (to jump): «i salti degli elettroni» = the jumps of the electrons.
Plural of l'elettrone, the tiny particles that move around the nucleus of an atom.
Il nucleo, the centre of an atom, its tiny heart; also the core of anything.
Contento (feminine contenta): glad about something that happened; «il gruppo era proprio contento» = the team was really glad.
La rivista, a magazine or a scientific journal: «sulla rivista Nature» = in the journal Nature (Italian says su, on).
The English name of a famous science journal, kept as it is: «la rivista Nature».
From separato + -mente: «hanno lavorato separatamente» = they worked separately, each on its own.
Il tic-tac, the sound of a clock: «il tic-tac degli elettroni» = the ticks of the electrons; it never changes in the plural.
Il torio is thorium; torio-229 (read «torio duecentoventinove») is the kind whose nucleus a laser can nudge, the heart of the new clocks.
Il cristallo, a clear solid whose atoms sit in neat rows, here holding the thorium; it also means fine glass.
Assorbire, lui/lei form: «il torio assorbe la luce laser» = the thorium takes in laser light.
Read «trenta»: «30 milioni di anni» = 30 million years, with di after milioni.
Plural of il fisico (physicist), with -ci; la fisica is both physics and a woman physicist.
Read «diecimila»: Italian groups thousands with a dot, not a comma: «10.000 volte» = 10,000 times.
Il fluoruro; «fluoruro di calcio» = calcium fluoride (here calcio is the element calcium, not football).
Lo + errore, shortened before the vowel: how far off a measure is; «l'errore?» = how far off?
First name of Ekkehard Peik, German physicist in Braunschweig, who wrote down the idea of a nuclear clock in 2003.
Ekkehard Peik, German physicist who proposed the thorium nuclear clock with Christian Tamm in 2003.
First name of Christian Tamm, the German physicist who proposed the nuclear clock with Ekkehard Peik in 2003.
Christian Tamm, German physicist, co-author of the 2003 nuclear clock idea with Ekkehard Peik.
Plural of il capo (head; end); «ai due capi del mondo» = at the two ends of the world, far apart.
A year, said as one number: millenovecentosessantasei; the first issue came out in March 1966.
L'ovest; «la Germania Ovest» = West Germany, the country from 1949 to 1990.
German for foundation; Italian keeps the German name: «la Stiftung Warentest», a foundation in Berlin that tests products.
German Waren (goods) + Test: the second half of the name «Stiftung Warentest», which Italian does not translate.
Infinitive; «una macchina da cucire» = a sewing machine: da + infinitive says what a machine is for.
Plural of il frullatore, the kitchen machine that blends or whisks food.
Read «centomila»: Italian groups thousands with a dot, not a comma.
Il prezzo, plural i prezzi; «il prezzo al chilo» = the price per kilo.
L'euro never changes in the plural: «2 euro», «4 euro al chilo» = 4 euros a kilo.
Italian writes a decimal comma: «3,50» is read «tre e cinquanta» (three fifty), short for 3,50 euro.
Feminine plural of europeo; «le regole europee» = the EU rules, the law all EU countries share.
Past participle of lanciare (to throw, to launch): «ha lanciato una nuova rivista» = it started a new magazine.
Plural of l'abbonato, someone who pays to get every issue of a magazine.
A year, said as one number: millenovecentosessantotto.
L'edicola, the kiosk that sells newspapers and magazines; «in edicola» = at the newsstand.
La fondazione, an organisation set up with money for a lasting purpose, here to test products.
La spesa; «fare la spesa» = to do the shopping, to buy food and everyday things.
Read «duecentodiecimila»: Italian groups thousands with a dot.
Caro means expensive (and dear, of a person): «sembra più caro» = it looks dearer.
Obbligare, loro form: «obbligare qualcuno a + infinitive» = to make someone do something, by law.
A year, said as one number: millenovecentosessantaquattro; when the foundation was set up.
«Con metodo scientifico» = with a scientific method, scientifically.
Plural of il prodotto (noun), a thing made to be sold: «prodotti dello stesso tipo» = products of the same kind.
Plural of la merce, the things shops sell: «provare le merci» = to test goods.
Infinitive; «gettare la spugna» = to throw in the towel, to give up.
Past participle of volere in «ci vuole» (it takes): «ci è voluta pazienza» = it took patience; it agrees with pazienza.
Su + l'etichetta: «sull'etichetta dello scaffale» = on the shelf label.
Lo scaffale, plural gli scaffali: the shelves in a shop; «scaffali interi» = whole shelves.
I tester, the people who test products; an English word that does not change in the plural.
Duemilacinque; nel 2005 = in 2005, and with a month nell'ottobre 2005 = in October 2005.
Duecentottanta: the 280 mothers and the 280 fathers in the Naples study.
Novantuno; «il 91 per cento» = 91 percent, with the article il before the number.
Quattro virgola cinque: Italian writes a comma where English writes a decimal point.
Part of the name Alfredo Pisacane, the children's doctor in Naples whose father study came out in 2005.
Part of the name Alfredo Pisacane, the children's doctor in Naples whose father study came out in 2005.
Il pediatra (a woman: la pediatra), the doctor who looks after children; it ends in -a but takes il here.
L'allattamento, from allattare (to breastfeed): feeding a baby at the breast.
Di + l'allattamento: «i problemi dell'allattamento» = breastfeeding problems.
Su + l'allattamento: «un corso sull'allattamento» = a breastfeeding class; su here means about.
A + l'allattamento: «cosa succede all'allattamento» = what happens to breastfeeding.
Allattare = to feed a baby at the breast; allatta (she feeds) is the present, allattava the imperfect, for a state that was still going on.
«Latte materno» = breast milk, literally mother's milk; the feminine is materna.
«Allattare in modo esclusivo» = to give only breast milk, nothing else.
In + l'altro: «nell'altro gruppo» = in the other group; alone, nell'altro means in the other one.
Past participle of andare, masculine plural: with essere it agrees with the subject, «i papà sono andati».
Past participle of aiutare, feminine: «l'aveva aiutata» agrees with l' (her, the mother).
Tu imperative of portare + le (to her), joined into one word: «portale un tè» = bring her a cup of tea.
Tu imperative di' (from dire) + le: the l doubles when the pronoun joins, di' + le = dille.
Tu imperative fa' (from fare) + le, with the l doubled: «falle i complimenti» = praise her, pay her compliments.
Tu imperative chiedi (from chiedere) + le (to her): «chiedile cosa serve a lei» = ask her what she needs.
Tu imperative of occuparsi, with the reflexive ti joined: «occupati tu di» = you take on, you handle.
Plural of il complimento; «fare i complimenti a qualcuno» = to praise someone, to tell them they're doing well.
Plural of il bagnetto, the small bath for a baby; the -etto ending makes it small and affectionate.
Plural of il pannolino; «cambiare i pannolini» = to change nappies.
Il sostegno, from sostenere (to hold up): help that keeps someone going.
L'incontro, a meeting or a session where people get together; from incontrare, to meet.
Imperfect of insegnare (lui/lei form), for what the class covered in general.
Plural of comune: «i problemi comuni» = the common problems; the same form for masculine and feminine.
Plural of frequente: «i problemi più frequenti» = the commonest problems.
Affrontare + li (them, the problems): the pronoun joins the infinitive; «come affrontarli» = how to handle them.
italian.translation: to deal with them, face them

italian.note: Masculine of universitaria: «l'ospedale universitario» = the university hospital.
A + l'ospedale: «all'ospedale universitario» = at the university hospital.
A + l'uomo: «insegnava all'uomo» = it taught the man; insegnare takes a before the person.
Millesettecentocinquantanove, the year Voltaire bought Ferney; nel febbraio 1759 = in February 1759.
Millesettecentottanta; nel 1780 = in 1780, with the article as for every year.
Milleottocentosettantotto, the year the name Ferney-Voltaire became official.
Voltaire (1694–1778), the French writer of Candide, who lived at Ferney from 1759.
Voltaire's short novel of 1759 and its hero; the title stays in French in Italian too.
A village on the French side of the border near Geneva, where Voltaire bought a castle in 1759.
Today's name of Ferney, official since 1878: the town took the name of the writer who built it up.
French title for a married woman, kept as it is before a French name: Madame Denis.
Marie-Louise Denis, Voltaire's niece; on paper the castle at Ferney was hers.
Months are written with a small letter in Italian: nel febbraio 1759 = in February 1759.
Il castello: in Italian any big old country house of a lord, like Voltaire's château at Ferney.
La fattoria, a farm with its house and land; una piccola fattoria = a small farm.
Il piccolo angolo: the suffix -ino makes it small and friendly; il tuo angolino = your own little corner.
La fontana, the public fountain in the village square where people fetched water.
From la palude (swamp); un terreno paludoso = swampy land.
Plural of il disastro; una vita di disastri = a lifetime of disasters.
La noia, the feeling of having nothing to do; also «che noia!» = how boring!
Il vizio, a bad habit or moral fault; the opposite of la virtù.
Feminine plural of lastricato, from la lastra (stone slab): strade lastricate = paved streets.
Il/la protagonista: the same form for a man or a woman, only the article changes.
Plural of il male (an evil, a harm); tre grandi mali = three great evils.
Tagliare + si; tagliarsi fuori dal mondo = to cut yourself off from the world.
Past participle of bonificare: to drain swampy land and make it good for farming.
Plural of la palude; bonificare le paludi = to drain the swamps.
Cento + anni, with the final o dropped before a vowel in speech: cent'anni dopo = a hundred years later.
The same form for masculine and feminine: il nome è diventato ufficiale = the name became official.
Past participle of risanare: ha risanato le paludi = he cleaned up the swamps, made the land healthy.

spanish.note: Read "ciento cincuenta": más de 150 años = over 150 years (since Little Women was published), 150 g de yogur = 150 grams of yoghurt.
The year Little Women was first published.
"Al" is a contraction of a + el.
Past participle of abrir, used as an adjective.
From acostarse (to go to bed). "Acuéstate" is a command ("go to bed!").
The liquid — takes "el" for pronunciation reasons despite being feminine.
As in "antes de que los alcance la nieve" (before the snow catches them).
As in "alrededor de la manzana" (around the block).
Forms of antiguo (old, ancient): antigua, antiguas (feminine), antiguos (masculine plural).
Forms of aprender across persons and tenses.
Fine grains, like at a beach.
As in "se quedan atrás" (they stay behind).
The state of being absent — here, the absence of fear.
"Ayuda" is the noun, "ayudar" the infinitive verb.
From añadir (to add): añade = adds, añadió = added (indefinido), añadía = was adding, añadido = added (participle); in a recipe añade is the tú command: añade la nata = add the cream.
spanish.translation: adds, added, was adding; add! (tú command)

spanish.note: As in Jo March's famous line about sailing her ship.
A very common adverb of manner.
"Buen" is used before a masculine singular noun, "buena" is feminine.
Same form for masculine and feminine.
A savory liquid used as a soup base.
Same form for masculine and feminine.
A group of traders traveling together, as in the old saying.
Past participle of cargar, used as an adjective.
Where you keep money and cards.
As in a squeeze of lemon.
As in "cientos de ríos" (hundreds of rivers).
A group of students, or the room.
Same form for masculine and feminine.
General word for food; also a meal: "la primera comida del año" = the first meal of the year.
"Compartir" infinitive, "comparten" ellos form, "compartían" ellos imperfect: hasta compartían nombre = they even shared a name.
One of the most common Spanish prepositions.
Past participle of conocer, used as an adjective.
The organ, and figuratively the "heart" of a sentence's meaning.
Where the caravan begins its journey.
As in "una vieja costumbre" (an old habit).
Infinitive — as in not harming the fish.
"Del" is a contraction of de + el.
From dejar (to leave); dejar de + infinitive = to stop doing: deja de preocuparte = stop worrying.
spanish.translation: leaves, was leaving, leaving; (dejar de + infinitive) stops, stop!

spanish.note: As in "todo lo demás" (all the rest).

spanish.translation: to give back / you gave back

spanish.note: Dividir (to divide): divide is the tú command form (divide la tarea grande = divide the big task), and dividieron the ellos pretérito, often standing in for a passive (cuando dividieron la India = when India was divided).
Forms of dudar across persons and tenses.
Used to ask about a place.
Variant of "y" (and), used before words starting with "i" sound.
Definite article for singular masculine nouns.
A worker — here, a train employee.
One of the most common Spanish prepositions.
Encontrar (to find), "él/ella" form. "Se encuentra" = is (somewhere); "se encuentra con" = meets, comes across.
spanish.translation: finds; (se encuentra) is; (se encuentra con) meets

spanish.note: As in physical energy or solar energy.
Introduces a result or next step.
Describes something located between two things.
Demonstrative pronouns/adjectives, gender- and number-inflected; eso sí, set off by commas, means mind you or that said.
spanish.translation: that, those; eso sí = mind you

spanish.note: "Esta" is the feminine demonstrative "this"; "esté" is subjunctive of estar.
Forms of estar, used for temporary states/locations, as opposed to ser.
Refers to someone or something from the United States.
Masculine demonstrative "this" (este año); as a noun, el este = the east (en el este de Finlandia).
"Estudian" is a verb form; "estudiante(s)" the noun.
As in "no hace falta" (it isn't necessary).
A glass container — here, the jar of stones.
A written or spoken sentence — here, a famous line.
Frente a = facing, or compared with: 25 por ciento frente al 15 = 25 percent against 15; ponerse al frente de algo = to take charge of it.
spanish.translation: front, facing; (frente a) against, compared with; (al frente de) in charge of

spanish.note: As in "a la luz del fuego" (by firelight); in a recipe, a fuego lento = over a low heat.
Same form for masculine and feminine.
Same form for masculine and feminine.
Grammatically singular even though it means "people."
"Gran" is used before a singular noun, "grandes" is plural.

Forms of hacer across tenses (hace, hacía, hiciera); "hace una semana" = a week ago, "hace falta" = it is needed. "Hacia" without an accent is another word: toward, or around a date (hacia el año 300).
spanish.translation: to do, make; (hace + time) ago; (hacia) toward, around

spanish.note: Marks an endpoint in time or space (hasta 1952); before a noun or verb it also means "even" (hasta un niño puede…).
Past participle of hacer, used as an adjective. For bread, "bien hecha" = well baked, with a darker crust.
spanish.translation: made; (bien hecha) well done, well baked

Plural of capa; "dos capas de barniz" = two coats of varnish.
Spanish uses no article with a profession: "es carpintero" = he is a carpenter.
The family name of Ole Kirk Christiansen, the Danish carpenter of this story.
A thin rope; "con una cuerda" = on (with) a string.
Danés (masculine), danesa (feminine); "en danés" = in Danish, the language. Nationalities take no capital letter in Spanish.
Pretérito indefinido of despachar: to send goods on their way.
The country in northern Europe; its adjective is danés.
A business; "su empresa" = his company. Plural: empresas.
Encargar is to order something to be made: "encargó" is pretérito indefinido, "encargaba" the imperfect for the background.
Here the railway station; estación also means season of the year.
Ole's son, who varnished every duck again that night.
Past participle of incendiarse: "se había incendiado" = had caught fire, had burned down.
Infinitive; jugar is for games and toys, while tocar is to play an instrument.
From jugar (to play); "juguetes de madera" = wooden toys.
The middle name of Ole Kirk Christiansen.
A block for building; here the plastic brick of the toy company.
The name Ole gave his company in 1934, from the Danish for "play well".
Masculine although it ends in -a: el lema.
Pretérito indefinido of mandar: to send, to tell someone to do something, and with an infinitive to have something done (mandó sacar = had it taken out).
Months are not capitalised in Spanish: "el 11 de marzo".
Ole Kirk Christiansen, the Danish carpenter who made wooden toys; not the Spanish cheer "olé".
The masculine plural of padre (father) means mother and father together.
A quantity of goods sent together; partida can also be a game (of chess, of cards).
Past participle of patentar; "fue patentado" = was patented, the passive with ser.
Un pato de madera = a wooden duck; plural patos.
Pretérito indefinido of reconstruir (re- + construir); the i becomes y between vowels, as in construyó.
Plural of yoyó: one word in Spanish, with the accent on the last o.
The year the English doctor Lucy Wills came to Bombay.
The year Lucy Wills published what she had found.
The year the substance was found in spinach and named folic acid.
Cuatrocientos: "400 microgramos" = 400 micrograms, the amount for each day in this story.
Past participle of aislar, feminine to agree with "sustancia": fue aislada = it was isolated, separated from the plant.
An illness of the blood that leaves a person pale and very tired; the adjective is anémico.
Feminine plural of anémico: ill with anaemia. The accent marks the stress: a-NÉ-mi-cas.
Used almost only in the medical name "espina bífida" = spina bifida.
The city in India where Lucy Wills arrived in 1928; this was the city's name at the time.
Short for "columna vertebral", the line of bones down the back; the word also means a column.
Pretérito indefinido of comprobar, to check something and find it true: "según comprobó" = as she found.
The moment a pregnancy begins: "antes de la concepción" = before becoming pregnant.
A soft food to spread on bread, as in "crema de cacahuete" (peanut butter): "crema de levadura" = yeast spread. It also means cream.
Same form for masculine and feminine; "una dieta deficiente" lacks something the body needs.
Everything a person or an animal usually eats, not only a plan to lose weight.
The amount of a medicine or vitamin taken at one time; the plural is the same: una dosis, dos dosis.
A false friend: it never means "embarrassed". Used with estar: está embarazada = she is pregnant.
The months in which a woman carries a baby; from the same family as embarazada.
Pretérito indefinido of enfermar (ellos/ellas); "enfermar de anemia" = to fall ill with anaemia.
Here in the medical name "espina bífida" = spina bifida; in everyday Spanish an espina is a thorn or a fish bone.
A dark green leaf vegetable; Spanish often uses the plural: comer espinacas.
Masculine plural of este: estos defectos = these defects.
Present of formar (ellos/ellas); with se it describes something that happens by itself: se forman = they form.
Plural of fábrica, a building where many people make things with machines; not "fabric", which is tela.
Only used in "ácido fólico" = folic acid, the vitamin of this story; the name comes from the Latin word for leaf.
Something found after looking or studying; from hallar = to find.
The green part of a plant; "hoja" is also a sheet of paper.
Infinitive after "para": para investigar = in order to investigate.
Feminine of latino: "la palabra latina" = the word in Latin.
Lucy Wills, the English doctor of this story, who came to Bombay in 1928.
Pretérito indefinido of mejorar (ellos/ellas): las mujeres mejoraron = the women got better.
Plural of microgramo, a very small unit of weight: one millionth of a gram.
"El tubo neural" = the neural tube, the early form of the baby's brain and spine.
Feminine plural of obrero, a person who works with their hands, often in a factory.
People in a doctor's care; el paciente / la paciente has one form for both genders. As an adjective, paciente means calm and willing to wait.
Pretérito indefinido of proteger; a living being takes "a": protegió a los animales.
Feminine plural of pálido: with little colour in the face.
Plural of rata; the word is always feminine, whatever the animal's sex.
Present of reducir (él/ella): "reduce el riesgo" = it lowers the risk, it makes the risk smaller.
Present subjunctive of saber, needed after "antes de que": antes de que sepa = before she knows.
Forms of sospechar; with "de" it names what you think is the cause: sospechar de la comida = to suspect the food.
A kind of matter; here the thing in the yeast that had no name yet.
A pot with a wide mouth, usually of glass, for jam, honey or a spread.
Plural of textil, about making cloth: fábricas textiles = textile factories.
A long hollow shape: "el tubo neural" = the neural tube.
A substance in food that the body needs in small amounts; close to the English word, and feminine.
The family name of Lucy Wills; the "factor de Wills" (Wills factor) carried her name until 1941.
The year of the war in this story: "el año 261 antes de Cristo" = the year 261 BC (doscientos sesenta y uno).
Cinco: "el verso 5" = verse 5; the number comes after the noun.
Alimentar with the pronoun se attached: "alimentarse de algo" = to feed on something.
spanish.translation: to feed on, to feed itself

spanish.note: Masculine: el amor; the verb is amar, and "con amor" = with love, by love.
The Indian king, also called emperor, of this story, who won a war around 261 BC and then gave up war.
Past participle of atribuir, plural to agree with "versos": atribuidos a Buda = attributed to the Buddha.
The teacher whose teaching is Buddhism; Spanish writes Buda, without an h.
Cavar, to dig: "cava" is the present, "cavó" the pretérito indefinido, "cavados" the participle (pozos cavados = wells dug).
Present of cesar, a formal word for coming to an end: "el odio cesa" = hatred ceases; everyday Spanish says termina.
Peaceful agreement between people or groups; a formal word.
The taking of a land by war; the verb is conquistar.
Pretérito indefinido of conquistar, to take a land by war.
"Dejar constancia de algo" = to put something on record.
Present of constatar: to state what one finds to be so, without judging it.
Goes with estar: "no está contento" = he is not happy; the feminine is contenta.
Plural of credo, a set of religious beliefs; more formal than religión.
Past participle of deportar, to send people away from their land by force; feminine plural to agree with "personas".
Detener + lo: the pronoun is attached to the infinitive, "puede detenerlo" = can stop it.
Plural of edicto, an order that a ruler makes public.
The ruler of an empire (imperio); the feminine is emperatriz.
Present of encajar: "encaja con él" = it fits him, it matches him.
Goes with estar: "estar enfadado" = to be angry; in Latin America enojado is more common.
The noun that goes with enfadarse (to get angry); in Latin America people say enojo.
What a teacher teaches; from enseñar, to teach.
From ganar, to win; the feminine is ganadora.
"Grabar en piedra" = to carve in stone; grabado is the participle. Grabar also means to record sound or video.
Haber with the pronoun se attached: "podría haberse escrito" = could have been written.
Hablar, ellos/ellas form; "hablar de" = to speak of, to be about.
From India; the feminine is india. Nationalities take no capital letter in Spanish.
Words cut into stone or metal; the plural, inscripciones, loses the accent.
A strong, formal word for anger; everyday Spanish says enfado or enojo.
The land on the east coast of India that Ashoka conquered around 261 BC.
Pretérito indefinido of llevar, ellos form; "llevarse a alguien" = to take someone away.
"Mataron" is the pretérito indefinido, ellos form; with no subject it says that people were killed, without naming who did it.
Plural of medicina, something you take against an illness; la medicina is also the science of medicine.
Feminine plural of muerto. In the passive it serves as the participle of matar: "fueron muertas" = were killed.
Plural of muerto used as a noun: "contó los muertos" = he counted the dead.
The opposite of amor; the verb is odiar, to hate.
Plural of pilar, a tall column of stone.
Plantar, to plant: "plantó" is the pretérito indefinido, "plantados" the participle (árboles plantados = trees planted).
Plural of pozo, a deep hole dug in the ground to reach water.
A rule that tells the followers of a teaching how to live.
Present of prohibir; the accent on the í keeps o and i in separate syllables.
A telling of what happened; from relatar, to tell.
Plural of religión; the accent disappears in the plural.
The pain of knowing that you have done wrong; "sentir remordimiento" = to feel remorse.
Pretérito indefinido of renunciar, always with a: "renunció a la guerra" = he gave up war.
Feminine of sanitario, about care for the sick: "atención sanitaria" = health care, medical care.
Past participle of tallar, to cut a shape or words into stone or wood; masculine plural to agree with "edictos".
From traducir, to translate; the plural, traducciones, loses the accent.
Past participle of vencer, to win or to defeat: "habiendo vencido" = having won.
Cien: "100 gramos" = a hundred grams; before a noun Spanish says cien, never ciento.
Years are said as whole numbers: "en 1894" = in 1894 (mil ochocientos noventa y cuatro).
Mil novecientos seis: "de 1894 a 1906" = from 1894 to 1906.
Imperfect of apreciar, ellos form: "lo apreciaban mucho" = they liked it very much, over a long time.
Past participle of apretar, to press, feminine plural to agree with "manzanas": bien apretadas = packed close together.
Feminine of apto: "una sartén apta para horno" = a pan that can go in the oven, an ovenproof pan.
Caroline Tatin, Stéphanie's sister; the two ran the hotel together.
Feminine of cocinero: "era la cocinera" = she was the cook.
Past participle of cortar, feminine plural to agree with "manzanas": cortadas por la mitad = cut in half.
A story people tell, often an invented one: "es solo un cuento" = it is only a tale.
Pretérito indefinido of dirigir, ellos form: dirigir un hotel = to run a hotel.
A flat round shape: "un disco de masa" = a round of pastry.
"Tenía la estación enfrente" = the station was right opposite; before a noun Spanish says "enfrente de" or "frente a".
Pretérito indefinido of escribir, ellos form: "nunca escribieron la receta" = they never wrote the recipe down.
Imperfect of existir, ellos form: "ya existían" = they already existed.
Tú imperative of extender (e becomes ie): "extiende un disco de masa" = lay a round of pastry out flat.
"Gozar del favor de alguien" = to be well liked by someone; "por favor" = please.
Plural of fogón, a cooking ring; "ocuparse de los fogones" is a set way to say doing the cooking.
Imperfect of gozar: "gozar de algo" = to enjoy something, to have something good.
Plural of gramo; the thing weighed follows with de: 100 gramos de azúcar.
Pretérito indefinido of gustar: "les gustó mucho" = they liked it a lot; the thing liked is the subject.
Imperfect of hornear, to bake in the oven, for something done again and again; "se horneaba" = was baked.
The same word as in English, but the h is silent and the stress is on the last syllable.
Feminine plural, from invertir, to turn the other way round: tartas invertidas = upside-down tarts.
Short for kilogramo: "un kilo de manzanas" = a kilo of apples.
The French town where the Tatin sisters had their hotel, opposite the station.
A story people tell without proof: "es una leyenda"; "dice la leyenda que…" = legend has it that…
Imperfect of ocuparse: "se ocupaba de la cocina" = she looked after the cooking, it was her job.
Past participle of partir, to cut or split, feminine plural: partidas por la mitad = cut in half.
Past participle of pelar, to peel, feminine plural to agree with "manzanas".
Pretérito indefinido of regentar, a formal word for running a hotel, a shop or a bar.
Tú imperative of remeter: to push the edges of something in, like a sheet under a mattress.
Used almost always in "al revés": upside down, back to front, the other way round.
spanish.translation: wrong way round (al revés = upside down)

spanish.note: The region of France where Lamotte-Beuvron lies; Spanish keeps the French name.
Stéphanie Tatin, the sister who did the cooking at the hotel; a French name, written with its French accent.
From sujetar, to hold in place: "un plato bien sujeto" = a plate held firmly; as a noun, sujeto means subject.
A round sweet bake, here pastry with fruit; in Spain tarta is also the usual word for a cake.
The family name of the sisters Stéphanie and Caroline; today the upside-down apple tart carries it.
Present subjunctive of tomar, ellos form, needed after "hasta que": hasta que tomen un color dorado = until they turn golden.
Tú imperative of volcar (o becomes ue) + lo; the accent keeps the stress on vuél-.
spanish.translation: turn it over, tip it out

spanish.note: Plural of tigre, a masculine noun: el tigre, los tigres.
Read "dos mil diez"; the year when there were about 3200 wild tigers.
Read "tres mil doscientos"; Spanish writes a four-digit number with no dot or comma: 3200.
Present of proteger, ellos/ellas form; the g of proteger becomes j only before o and a: yo protejo.
Feminine of marino, from "mar" (sea): una tortuga marina = a sea turtle.
Plural of playa; the turtles lay their eggs on the beach.
English word, part of the report's English title, The Science of Hope; in Spanish "the" is el, la, los or las.
English word from the title The Science of Hope; the Spanish word is "ciencia".
English word from the title The Science of Hope; the Spanish word is "de".
English word from the title The Science of Hope, in Spanish "la ciencia de la esperanza"; hope = esperanza.
Ocho: "a 8 km" = 8 km away; dates use the plain number, not an ordinal: "el 8 de octubre" = 8 October.
The organisation that published the report on 8 October 2026; Spanish usually writes the name with no article.
"En promedio" = on average; "el promedio" is the average of several numbers.
Setenta y tres; "un 73 por ciento" = 73 per cent, and Spanish puts "un" or "el" before a percentage.
Pretérito indefinido of pagar, ellos/ellas form; paying a person takes "a": pagaron a más guardabosques.
Made of guardar (to guard) + bosques (forests); the form is the same in singular and plural: el guardabosques, los guardabosques.
"La ciencia de la esperanza" = the science of hope; the adjective is "científico".
Nouns in -ción are feminine; the plural drops the accent: las lecciones.
English word, part of the report's English name, Living Planet Report; in Spanish, "vivo".
English word from the name Living Planet Report; the Spanish word is "planeta".
English word from the name Living Planet Report; the Spanish word is "informe".
"El titular" is the headline of a piece of news; it comes from "título" (title).
Present of titularse: "el informe se titula…" = the report is titled…; always with "se" in this sense.
After "nada" the adjective stays masculine singular: nada mágico = nothing magical.
Pretérito indefinido of formar; with people it means to train: formaron guardabosques = they trained rangers.
Pretérito indefinido of luchar; "luchar contra" = to fight against.
"El comercio ilegal" = the illegal trade; "comercio" can also mean a shop.
The same form for masculine and feminine; the plural is "ilegales".
Gerund of hacer + lo; the pronoun joins the gerund, which then takes a written accent: "siguieron haciéndolo" = they kept doing it.
"Unos ochenta países" = some eighty countries; ochenta never changes for gender.
The Atlantic bluefin tuna is called "atún rojo" in Spanish, literally "red tuna".
"El Atlántico" is the Atlantic Ocean; names of oceans are masculine and written with a capital letter.
"Se recuperó" is the pretérito indefinido of recuperarse (to recover); "recuperado" is the past participle: se ha recuperado = has recovered.
Plural of límite, a masculine noun: "los límites de pesca" = the fishing limits.
From pescar (to fish); "los límites de pesca" say how much fish may be caught.
Past participle of estudiar used as an adjective; it agrees with feminine plural "poblaciones".
What belongs to every day: "un trabajo cotidiano" = everyday, ordinary work; the feminine is "cotidiana".
From "sombra" (shadow); "tan sombrío como siempre" = as grim as ever.
The animals of a place taken together; "la fauna salvaje" = wildlife.
Present of subtitularse: "se subtitula…" = it is subtitled…; from "subtítulo" (subtitle).
Present of examinar, él/ella form: to look at something carefully.
Pretérito indefinido of haber, the past of "hay" for an event; like "hay" it has one form: no hubo ningún milagro = there was no miracle.
Pretérito indefinido of ampliar, to make bigger; related to "amplio" (wide).
Plural of área, which is feminine but takes "el" in the singular: el área protegida, las áreas protegidas.
Past participle of proteger, feminine plural: áreas protegidas = protected areas. In "protegidas sus playas" it agrees with "playas".
Pretérito indefinido of perseguir; the e changes to i in this form (persiguió, persiguieron), and a person pursued takes "a".
Plural of traficante, someone who trades illegally; the singular is the same for a man or a woman.
Plural of frontera: "a través de las fronteras" = across borders.
From "nido" (nest): "playas de anidación" = nesting beaches, where the turtles lay their eggs.
Past participle of catalogar, agreeing with "el atún": catalogado En Peligro = listed as Endangered.
Past participle of recortar; "una vez recortados los límites" = once the limits were cut, and it agrees with "límites".
From capturar; "los límites de captura" = catch limits, how much fish may be taken.
Plural of avance, a step forward; from the verb avanzar (z becomes c before e).
Future of durar, ellos/ellas form: the endings are added to the whole infinitive (durar + án).
Plural of the noun causa: "las causas de las pérdidas" = the causes of the losses.
Read "ciento dos": 100 alone is "cien", but before another number it becomes "ciento".
Read "veinticuatro": the numbers from 21 to 29 are written as one word.
Read "veinticinco"; in dates Spanish uses the plain number, not an ordinal: "el 25 de octubre".
Read "doscientos cincuenta"; "su Gran Premio número 250" = his 250th Grand Prix, because high ordinals are rarely used in Spanish.
Read "sesenta y dos": from 31 to 99 the tens and units are joined with "y".
A city in Texas, in the United States, with a Formula 1 track.
Spanish uses hacer for the weather: "hace calor" = it is hot, "hizo calor" = it was hot; the noun is masculine: el calor.
Feminine of caluroso, from calor (heat); used for days, nights and climates: "una noche calurosa" = a hot night.
The winner of a championship (campeonato); the feminine is campeona and the plural campeones, both without the accent.
Pretérito indefinido of caer (él/ella), written with y; "cayó al sexto lugar" = he dropped to sixth place.
Pretérito indefinido of correr (to run); in motor sport correr means to race: "la Fórmula 1 corrió en Singapur".
Past participle of encender (to switch on, to light), feminine plural to agree with "las luces": "están encendidas" = they are on.
Plural of estado (state); "Estados Unidos" = the United States, often used without an article: "en Estados Unidos".
Plural of foco, a strong lamp; "bajo los focos" = under the floodlights, as at a night race.
The infinitive, used after puede and podría: "puede ganar el título" = he can win the title; ganar also means to earn.
Masculine form, here agreeing with "el calor": "calor húmedo" = humid heat; the noun is la humedad (humidity).
The first name of the driver Lando Norris.
Charles Leclerc, a driver for the Ferrari team; second in this race.
Pretérito indefinido of liderar (to lead), from the noun líder: "lideró todas las vueltas" = he led every lap.
Plural of luz: a final -z becomes -c- before -es (luz, luces).
A racing team; Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri drive for it. "Los McLaren" = the team's cars: the name takes no plural -s.
The engine of a car; the plural is motores. "Una penalización por el motor" = an engine penalty.
From noche: "un Gran Premio nocturno" is a Grand Prix run at night; the feminine is nocturna.
Lando Norris, a driver for the McLaren team; fourth in this race.
Ordinal of nueve; as a place in a race it stands without an article: "termina noveno" = he finishes ninth.
The first name of the driver Oscar Piastri.
From penalizar (to penalise): in racing, a punishment under the rules, such as a place further back at the start; the plural penalizaciones has no accent.
Oscar Piastri, a driver for the McLaren team; fifth in this race.
Ordinal of cinco: cuarto, quinto, sexto = fourth, fifth, sixth; the feminine is quinta.
Past participle of relegar (to send to a lower place), used like an adjective and agreeing with Russell: "relegado al fondo de la parrilla".
Feminine plural of seguido, from seguir (to follow): "dos victorias seguidas" = two wins in a row.
Masculine ordinal of seis: "terminó sexto" = he finished sixth; "el sexto lugar" = sixth place.
A part of a road, a race or a period of time: "el tramo final" = the last stretch, the closing stages.
In sport, the title of champion: "ganar el título" = to win the championship; it is also the title of a book or a film, and a university degree: "un título completo".
Past participle of unir (to join), masculine plural: "Estados Unidos" = the United States.
The first name of Edson Arantes do Nascimento (1940–2022), the Brazilian footballer the world knows as Pelé.
The town in Brazil where Edson grew up.
The ball of a game: "no tiene pelota" = he has no ball; a large football is also called un balón.
A masculine noun in -ín; the plural drops the accent: los calcetines.
A sports club: "un gran club" = a big club; the plural is clubes.
Written as one word, with an accent on the last syllable; "a los dieciséis" = at sixteen.
One game between two teams; "el último partido" of a cup is the one that decides the title.
"La Copa del Mundo" = the World Cup; a copa is also a glass with a stem.
"Meter" or "marcar un gol" = to score a goal; the plural adds -es: dos goles.
The name by which the world knows the Brazilian footballer Edson Arantes do Nascimento.
Part of the family name of Edson Arantes do Nascimento, known as Pelé.
Portuguese word (de + o), part of the Brazilian family name Arantes do Nascimento; the Spanish word is "del".
The last part of the family name of Edson Arantes do Nascimento, known as Pelé.
Veintitrés; dates use the plain number: "el 23 de octubre de 1940" = 23 October 1940, the day Edson was born.
Nouns in -ista have one form for men and women: el futbolista, la futbolista.
Singular; "papel de periódico" = newspaper as a material, old sheets of it. Plural: periódicos.
The Brazilian football club that Edson joined at fifteen; Spanish puts the article before a club's name: el Santos.
A country in the north of Europe; no article: en Suecia = in Sweden.
"Marcar un gol" = to score a goal: marcó is the pretérito indefinido, "ha marcado" the pretérito perfecto; elsewhere marcar means to mark.
Read "cinco a dos"; Spanish writes a score with a hyphen: "Brasil ganó 5-2" = Brazil won 5–2.
The name by which Edson's father, a footballer, was known.
Infinitive after solía: "solía practicar" = he usually practised, he used to practise.
Forms of rellenar (to stuff, to fill something completely): rellenaba is the imperfect, "había rellenado" the pluperfect.
Pretérito indefinido of fichar: a player ficha por a club (fichó por el Santos = he signed for Santos) and a club ficha a player (el Santos lo fichó = Santos signed him).
Veintinueve; "el 29 de junio de 1958" is the day of the last match, and "el 29 de diciembre de 2022" the day Pelé died.
The sixth month; months are written without a capital letter in Spanish: "el 29 de junio".
From jugar (to play); the feminine is jugadora.
Relative cuanto agrees with its noun: "cuantas horas le quedaban" = all the hours he had left; it is written Spanish, and has no accent, unlike the question word cuántas.
spanish.translation: as many … as, all the … that

spanish.note: Pretérito indefinido of convocar: in sport, to pick a player for a team, here the team of Brazil.
A competition of many matches; here "el torneo" is the World Cup.
Read "mil novecientos sesenta y dos"; the year of the second World Cup that Pelé won.
Past participle of igualar, from igual (equal): "nadie ha igualado" = nobody has equalled.
The material: "una pelota de cuero" = a leather ball; Spanish names the material with "de".
Read "mil novecientos setenta y cuatro"; the year Sweden's parental leave began, on 1 January.
A rule made by a country: "una ley nueva" = a new law; the plural is leyes.
Read "mil novecientos noventa y cinco"; the year Sweden reserved one month of leave for each parent.
The everyday word for a married man in relation to his wife: "marido o pareja" = husband or partner.
Regular -ar verb: no fuma = he does not smoke; "dejar de fumar" = to stop smoking (dejar de + infinitive).
Present of levantarse, a reflexive verb: se levanta = he gets up; without se, levantar means to lift. Of the wind, "se levanta el viento" = the wind picks up.
spanish.translation: gets up; (of the wind) picks up

spanish.note: Preguntar takes "a" before the person who is asked: preguntan a la matrona = they ask the midwife.
Read "cero coma cinco"; Spanish writes decimals with a comma where English uses a point.
Gerund of cobrar (to receive one's pay); seguir + gerund means to keep doing: seguir cobrando = to go on being paid.
Pretérito indefinido of reservar, él/ella form: Suecia reservó un mes; "se reservó un mes" = a month was reserved.
Of a mother or a father; "permiso parental" = parental leave, paid time away from work to care for a child.
Read "ciento ochenta"; the number of paid days the two parents could share in 1974.
Past participle of pagar used as an adjective, masculine plural to agree with días: días pagados = paid days.
Read "noventa y nueve coma cinco"; the decimal comma is the Spanish way of writing 99.5.
What rises from a cigarette or a fire; "humo de segunda mano" = second-hand smoke, the smoke of another person's cigarette.
Same form for masculine and feminine; it takes para: perjudicial para el bebé = harmful for the baby.
Dar + le, written as one word because the pronoun is attached to an infinitive; "darle de comer" = to feed him or her.
Des- + aparecer (to appear); after suele it stays in the infinitive: suele desaparecer = it usually goes away.
Sustituir A por B = to replace A with B: the new thing takes por.
From madre; "permiso de maternidad" = maternity leave, the leave for mothers only.
A change made to a law or a system: antes de la reforma = before the reform.
Present subjunctive of durar, used because the clause describes any low mood of that kind: un ánimo que dure más de dos semanas.
First name of Virginia Woolf (1882–1941), the English writer of A Room of One's Own.
Surname of Virginia Woolf, the English novelist and essayist; pronounced like the English word "wolf".
Feminine of escritor; after ser it takes no article: es escritora = she is a writer.
Plural of charla, an informal word for a talk or lecture; dar una charla = to give a talk.
Read mil novecientos veintinueve; the year the talks became a book.
Read mil novecientos cuarenta y ocho; the year Cambridge first gave women full degrees.
The lock built into a door, opened with a key; a padlock is a candado.
Newnham College, a college for women at the University of Cambridge, founded in 1871.
Girton College, a college for women at the University of Cambridge, founded in 1869.
Plural of colegio; usually a school, but for Cambridge or Oxford it names the colleges that make up the university.
Stories that are invented, such as novels; escribir ficción = to write fiction.
Quinientos agrees with a feminine noun: quinientas libras, but quinientos años.
Plural of libra, the British pound (money); also a unit of weight.
Asistir a = to attend, to go to (a class, a meeting); it does not mean "to assist" here.
Nouns ending in -dad are feminine: la universidad.
Dar + les (to them): object pronouns are attached to the end of an infinitive.
Same form for masculine and feminine: la idea central = the main idea.
Feminine of preciso, here describing Woolf: es precisa = she is precise.
Nouns ending in -tad are feminine: la libertad de pensar = the freedom to think.
Plural of novelista, a writer of novels; the same form for a man or a woman (el/la novelista).
Plural of oyente (from oír, to hear), the people listening to a talk; el/la oyente, one form for both.
Reflexive; presentarse a un examen = to sit or take an exam.
spanish.translation: to sit (an exam), to present oneself

spanish.note: Past participle of revisar used as an adjective, feminine plural to agree with las charlas.
Past participle of ampliar used as an adjective, feminine plural to agree with las charlas.
Condensar with se: se condensa en una frase = it is condensed into one sentence, a se form instead of the passive.
A more formal word than pensar; reflexionar sobre algo = to reflect on something.
Something only some people have; un privilegio de los ricos = a privilege of the rich.
Same form for masculine and feminine; trabajo intelectual = work done with the mind.
Plural of femenino; colegios femeninos = colleges for women.
Read "mil novecientos cuatro"; the year Bircher-Benner opened his sanatorium above Zurich.
First name of Maximilian Bircher-Benner (1867–1939), the Swiss doctor behind the original muesli.
Surname of Maximilian Bircher-Benner, a doctor in Zurich; the hyphen joins two family names into one.
The largest city in Switzerland; Spanish writes it with an accent on the u: Zúrich.
Bircher-Benner's own Swiss German name for his apple dish; it stays untranslated in the Spanish text.
Feminine of crudo, agreeing with comida or manzana: manzana cruda = raw apple.
Masculine form (feminine suiza); alemán suizo = Swiss German, the German spoken in Switzerland.
From rallar: ralla is the tú imperative, rallada the past participle used as an adjective (manzana rallada).
From remojar: remoja is the tú imperative, remojada the past participle agreeing with avena.
Used in "en remojo": dejar en remojo = to leave to soak.
Plural of fruto; "frutos secos" is the everyday Spanish word for nuts such as almonds or hazelnuts.
A clinic where patients stay to rest and recover, often in the mountains or the countryside.
The mountain range across Switzerland and its neighbours; always plural with the article: los Alpes.
The continent; "toda Europa" = all over Europe, with no article.
The oat and fruit dish that grew out of Bircher-Benner's evening apple dish; el muesli.
German adjective in the name of Bircher-Benner's sanatorium, Lebendige Kraft = living strength.
German noun in the name Lebendige Kraft, kept untranslated; the Spanish text glosses it as «fuerza viva».
The amount of food for one person: para una ración = for one serving.
In "cucharada sopera" (a tablespoon); it agrees with cucharada: tres cucharadas soperas.
Spanish spelling of yoghurt; the plural is yogures.
Feminine, agreeing with leche: leche condensada = condensed milk.
From azúcar (sugar), feminine to agree with leche: leche condensada azucarada = sweetened condensed milk.
A lung disease; the same form in singular and plural, with the article la.
Here used as a noun, el original = the first version; the same form serves both genders as an adjective.
The year Haiti became independent; read "mil ochocientos cuatro".
A country in the Caribbean, on the island of La Española; written with an accent on the í.
Nationality words are not capitalised in Spanish: los haitianos = the Haitians, las familias haitianas = Haitian families.
Sopa de calabaza = pumpkin soup; in Spanish the material or ingredient follows de.
Part of the Haitian name soup joumou, kept as it is; the Spanish word is sopa.
Haitian Creole for pumpkin, in the name soup joumou; the soup is often called sopa joumou in Spanish.
Comer + la: an object pronoun joins the end of an infinitive, here la = la sopa.
Hacer un puré = to blend or mash something until it is smooth.
Spanish of Spain; in Latin America the word is papas.
The small green citrus fruit; zumo de lima = lime juice (and Lima, with a capital, is the capital of Peru).
Pretérito indefinido of independizarse, a reflexive verb: Haití se independizó = Haiti became independent.
Personas esclavizadas = enslaved people: the word stresses that someone was forced into slavery, so it is preferred to esclavos.
La cultura viva = living culture, traditions people still practise.
A town in the north-west of Haiti where independence was declared on 1 January 1804.
French first name of Jean-Jacques Dessalines, the leader of Haiti's independence.
Jean-Jacques Dessalines (1758–1806), who declared Haiti's independence in 1804.
Nouns ending in -encia are feminine: la independencia de Haití.
Nouns ending in -ción are feminine; the plural revoluciones loses the accent.
Tú imperative of triturar + la; the written accent keeps the stress on the same syllable as tritura.
Litro y medio = a litre and a half, with no article before litro.
Carne de vaca = beef; carne de res is the usual phrase in much of Latin America.
Patrimonio vivo = living heritage: traditions that a people still keep.
Past participle of encabezar (from cabeza, head), agreeing with revolución: encabezada por = led by.
Owners of a hacienda, a large farm or plantation; singular hacendado.
"El salón del automóvil" is the usual Spanish name for a motor show; the plural is salones, without the accent.
A more formal word than "coche"; it appears in set names like el Salón del Automóvil (the Motor Show).
The capital of France; Spanish writes it with an accent on the i: París.
The town west of Paris with the royal palace; Spanish has its own name for it, Versalles.
French word in the place name Porte de Versailles, the exhibition centre in the south-west of Paris; the name stays in French.
French spelling, kept only in the place name Porte de Versailles; on its own the town is Versalles in Spanish.
El jardín de las Tullerías is the Tuileries garden in the centre of Paris, next to the Louvre; Spanish uses its own name for it.
Read "mil ochocientos noventa y ocho"; the year of the first Paris Motor Show.
Read "quince"; dates in Spanish put the day first: el 15 de junio de 1898.
Read "dieciocho"; "del 13 al 18 de octubre" = from 13 to 18 October.
Read "quinientos mil"; Spanish separates thousands with a dot and decimals with a comma.
Read "quinientos dieciocho mil trescientos setenta y dos"; the dot separates the thousands in Spanish.
Read "ciento cuarenta mil"; "unas 140.000 personas" = about 140,000 people.
Read "nonagésima primera"; the raised ª marks a feminine ordinal agreeing with "vez": por 91.ª vez = for the 91st time.
Adjective that agrees with its noun: un coche eléctrico, una versión eléctrica, coches eléctricos.
Plural of el fabricante; fabricantes de coches = car makers. The same form is used for a man, a woman or a company.
Plural of popular; the same form serves masculine and feminine: los coches más populares.
Pretérito indefinido of visitar, ellos/ellas form; "lo visitaron" = they visited it.
Pretérito indefinido of celebrar; with events it means "to hold": se celebró el salón = the show was held.
Pretérito indefinido of presentar, él/ella form: uno presentó una versión = one showed a version.
Plural of el taxi; a word that is almost the same in many languages.
A flat raised area of a garden or building; la terraza del jardín = the garden's terrace.
"Aquel verano" = that summer; the first show ran from June to July 1898.
Plural of el organizador, from organizar (to organise).
Pretérito indefinido of participar; often placed before its subject in news style: participaron más de sesenta fabricantes.
"Pensado para" means made with a purpose in mind, here agreeing with coches: pensados para las calles = meant for the streets.
Used as a collective noun for the people who come to see something: atraer al público = to draw the crowds.
Exponer (to exhibit) with "se" gives a passive meaning: ningún coche podía exponerse = no car could be shown.
spanish.translation: to be exhibited, to be shown

spanish.note: Plural of el agricultor, a person who works the land; from agricultura.
Un campo arado is a ploughed field; in football el campo is the pitch or ground ("en el campo del Real Betis"); it can also mean the countryside.
Participle of arar (to plough), here an adjective: un campo arado = a ploughed field; as a noun, el arado is the plough.
Plural of asequible; más asequibles = more affordable, a neutral word that avoids talking about prices.
Pretérito indefinido of acudir, a more formal verb than venir for people going to an event.
Past participle of concebir, used here like an adjective: concebido para llevar = designed to carry.
Imperfect of figurar; "entre ellos figuraba" = among them was, a formal way to name one item of a group.
"Por sus propios medios" = by its own means; in F1, "de medios a duros" = from medium to hard tyres.
Plural of el modelo; for cars it means a type made by a maker.
Pretérito indefinido of resucitar (to bring back to life), used figuratively for old names.
Feminine plural of urbano, agreeing with calles: calles urbanas = city streets.
Plural of el vehículo, the general word for anything that carries people or goods.
Plural of el/la visitante; the same form is used for men and women.
Read "diecisiete"; in dates Spanish uses the plain number, not an ordinal: "el sábado 17 de octubre".
Read "setenta y siete"; "hasta el minuto 77" = until the 77th minute, because Spanish names a minute with the plain number.
Read "uno a cero"; Spanish writes a score with a hyphen and says "a" between the numbers: "ganó 1-0".
Read "tres a cero"; "al descanso ganaba 3-0" = it was 3–0 up at half-time.
Read "tres a uno"; the winner's goals come first after "ganó": "el Inter ganó 3-1".
Read "tres a dos"; a 3-2 is a win "por la mínima", by a single goal.
Read "seis a uno"; with the article it names the match itself: "en el 6-1 del Bayern" = in Bayern's 6–1 win.
First name of Luis Díaz, the Colombian forward of FC Bayern who scored three goals against RB Leipzig on 17 October 2026.
Surname of Luis Díaz, Bayern's Colombian forward; the accent marks the stress on the í: DÍ-az.
First name of Aleksandar Pavlović, a German midfielder of FC Bayern who scored against RB Leipzig.
Surname of Aleksandar Pavlović, Bayern midfielder; the ć is a Serbian letter, read like a soft "ch".
First name of Michael Olise, a French winger of FC Bayern who scored against RB Leipzig.
Surname of Michael Olise, Bayern's French winger.
First name of Harry Kane, the England captain who plays for FC Bayern.
Surname of Harry Kane, Bayern's English striker, who scored the fifth goal against Leipzig.
FC Bayern München, Germany's most successful football club; Spanish press says "el Bayern" or "el Bayern de Múnich".
The capital of Bavaria in southern Germany, written Múnich in Spanish with an accent; München in German.
Part of the club name RB Leipzig; the letters stand for RasenBallsport ("lawn ball sport").
A city in eastern Germany; here the club RB Leipzig, which Spanish press calls "el Leipzig".
Part of "Allianz Arena", Bayern's stadium in the north of Munich; the name is kept in German.
The German first division; Spanish keeps the German name and makes it feminine because of "la liga": "la Bundesliga".
Part of the name Borussia Dortmund; Borussia is the Latin name for Prussia.
A city in western Germany; here the club Borussia Dortmund, which Spanish press often calls just "el Dortmund".
The country; the people and the language are "alemán", "alemana".
A city in north-west England; part of the club name Manchester City.
Part of the club name Manchester City; Spanish press often says just "el City".
A town in the east of England; here the club Ipswich Town, "el Ipswich" in Spanish press.
English for a town; part of the club name Ipswich Town.
A London football club; Spanish press says "el Arsenal".
A city in central England; part of the club name Nottingham Forest.
English for forest; part of the club name Nottingham Forest.
The capital of Catalonia; here the club FC Barcelona, "el Barcelona" or "el Barça" in Spanish press.
Part of the name Real Betis, the club from Seville; "Betis" comes from Baetis, the Latin name of the river Guadalquivir.
FC Internazionale Milano, a club from Milan; Spanish press says "el Inter".
The football club of the Italian city of Bologna; the club keeps its Italian name, while the city is Bolonia in Spanish.
Part of the club name Paris Saint-Germain, written without the accent of the Spanish city name París.
Part of the club name Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), after the town of Saint-Germain-en-Laye near Paris; one hyphenated word.
A city in north-east France, on the German border; Spanish writes it Estrasburgo.
The sporting year; in football it runs from August to May: "la temporada 2026-2027".
From descansar (to rest); in football "al descanso" = at half-time.
Pretérito indefinido of golear, from gol: to win by a lot of goals; it takes "a" before the team: "goleó al Leipzig".
A win by many goals, from golear; "completar la goleada" = to add the last goals of a big win.
Three goals by one player in one match; Spanish press also uses the English "hat-trick"; "firmar un triplete" = to score a hat-trick.
Pretérito indefinido of firmar (to sign); sports press uses it for a feat that carries a player's signature: "firmó un triplete".
Pretérito indefinido of arrollar (to run over); in sport it means to beat a team by far: "arrolló 6-1 al Leipzig".
Pretérito indefinido of aupar (to lift up), written with an accent on the ó; "aupó al Bayern al liderato" = took Bayern to the top.
First place in a league table, from líder (leader): "el liderato de la Bundesliga".
Pretérito indefinido of superar (to overcome, to beat); "superó por la mínima" = edged past.
Feminine of mínimo; "por la mínima" (by the minimum) means winning by a single goal, as in 3-2.
Pretérito indefinido of prolongar (to make longer): "prolongó su arranque impecable" = kept its flawless start going.
From arrancar (to start up, as an engine); in sport "el arranque de temporada" is the first weeks of the season.
Pretérito indefinido of sobreponerse (to get over something), irregular like poner → puso; it is reflexive: "se sobrepuso a un gol".
From temprano (early); "un gol tempranero" = an early goal, scored in the first minutes.
From vencer (to defeat); "vencedor por 1-0" = 1–0 winner, a noun used in apposition instead of "que ganó".
Maria Montessori (1870–1952), the Italian doctor who opened the first Casa dei Bambini in Rome; her Italian first name has no accent, unlike Spanish María.
The surname of Maria Montessori; it is also the name of the teaching method she created (el método Montessori).
Read "seis"; Spanish puts the day first and adds de before month and year: el 6 de enero de 1907.
Read "mil novecientos siete"; the year Montessori opened her first room for children in Rome.
Read "mil ochocientos noventa y seis"; the year Montessori qualified in medicine.
Read "mil novecientos cincuenta y dos"; the year Montessori died, in the Netherlands.
Feminine, plural sillas; the small form sillita is a common, affectionate way to say a child's chair.
A regular -er verb: barren (they sweep), barrieron (they swept), barrían (they used to sweep); barrer el suelo = to sweep the floor.
El suelo is the floor of a room or the ground outside; it is also "I usually" from the verb soler, a different word.
A jug with a handle for water or milk; una jarra pequeña is a small one a child can hold.
Feminine; barrer con una escoba = to sweep with a broom.
Short form of santo used before most male saints' names: San Lorenzo, San Pedro (but Santo Tomás, Santo Domingo).
San Lorenzo is a working-class district of Rome, near the main railway station, where the first Casa dei Bambini opened.
Graduarse en medicina = to graduate in medicine, to get a medical degree; Spanish often writes the degree subject with a capital: Medicina.
Masculine; un edificio de viviendas = an apartment building.
Spanish counts furniture: un mueble is one piece, los muebles is the furniture.
Participle of estrenar (to use or wear for the first time); recién estrenado = brand-new, just opened.
Reflexive: graduarse en medicina = to graduate in medicine; las primeras en graduarse = the first to graduate, with en before the infinitive.
Plural of humilde, the same for masculine and feminine; familias humildes is the everyday, kind way to say low-income families.
Meterse en = to get into something; meterse con = to pick on.
spanish.translation: to get into, to take on; to interfere

spanish.note: Said as a whole number: mil novecientos setenta y uno; en 1971 = in 1971.
Said dos mil catorce; "para 2014" means "by 2014", "hasta 2014" means "up to 2014".
Read "ochenta"; un 80 por ciento = 80 percent, with "un" before the figure as people say it.
The country in northern Europe; country names take no article in Spanish: en Finlandia.
A region on both sides of the border between Finland and Russia; Karelia del Norte (North Karelia) is the Finnish region in the east.
Pekka Puska, the young Finnish doctor who started the North Karelia Project in 1972.
Pekka Puska, the Finnish doctor who led the North Karelia Project from 1972.
Feminine plural of asustado (from asustar, to frighten); estar asustado = to be scared, a feeling, so it takes estar.
Past participle of copiar; había copiado = had copied (pluperfect, había + participle).
From empujar (to push); in talk, el empujón also means the push that gets something going.
Same form for masculine and feminine; locales is the plural: los líderes locales = the local leaders. As a noun, el local = the premises, the shop: "en el local" = on the premises.
spanish.translation: local; (el local) the premises, the shop

spanish.note: Plural of central, a plant; las centrales lecheras = the dairies, the plants that process milk.
Feminine plural of lechero, from leche: centrales lecheras = dairies.
A place that makes or sells milk, from leche; la lechería local = the local dairy.
Leche desnatada = skimmed milk, with the cream (la nata) taken out; in Latin America it is often called leche descremada.
Leche baja en grasa = low-fat milk; grasa is the fat in food.
A spread made from plant oils; margarina vegetal = plant spread.
Same form for masculine and feminine: margarina vegetal = a spread made from plants, not from milk.
Feminine of mediano; la mediana edad = middle age, roughly from forty to sixty.
A medicine you take; ningún medicamento nuevo = no new medicine at all.
Poner en marcha = to start, to get something going: puso en marcha el proyecto = started the project.
Firmar una petición = to sign a petition; from pedir, to ask.
In everyday Spanish precioso means very pretty or lovely, not "precious": un sitio precioso = a lovely place.
A best or worst figure no one else has; un récord muy triste = a very sad record. Written with an accent.
Repartir pastillas = to hand out pills, to give one to each person.
Same form for masculine and feminine; un récord terrible = a terrible record.
Said "mil novecientos noventa y tres"; en octubre de 1993 = in October 1993.
Said "trescientos"; el año 300 antes de Cristo = the year 300 BC.
Said "ochocientos"; unas 800 tiras = about 800 strips (unas = about, before a number).
Said "sesenta y cuatro"; el capítulo 64 = chapter 64.
The country; the adjective and the language are chino/china, with a small letter.
A city in Hubei, central China; the Guodian tomb was found near it in 1993.
An old Chinese book of short wise sayings, about 2,300 years old; it is also the name given to its legendary author.
The other name of the Laozi, "the book of the way and of virtue"; also written Tao Te Ching.
An old Chinese measure of distance, about half a kilometre; it does not change in the plural: mil li.
Medio kilómetro = half a kilometre; the plural is kilómetros.
Abrir una tumba = to open a tomb; feminine noun.
Keeps the accent on the last syllable; tiras de bambú = bamboo strips.
The written signs on something (escritura antigua = old writing); from escribir, to write.
Plural of arqueólogo (archaeologist), the person who digs up and studies old things.
Plural of ladrón (thief); the accent goes away in the plural.
El capítulo 64 = chapter 64; the number comes after the noun.
Masculine even though it ends in -a: un idioma, aprender un idioma = to learn a language.
Abrazar (to hug) + lo (it) joined at the end of the infinitive; demasiado grande para abrazarlo = too big to hug.
Short, everyday word for bicicleta, used all over the Spanish-speaking world; ir en bici = to go by bike.
-ísimo makes an adjective much stronger: lento → lentísimo (really slow).
No hacerle ninguna gracia a alguien = someone is not pleased at all.
Participle of adueñarse (to take over, make one's own): se habían adueñado de = had taken over.
Jugársela = to take a gamble; the pronouns se and la are attached to the infinitive.
Poner el grito en el cielo (put the shout in the sky) = to protest loudly, hit the roof.
En su sano juicio = in their right mind.
Ir contra la intuición = to go against what you would expect.
Fijarse (en) = to pay attention to, notice; fíjate is the tú imperative, se fijó the past.
Forms of cargar (to carry something heavy): ella cargaba = she carried; lo que cargas = what you carry.
Tomárselo en serio = to take it seriously; se and lo are attached to the infinitive.
Gerund of saltar: saltando de una pantalla a otra = jumping from one screen to the next.
Imperfect of apartar: apartaba la vista = he looked away (each time).
From arder; the burning feeling in the eyes.
Has + participle is the tú present perfect: casi ni has cocinado = you've hardly even cooked.
Lo lógico es que + subjunctive = the sensible thing is for…
Siendo realistas = let's be realistic, if we're honest.
Imperative of repartir + las: spread them (the vegetables) across the tray.
Un buen chorro de aceite = a good glug of oil; chorrito is the small version.
Encargarse de = to take care of, be in charge of: el horno se encarga = the oven takes care of it.
Imperfect of turnarse: se turnaban para = they took turns to.
Echarse una siesta = to have a nap, in everyday Spanish everywhere; se echaron = they had (a nap).
-ísimo strengthens mucho: muchísimo más complejo = far more complex.
A principios de = at the start of: a principios de los noventa = in the early nineties.
The year Atlantic bluefin tuna was listed as Endangered.
Present of anidar: where the turtle nests (lays its eggs).
Pretérito indefinido of recortar, here in impersonal se: se recortaron los límites = the limits were cut.
Centrarse en = to focus on: se centran en unos pocos ríos = they focus on a few rivers.
Copiar + los: pueden copiarlos = they can copy them (the machines).
Atacar un problema = to tackle a problem, an everyday figurative use.
Plural of aparato: any machine or device.
Gerund of guiar; ir + gerund (va guiando) shows an action going on step by step.
Participle of atrapar: habían atrapado = they had caught.
Adiós a algo = goodbye to something, said of something you lose.
Pretérito indefinido of pesar (to weigh): pesó sus palabras = she weighed her words.
Pasarse = to go too far, overdo it: sin pasarse = without overdoing it.
Ni una miga = not a single crumb.
Forms of soltar: le soltaba el mismo consejo = he'd come out with the same advice; soltó una carcajada = he burst out laughing.
Con la mejor intención = with the best of intentions.
Imperfect subjunctive of convencer: una respuesta que la convenciera = an answer that would convince her.
Un negocio = a business, a shop or company.
Participle of tragar: se habría tragado = would have swallowed up.
Forms of almorzar (to have lunch): almorzó = she had lunch (indefinido); almorzaba = she used to have lunch (imperfect).
Soltar una carcajada = to burst out laughing.
Oler de maravilla = to smell wonderful; de maravilla = wonderfully.
Cuajarse: eggs setting as they cook; se cuajan = they set, se han cuajado = they have set.
Present of acordarse (de): nadie se acuerda de ellos = nobody remembers them.
Present of ablandarse: se ablandan = they go soft.
Participle of sofreír: fried slowly in a little oil, the base of many sauces.
Present of soltar, ellos form: sueltan su aroma = they give off their aroma.
Ir derecho/derecha a = to go straight to; here it agrees with la sartén.
Pretérito indefinido of meter: metió el teléfono en un cajón = she put the phone in a drawer.
Present of malgastar (to waste): la malgastan = they waste it.
-ísimo makes an adjective very strong: ocupadísimo = extremely busy.
Regalar + se (for le) + la: regalársela a «más tarde» = to hand it over to 'later'.
Present subjunctive of conseguir after antes de que: antes de que consiga sentarse = before she manages to sit down.
Cured pork belly, used in Spain and Latin America alike.
Sin rastro de = without a trace of.
From English: la pole = first place on the starting grid.
Encadenar = to link up: encadena dos victorias = he wins two in a row.
Present of plantar; se plantan = are planted, the impersonal se.
-ito makes a word smaller and warmer: pequeño → pequeñito.
Masculine of espesa: un bosque espeso = a dense forest.
Present of ver for tú; ya ves = you see, there you go, a spoken filler.
Pretérito indefinido of inventar for él/ella.
Pretérito indefinido of evitar for ellos.
Pretérito indefinido of idear (to devise), for él/ella.
Gerund of estudiar; pasarse la vida estudiando = to spend one's life studying.
Present of competir, an e → i verb: compito, compite, compiten.
Conditional of pensar; uno pensaría = you'd think.
Present of frenar (to brake); eso los frena = that holds them back.
Árbol + -ito: a small or young tree.
Participle of apuntarse; apuntarse a algo = to sign up for, to join in.
Le encanta = she loves it: encantar works like gustar, the thing loved is the subject.
Masculine singular of feo/fea: the everyday word for ugly, not nice to look at.
The everyday word for nice to look at, used everywhere Spanish is spoken.
Agrees with the person: ella va descalza, ellos van descalzos.
Imperfect of comparar: something she did again and again.
Pretérito indefinido of parar (and pararse) for él/ella: se paró = he stopped.
Present of conseguir for yo, g-form: consigo, consigues, consigue. Also means 'with himself' in other contexts.
Imperfect of adorar: a strong 'love' for a thing or a place.
Infinitive comparar + los; al compararlos = when she compared them.
Participle of adorar; había adorado = had loved.
De golpe = all of a sudden.
Imperfect of parar; no paraba de = she kept on (doing).
Dar la talla = to measure up, to be good enough.
Infinitive ver + la (her); para verla = to see her.
Paso + -ito: a small step, said warmly.
Imperfect of tener for tú: describes a situation in the past.
Reflexive: atreverse a + infinitive = to dare to, to find the nerve to.
Tú imperative of centrarse with the pronoun attached: céntrate en = focus on.
Present of circular; circula desde hace años = it has been going around for years.
Tú imperative of acordarse, o → ue: acuérdate de = remember.
Poner orden = to tidy up, to sort things out.
Imperfect of haber for tú; with a participle it makes the pluperfect: habías probado = you had tried.
Participle of probar (to try, to taste).
Infinitive convencer + te; convencerte de = to get yourself to.
Plural of manejable: easy to handle.
Infinitive comprometerse with te attached: comprometerte con algo = to commit to it.
From llevar: más llevadero = easier to cope with.
Recorrer un camino = to walk a path all the way.
Feminine of feo; for food or dough: not nice to look at.
Tú imperative of olvidarse with te attached; olvídate de ella = forget about it.
Parecer un desastre = to look a mess.
Present subjunctive of intentar for tú, used for a negative command: no intentes.
Present of ir for tú; te vas = you leave, you walk away.
Adjective from desastre: con un aspecto desastroso = looking a mess.
Tú imperative of resistir, the same as the él/ella present.
Resistir la tentación de + infinitive = to resist the urge to.
Present of firmar (to sign); firmar con un nombre = to sign with a name.
Imperfect subjunctive of tomar; para que se tomaran en serio = so they would be taken seriously.
Present of soñar, o → ue: soñar con = to dream of.
Present of lograr for él/ella: nunca lo logra = she never manages it.
Ser una tontería = to be silly, a waste of time.
Present of arreglar: the everyday word for fix.
Present of pensar for yo, e → ie: pienso, piensas, piensa.
Singular of iglesias; relojes de iglesia = church clocks.
Imperfect of arreglar: what she did again and again.
Poner su granito de arena = to do one's bit.
Infinitive of tirar; tirar algo = to throw it away (also to throw).
Present of fiarse: se fía de mí = trusts me.
Imperfect of parar; no paraban de cambiar = they kept on changing.
Pretérito indefinido of atender: for doctors, to treat or see to a patient or a wound.
Imperfect of atender: what the doctors did every time.
Infinitive of morder, o → ue: muerde. Al morder = when they bite.
Imperfect of consistir; consistir en = to consist of.
Infinitive of eliminar; por eliminar = for eliminating.
Estar atento a = to keep an eye on, to watch out for.
Before a noun, puro/pura means 'nothing but': pura rutina = sheer routine.
In sport, la selección = the national team.
Imperfect of practicar: what he did again and again.
From jugar: el juego = the game, how it is played.
De acuerdo = in agreement: están de acuerdo = they agree.
Present of afinar for él/ella: afina el cerebro = sharpens the brain.
Infinitive of agrupar: volvió a agrupar a los pilotos = it bunched the drivers up again.
Pretérito indefinido of arrancar; for a car or a race start it means to pull away: arrancó despacio = he got away slowly.
Infinitive of cazar; la caza is the noun (hunting).
Present of convenir: conviene + infinitive = it's a good idea to.
spanish.translation: it's a good idea, it's best

spanish.note: Conditional of decir for él/ella: te diría = would tell you.
Pretérito indefinido of encerrar for ellos: lo encerraron = they locked him up.
It never changes: la electricidad extra, los días extra.
Imperfect subjunctive of felicitar, after esperaba que: he hoped she would praise him.
Same form for masculine and feminine: la vuelta ha sido impresionante.
-ísimo makes mucho stronger; feminine plural here because it stands for las ballenas.
Feminine of polémico: fue polémica = it was controversial (la moratoria).
Present of presumir for él/ella: no presume = it doesn't show off.
Una prohibición internacional = an international ban.
Repartir + se: podían repartirse los días = they could split the days between them.
spanish.translation: to share out, split between them

spanish.note: Imperfect of resfriarse, for a repeated event: se resfriaba mucho = she kept catching colds.
El más sabio = the wisest; used of advice as well as of people.
Present of saltar; saltar a la vista = to jump out at you, to be obvious.
spanish.translation: jumps; salta a la vista = it's obvious

spanish.note: Present of sentar (not sentir): abril les sienta bien al viento = April suits the wind.
spanish.translation: suits; sentarle bien a = to be good for

spanish.note: Feminine of terco: la esperanza es terca = hope is stubborn.
A toda velocidad = at full speed.
Same form for masculine and feminine: patrimonio cultural, vida cultural.
Patrimonio cultural inmaterial = intangible cultural heritage, UNESCO's name for living traditions such as songs and crafts.
-ísimo/-ísima makes an adjective much stronger: larga → larguísima; the g takes a u to keep its hard sound.
Feminine of helado; una isla helada = a frozen island.
Written as one word: diez y ocho → dieciocho.
Plural of grado; dieciocho grados bajo cero = minus eighteen degrees.
The sloping side of a mountain: en la ladera de una montaña.
Plural of túnel; words ending in -l add -es.
Present of mantener, ellos form; irregular like tener: mantienen = they keep.
Present of fallar; si falla la electricidad = if the power fails.
Present of conservar: to keep something as it is, often cold or fresh.
Plural señales; la señal de que… = the sign that…
No tiene más misterio = there's nothing more to it.
Past participle of resolver; desayuno resuelto = breakfast sorted.
Imperative of rellenar: to fill a hollow with something (relleno = filling).
Present of fundirse: todo se funde = everything melts together.
Same form for masculine and feminine: un pimiento picante = a hot pepper.
Present of picar, ellos form; for peppers it means to be hot: de los que pican = the hot kind.
Imperative of pelar (to peel): pela dos dientes de ajo.
Imperative corta + los (them); córtalos en láminas = slice them.
Present of amargar: el ajo que se tuesta amarga = garlic that browns turns bitter.
Present of planear: nadie la planea = nobody plans it.
